title: GM bus: High-Speed GMLAN
text: General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): High-Speed GMLAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2004+ (full by 2008). Powertrain/chassis bus. 120-ohm terminators at each end; ~60 ohms across DLC 6/14 (key off) is the standard health check.

title: GM bus: Mid-Speed GMLAN
text: General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): Mid-Speed GMLAN — 95.2 kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 2-wire, years 2004+. Infotainment (display, navigation). BITRATE CONFLICT: ACDelco says 95.2 kbps [A]; GM Enhanced Diag spec excerpt says 'approximately 95.2 or 125 kbps' [B] — treat as model-dependent.

title: GM bus: Single-Wire (Low-Speed) GMLAN
text: General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): Single-Wire (Low-Speed) GMLAN — 33.33 kbps, DLC pins 1, 1-wire, years 2004+. Per GMW3089. 83.33 kbps high-speed mode used for flashing (transceiver must switch, not just the CAN bitrate). Sleeping nodes REQUIRE high-voltage wake-up before they answer normal traffic.

title: GM bus: Second High-Speed GMLAN (select models)
text: General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): Second High-Speed GMLAN (select models) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 12, 13, 2-wire, years model-dependent. CONFLICT: a 2010 Camaro reportedly has a second HS bus on DLC 12/13 [C], but the 2002 Intrepid pinout labels 12/13 'LSFT H/L' (discretionary) [B]. Pin 12/13 usage varies by model/year — verify per vehicle.

title: GM legacy: Class 2 / SAE J1850 VPW
text: General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac) legacy: Class 2 / SAE J1850 VPW — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 2, years 1996–~2007 (gradual, model-dependent). VPW uses pin 2 ONLY (pin 10 is the J1850 PWM negative leg — Ford, not GM). Phase-in of GMLAN began 2004; 2005 Colorado/Yukon still VPW per owner reports; complete by the 2008 federal CAN mandate.

title: M2 mapping: High-Speed GMLAN (6/14)
text: M2 hardware mapping for General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): CAN0 (TJA1051, HSC_BUS) -> High-Speed GMLAN (6/14). 500 kbps via due_can. Standard M2RET/ELM path.

title: M2 mapping: Mid-Speed GMLAN (3/11)
text: M2 hardware mapping for General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): CAN1 (TJA1051, MSC_BUS) -> Mid-Speed GMLAN (3/11). The M2's CAN1 transceiver is wired to DLC 3/11 — exactly the GMLAN mid-speed pins. No extra hardware needed; set due_can to 95.2 or 125 kbps per model.

title: M2 mapping: Single-Wire GMLAN (pin 1)
text: M2 hardware mapping for General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): SWCAN (MCP2515 + TH8056, SWC_BUS) -> Single-Wire GMLAN (pin 1). setupSW(33) normal / setupSW(83) flashing; mode(2) HV-wake BEFORE expecting replies from sleeping modules, then mode(3).

title: M2 mapping: Class 2 (pin 2)
text: M2 hardware mapping for General Motors (Chevrolet / Buick / GMC / Cadillac): J1850 discrete circuit, VPW mode (pin 50 LOW) -> Class 2 (pin 2). VPW-only on GM: use pin 52 (VPW RX) / pin 53 (J1850+ TX). M2 J1850- (DLC pin 10) has no GM use.

title: FORD bus: HS-CAN
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: HS-CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2004+ (full by 2008). Powertrain bus; also the legislated emissions bus (ISO 15765-4) — any generic OBD-II tool sees it. Modules: PCM, TCM, ABS, EPAS.

title: FORD bus: MS-CAN
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: MS-CAN — 125 kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 2-wire, years ~2003+ (not all models). Ford-PROPRIETARY pins — dead on non-Ford vehicles. Body/comfort: GEM, doors, cluster, RCM, EATC. This pin split is why FORScan needs the HS/MS toggle on ELM327 adapters. BITRATE CONFLICT: one community glossary claims '125-500 kbps depending on chassis' [C] vs unanimous 125 kbps — treat 125 as standard. MS-CAN is NOT on all Fords: probe, don't assume.

title: FORD bus: HS-CAN2
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: HS-CAN2 — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years newer platforms. Second high-speed bus on newer platforms (FDSM, ABS, RCM, PSCM, SCCM, GWM, IPMA per one vendor source). DLC availability varies; often gateway-internal only.

title: FORD bus: CAN FD
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: CAN FD — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2021+ select models (F-150, Lightning, Mach-E, Escape 2023+, Expedition/Navigator 2022+, Nautilus 2024). M2 CANNOT PARTICIPATE: TJA1051 transceivers are CAN 2.0 only. 2021+ CAN-FD Fords are out of scope for M2 CAN work (hardware fact from the knowledge pack; vehicle consequence inferred but solid).

title: FORD legacy: SCP / SAE J1850 PWM
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury legacy: SCP / SAE J1850 PWM — 41.6 kbps, DLC pins 2, 10, years 1996–~2006 (model-dependent); all-CAN by 2008 mandate. Ford's SCP variant REQUIRES In-Frame Response (IFR) bytes — unlike GM's VPW. Timeline approx: 1996-2001 PWM-only, 2002-2006 mixed by model, post-2006 CAN.

title: M2 mapping: HS-CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> HS-CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps. Standard path.

title: M2 mapping: MS-CAN (3/11) @ 125 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> MS-CAN (3/11) @ 125 kbps. KEY M2 ADVANTAGE: a switched ELM327 sees one bus at a time, but the M2's two independent CAN controllers can watch HS-CAN and MS-CAN SIMULTANEOUSLY — FORScan+ELM327 cannot do this.

title: M2 mapping: SCP (pins 2/10)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: J1850 discrete circuit, PWM mode (pin 50 HIGH) -> SCP (pins 2/10). Pre-2004 Fords. IFR bytes REQUIRED by Ford's SCP variant.

title: M2 mapping: Body LIN sub-buses
text: M2 hardware mapping for Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: LIN1/LIN2 (TJA1027) -> Body LIN sub-buses. Door/climate sub-buses on some models, if tapped at the module.

title: M2 mapping: CAN FD (2021+)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Ford / Lincoln / Mercury: NONE -> CAN FD (2021+). Out of scope — TJA1051 is CAN 2.0 only.

title: STELLANTIS bus: CAN-C1
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): CAN-C1 — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years ~2004/05+. Powertrain/chassis high-speed CAN (SAE J2284). 11-bit identifiers the norm. 120-ohm terminators; ~60 ohms per pair (key off) = continuity check.

title: STELLANTIS bus: CAN-C2
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): CAN-C2 — 500 kbps, DLC pins 12, 13, 2-wire, years some platforms. Second high-speed CAN on some platforms (e.g. Alfa/Fiat 'second high-speed CANBUS' per aftermarket vendors). Pins confirmed [A]; BITRATE UNCONFIRMED — treat 500 kbps as provisional.

title: STELLANTIS bus: CAN-BH
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): CAN-BH — ? kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 2-wire, years ~2004/05+. Body/harness CAN. Pins confirmed [A]; BITRATE UNCONFIRMED. NOT reachable with stock M2 hardware (both native CAN controllers spoken for by C1/C2; MCP2515 is tied to the SWCAN transceiver).

title: STELLANTIS bus: CAN-IHS
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): CAN-IHS — 125 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years ~2004/05+. 'Interior High Speed' is the SLOW bus (125 kbps) — the name misleads. Interior/comfort modules. Not on the DLC; reachable only via gateway or direct tap.

title: STELLANTIS legacy: PCI / SAE J1850 VPW
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) legacy: PCI / SAE J1850 VPW — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 2, years ~1999–~2005 (model-dependent). Single wire, idle low, active high ~7-7.5V. Used for inter-module comms and scan-tool/flash until CAN replaced it.

title: STELLANTIS legacy: CCD (Chrysler Collision Detection)
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) legacy: CCD (Chrysler Collision Detection) — 7.8125 kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, years 1988–~1998. Proprietary 2-wire bus. TRAP: pins 3/11 were later recycled for CAN-BH — year/model determines which protocol is on those pins.

title: STELLANTIS legacy: SCI (SAE J2610, Chrysler-proprietary serial)
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) legacy: SCI (SAE J2610, Chrysler-proprietary serial) — ? kbps, DLC pins 6, 7, 9, 12, 14, 15, years 1990s–early 2000s (PCM/TCM flashing). UART-based proprietary serial for PCM/TCM diagnostics and flash reprogramming. Multiple channels (SCI A Engine/Trans, SCI B); pin assignments vary by model/year. M2 HAS NO SCI HARDWARE — pre-CAN Chrysler powertrain flashing via SCI is out of reach for stock M2 firmware.

title: STELLANTIS legacy: K-line (ISO 9141-2 / ISO 14230)
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) legacy: K-line (ISO 9141-2 / ISO 14230) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1996–~2004. On many 1996-~2004 models alongside PCI/SCI. M2 K-line transceiver (TJA1027) covers this.

title: M2 mapping: CAN-C1 (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> CAN-C1 (6/14) @ 500 kbps. Primary diagnostic bus. On 2018+ SGW vehicles, reads work through the gateway; writes are blocked.

title: M2 mapping: CAN-C2 (12/13)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> CAN-C2 (12/13). Second native controller covers this where present.

title: M2 mapping: CAN-BH (3/11)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): NONE (stock) -> CAN-BH (3/11). Not reachable with stock M2 hardware — would need an external CAN transceiver on SPI.

title: M2 mapping: PCI (pin 2)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): J1850 discrete circuit, VPW mode (pin 50 LOW) -> PCI (pin 2). Pre-CAN Chrysler.

title: M2 mapping: ISO 9141 K-line (pin 7)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): K-line (TJA1027) -> ISO 9141 K-line (pin 7). 1996-~2004 models.

title: M2 mapping: LIN sub-buses (e.g. CCN -> multifunction switch)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): LIN1/LIN2 (TJA1027) -> LIN sub-buses (e.g. CCN -> multifunction switch). If tapped at the module; plain 19.2k-class LIN.

title: M2 mapping: SCI (J2610)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo): NONE -> SCI (J2610). No M2 hardware support — proprietary serial, not J1850/K-line/LIN.

title: TOYOTA bus: CAN V Bus (HS)
text: Toyota / Lexus: CAN V Bus (HS) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2004+. Powertrain/chassis: ECM, HV ECU, battery ECU, skid control, EPS, airbag, gateway ECU. Termination spec 54-69 ohms across 6/14 (ignition off) [A].

title: TOYOTA bus: MS-CAN
text: Toyota / Lexus: MS-CAN — 250 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2004+. Body/comfort traffic BEHIND the gateway ECU — not on the DLC in any source found. A scan tool reaches it only through gateway routing.

title: TOYOTA legacy: K-line / SIL (ISO 9141-2)
text: Toyota / Lexus legacy: K-line / SIL (ISO 9141-2) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years pre-2008+ (survived into CAN era). DLC3 pin 7 (SIL), optional L-line pin 15. Non-CAN modules (TPMS, air suspension) used K-line deep into the CAN era.

title: TOYOTA legacy: BEAN (Body Electronics Area Network)
text: Toyota / Lexus legacy: BEAN (Body Electronics Area Network) — 10 kbps, DLC pins —, years early 2000s+. Toyota-PROPRIETARY single-wire body bus, 0-10V. NO M2 HARDWARE SUPPORT — not J1850, not K-line, not LIN.

title: TOYOTA legacy: AVC-LAN
text: Toyota / Lexus legacy: AVC-LAN — 17.8 kbps, DLC pins —, years early 2000s+. Toyota-proprietary audio/visual bus; star topology. Not a diagnostic target.

title: M2 mapping: HS CAN V Bus (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Toyota / Lexus: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> HS CAN V Bus (6/14) @ 500 kbps. Primary diagnostic + logging bus. One controller normally suffices at the DLC (no HS/MS pin split like Ford).

title: M2 mapping: MS-CAN @ 250 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Toyota / Lexus: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> MS-CAN @ 250 kbps. Only if tapped behind the gateway (interior harness) — not on the DLC.

title: M2 mapping: SIL K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Toyota / Lexus: K-line (TJA1027) -> SIL K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps. Non-CAN modules on CAN-era vehicles; pre-CAN diagnostics.

title: M2 mapping: LIN sub-buses @ 9.6 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Toyota / Lexus: LIN1/LIN2 (TJA1027) -> LIN sub-buses @ 9.6 kbps. If tapped at the module.

title: M2 mapping: BEAN
text: M2 hardware mapping for Toyota / Lexus: NONE -> BEAN. Out of reach — proprietary 0-10V single-wire protocol, no M2 hardware speaks it.

title: HONDA bus: F-CAN
text: Honda / Acura: F-CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2003+. Powertrain bus: ECM/PCM, TCM, ABS/VSA, EPS, SRS. TWO SEGMENTS: F-CAN A (OBD-II/diagnostic side) and F-CAN B (internal powertrain) — openpilot relays between them.

title: HONDA bus: B-CAN
text: Honda / Acura: B-CAN — 33.33 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 1-wire, years 2006+. Body CAN: gauge module, MICU, climate, immobilizer-keyless. SINGLE-WIRE 33.33 kbps per service manual. NEVER at the DLC — requires a behind-dash tap (BCM 36-pin connector on 2016 Civic/2017 CR-V). SPEED CONFLICT: one community project claims 150 kbps on 2016+ [C] — unverified, contradicts the manual.

title: HONDA bus: IMA CAN (hybrids)
text: Honda / Acura: IMA CAN (hybrids) — ? kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years hybrids. Separate CAN bus for the Integrated Motor Assist hybrid system; own malfunction DTCs.

title: HONDA legacy: K-line (ISO 9141-2)
text: Honda / Acura legacy: K-line (ISO 9141-2) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1990s-2010s. Honda was a heavy K-line user and NEVER used J1850. Pin 7 kept populated alongside CAN into the 2010s (SRS/ABS/VSA/EPS/immobilizer K-line troubleshooting in service manual).

title: HONDA legacy: SCS (Service Check Signal)
text: Honda / Acura legacy: SCS (Service Check Signal) — ? kbps, DLC pins 9, years 1990s+. Honda-SPECIFIC pin 9: grounding it puts modules into service-check / blink-code mode. Readable as a digital input; a diagnostic aid, not a bus.

title: M2 mapping: F-CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Honda / Acura: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> F-CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps. This is F-CAN A (diagnostic side) at the DLC; F-CAN B (powertrain) sits behind the gateway.

title: M2 mapping: B-CAN 33.33k single-wire
text: M2 hardware mapping for Honda / Acura: SWCAN (MCP2515 + TH8056) -> B-CAN 33.33k single-wire. NATURAL FIT (inferred): single-wire 33.33 kbps CAN matches the TH8056. setupSW(33). ONLY via BCM-harness tap — never the DLC. Caveat: if the 150 kbps B-CAN claim proves true for 2016+, the TH8056 cannot do that rate.

title: M2 mapping: K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Honda / Acura: K-line (TJA1027) -> K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps. Pre-CAN diagnostics and still-populated K-line on CAN-era Hondas.

title: M2 mapping: SCS (pin 9)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Honda / Acura: 12VIO digital input -> SCS (pin 9). Readable as a digital input; grounding enters service-check mode.

title: M2 mapping: J1850
text: M2 hardware mapping for Honda / Acura: NONE -> J1850. Honda never used J1850 — the M2 J1850 hardware has no Honda application.

title: VW bus: Diagnosis CAN
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): Diagnosis CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2004+. THE single CAN pair on the DLC — it is the diagnosis CAN to the J533 gateway. VW does NOT put comfort/infotainment CAN pairs on the DLC; those are gateway-internal.

title: VW bus: Powertrain CAN
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): Powertrain CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2004+. Engine, transmission, ABS. Gateway-internal; reached through J533 routing from the DLC pair.

title: VW bus: Convenience CAN
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): Convenience CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2004+. Windows, locks, doors. 100 kbps on PQ-era (A8L SSP287); ALL buses moved to 500 kbps on MQB (Tiguan SSP553). Gateway-internal.

title: VW bus: Infotainment CAN
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): Infotainment CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2004+. Radio, navigation. Gateway-internal. MOST (fibre-optic, 25M PQ / 150M MQB) carries premium audio — electrically invisible to any CAN tool.

title: VW bus: CAN FD (MQB Evo)
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): CAN FD (MQB Evo) — ? kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2020+. UNCONFIRMED in this pass — one forum poster mentions CAN-FD DBCs assumed MQB Evo. If confirmed, those buses are OUT OF M2 SCOPE (TJA1051 = CAN 2.0 only).

title: VW legacy: K-line (ISO 9141-2)
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda) legacy: K-line (ISO 9141-2) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years pre-2004+ (remnants). DLC pin 7 bidirectional, L-line pin 15 optional wake-up. Retained on early CAN-era cars for some modules.

title: VW legacy: KWP-1281 (VAG proprietary)
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda) legacy: KWP-1281 (VAG proprietary) — ? kbps, DLC pins 7, years ~1995-2006. 5-baud init. ECU addresses: 0x01 engine, 0x03 ABS, 0x08 HVAC, 0x17 instruments, 0x19 gateway, 0x46 central convenience.

title: VW legacy: KWP2000 (ISO 14230)
text: Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda) legacy: KWP2000 (ISO 14230) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 2003+ pre-CAN. Fast init (~500ms), up to 255-byte messages. Common on 2003+ pre-CAN VAG vehicles.

title: M2 mapping: Diagnosis CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> Diagnosis CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps. Primary diagnostic path — via the J533 gateway to all buses.

title: M2 mapping: K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): K-line (TJA1027) -> K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps. Covers KWP-1281 / KWP2000 / ISO 9141.

title: M2 mapping: LIN sub-buses @ 19.2 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): LIN1/LIN2 (TJA1027) -> LIN sub-buses @ 19.2 kbps. Doors, sunroof, wipers, steering wheel — if tapped at the module.

title: M2 mapping: MOST (optical)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): NONE -> MOST (optical). Fibre-optic — electrically invisible to any CAN tool.

title: M2 mapping: CAN FD (MQB Evo)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volkswagen Group (VW / Audi / SEAT / Skoda): NONE (if present) -> CAN FD (MQB Evo). Out of scope if present — TJA1051 is CAN 2.0 only.

title: HYUNDAI bus: C-CAN
text: Hyundai / Kia: C-CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2005+. Chassis CAN: EMS/ECM, TCU, ESC/ABS, EPB, SCC, MDPS. Primary diagnostic + powertrain bus. Legislated OBD-II confirmed live (2018 Kia Soul, responders 0x7E8-0x7EF).

title: HYUNDAI bus: M-CAN
text: Hyundai / Kia: M-CAN — ? kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2005+. Multimedia/body CAN (171 messages in opendbc hyundai_2015_mcan.dbc). BITRATE UNCONFIRMED [?]. DLC pin exposure UNCONFIRMED [?] — treat as interior-only unless a per-model wiring diagram says otherwise.

title: HYUNDAI bus: CAN FD (select 2021+)
text: Hyundai / Kia: CAN FD (select 2021+) — ? kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2021+ select. Per community reports, DIAGNOSTICS STAY ON CLASSIC CAN even on CAN-FD vehicles — so M2 CAN 2.0 transceivers can still do OBD-II diagnostics; CAN-FD bus participation is out of scope.

title: HYUNDAI legacy: K-line (ISO 9141 / KWP2000)
text: Hyundai / Kia legacy: K-line (ISO 9141 / KWP2000) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1991-~2010. Hyundai/Kia NEVER used J1850. QUIRK: K-lines appear on MANY DLC pins — 1,2,3,7,8,9,11,12,13 — one per system (engine, ABS, airbag, gearbox), not one shared line. Wire the M2 K-line to the TARGET SYSTEM pin, not just pin 7. KW71 (1991-2001 engine), ISO 9141 (1996-~2005), KWP2000-over-K-line (1996+, all systems).

title: M2 mapping: C-CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Hyundai / Kia: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> C-CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps. Primary diagnostic + powertrain bus. Standard M2RET/ELM path.

title: M2 mapping: M-CAN (if tapped)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Hyundai / Kia: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> M-CAN (if tapped). Interior-only per available sources; tap at the module if needed.

title: M2 mapping: K-line @ 10.4 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Hyundai / Kia: K-line (TJA1027) -> K-line @ 10.4 kbps. Pre-CAN models. Identify the target SYSTEM pin (1,2,3,7,8,9,11,12,13) — not just pin 7.

title: M2 mapping: J1850 VPW/PWM
text: M2 hardware mapping for Hyundai / Kia: NONE -> J1850 VPW/PWM. Not applicable — Hyundai/Kia never used J1850.

title: M2 mapping: CAN FD (2021+ select)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Hyundai / Kia: NONE -> CAN FD (2021+ select). Out of scope for bus participation; diagnostics reportedly remain on classic CAN.

title: NISSAN bus: Main CAN (V-CAN)
text: Nissan / Infiniti: Main CAN (V-CAN) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years ~2003+. Powertrain, chassis, body, diagnostics. Two 120-ohm terminators (ECM + IPDM/TCM/BCM); ~60 ohms across 6/14 = healthy [A]. BITRATE CONFLICT: Nissan Tech News claims 1 Mbit/s [A] vs all community captures at 500 kbps [B] — the 1 Mbit/s figure is likely a trade-article error. Most Nissans have a single major CAN bus (6-12 devices).

title: NISSAN bus: AV-CAN (infotainment)
text: Nissan / Infiniti: AV-CAN (infotainment) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 2-wire, years model-dependent. Infotainment traffic on models that expose it (e.g. Leaf).

title: NISSAN bus: AV COMM (audio-NAVI, isolated)
text: Nissan / Infiniti: AV COMM (audio-NAVI, isolated) — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years model-dependent. Audio unit to NAVI unit (NAVI = bus master). Not on the DLC.

title: NISSAN legacy: DDL / Consult I
text: Nissan / Infiniti legacy: DDL / Consult I — 9.6 kbps, DLC pins —, years 1989-~2004. Nissan-PROPRIETARY 3-wire serial: TX, RX, host-generated 153.6 kHz async clock. Host TX = 12V idle-LOW; ECU = open-collector idle-HIGH (host 5V pull-up). 9600 8N1 LSB-first. Init: FF FF EF -> 0x10 (send twice if needed). Commands: 0xD1 read DTCs, 0xC1 clear, 0x5A stream, 0xC9 read ROM. 14-pin gray connector (~1989-2000); 1996+ 16-pin DLC carries Consult Rx/Tx/Clk lines (exact DLC pin numbers UNCONFIRMED [?]) alongside K-line. ELM327/STN CANNOT speak DDL.

title: NISSAN legacy: K-line (ISO 9141)
text: Nissan / Infiniti legacy: K-line (ISO 9141) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1996-2004. Nissan's OBD2-compliance path during the transition era (DDL is not OBD2-compliant). Factory ECU pinout labels it for GST (generic scan tool) use.

title: M2 mapping: Main CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Nissan / Infiniti: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> Main CAN (6/14) @ 500 kbps. Standard ISO 15765-4. Note: on BCM-gatewayed models (e.g. 2018 Pathfinder) the DLC is QUERY-ONLY — passive sniffing sees zero frames; send an active request first.

title: M2 mapping: AV-CAN (3/11) @ 500 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Nissan / Infiniti: CAN0 / CAN1 (TJA1051) -> AV-CAN (3/11) @ 500 kbps. Second controller covers it where exposed (Leaf-class).

title: M2 mapping: K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps
text: M2 hardware mapping for Nissan / Infiniti: K-line (TJA1027) -> K-line (pin 7) @ 10.4 kbps. 1996-2004 transition era.

title: M2 mapping: DDL / Consult I
text: M2 hardware mapping for Nissan / Infiniti: CUSTOM (12VIO + GPIO + PWM clock) -> DDL / Consult I. Electrically reachable (12VIO drives 12V idle-low TX; GPIO+divider reads 5V ECU output; SAM3X PWM generates the 153.6 kHz clock) but needs a purpose-written DDL driver — NOT stock-firmware capable. Bench-test against a real ECU first. [C - untested inference]

title: M2 mapping: J1850 / SWCAN
text: M2 hardware mapping for Nissan / Infiniti: NONE -> J1850 / SWCAN. No evidence Nissan ever used J1850 or single-wire CAN [?].

title: SUBARU bus: HS CAN
text: Subaru: HS CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2008+. Primary diagnostic bus. 120-ohm end termination (U1201 FSM procedure confirms: fit 120 ohms across CAN-Hi/Lo when ECM or VDC module is disconnected).

title: SUBARU bus: CAN-LS (low-speed CAN)
text: Subaru: CAN-LS (low-speed CAN) — 250 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2008+. Separate body/comfort network; U1321 'CAN-LS METER NO-RECEIVE DATA' confirms it exists. Bitrate and DLC presence NOT documented — interior only unless proven otherwise. BIU gateway function HS<->LS is INFERRED, not verified.

title: SUBARU legacy: SSM2 (Subaru Select Monitor, K-line)
text: Subaru legacy: SSM2 (Subaru Select Monitor, K-line) — 4.8 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1999-~2015. Proprietary memory-address-oriented protocol (not UDS): 4800 bps 8N1, packet 0x80 DEST SRC LEN CMD data CHECKSUM; dest 0x10 = ECM, 0x18 = TCU. Commands 0xA0 block read, 0xA8 address read, 0xBF ECU init. Lives on pin 7 even on CAN-era cars.

title: SUBARU legacy: ISO 9141-2 (generic OBD-II)
text: Subaru legacy: ISO 9141-2 (generic OBD-II) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1999-2007. Emissions OBD-II on the K-line for EJ-era cars; SSM2 shares the same pin with its own protocol.

title: M2 mapping: HS CAN (6/14)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Subaru: CAN0 or CAN1 (TJA1051, due_can) -> HS CAN (6/14). Primary diagnostic + logging bus, all platforms 2008+.

title: M2 mapping: SSM2 on pin 7
text: M2 hardware mapping for Subaru: K-line transceiver (TJA1027) -> SSM2 on pin 7. 4800 bps 8N1 is within the TJA1027's capability; the work is the SSM2 packet layer (init 0xBF, address reads 0xA8, checksum). Covers 1999-~2015 ECM/TCU including CAN-era cars — two independent diagnostic paths from the DLC alone.

title: M2 mapping: CAN-LS (interior tap)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Subaru: Second CAN controller (TJA1051) -> CAN-LS (interior tap). Only if tapped behind the BIU (combination-meter branch); bitrate undocumented, verify per car.

title: MAZDA bus: HS-CAN
text: Mazda: HS-CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2001+ (SkyActiv 2012+). Powertrain/chassis: PCM, TCM, DSC/ABS HU/CM, SAS (airbag), IC.

title: MAZDA bus: MS-CAN
text: Mazda: MS-CAN — 125 kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 2-wire, years 2001+. Body/comfort: FBCM/RBCM, HVAC, audio, TPMS, RKE. EXPOSED AT THE DLC (pins 3/11) — the M2's two CAN controllers can watch HS+MS simultaneously straight from the OBD port, unlike Toyota.

title: MAZDA legacy: SCP (SAE J1850 PWM, Ford era)
text: Mazda legacy: SCP (SAE J1850 PWM, Ford era) — 41.6 kbps, DLC pins 2, 10, years ~2001-2012. Ford-platform-era diagnostics; pin 13 FLASH line signals the PCM to erase EPROM during programming — never drive it from the M2.

title: MAZDA legacy: ISO 9141 K-line
text: Mazda legacy: ISO 9141 K-line — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years Ford era. On some Ford-era models.

title: M2 mapping: HS-CAN (6/14)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mazda: CAN0 or CAN1 (TJA1051, due_can) -> HS-CAN (6/14). Primary diagnostic + logging bus.

title: M2 mapping: MS-CAN (3/11)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mazda: Second CAN controller (TJA1051) -> MS-CAN (3/11). Exposed at the DLC — no gateway traversal needed.

title: M2 mapping: SCP J1850 PWM (2/10)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mazda: M2 J1850 hardware (discrete circuit, pins 49-54) -> SCP J1850 PWM (2/10). Ford-era models only (pre-~2008).

title: M2 mapping: K-line (7)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mazda: K-line transceiver (TJA1027) -> K-line (7). Ford-era non-CAN modules.

title: M2 mapping: 7th-gen BP/CX-30 / 2024+ ND3 buses
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mazda: None -> 7th-gen BP/CX-30 / 2024+ ND3 buses. OUT OF M2 SCOPE IF CAN FD — unverified, treat as unknown [?].

title: BMW bus: D-CAN (diagnostic CAN)
text: BMW: D-CAN (diagnostic CAN) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 03/2007+ E-series; F-series. Diagnostic bus to the DLC (replaced K-line 03/2007). E-series diagnostics are KWP2000-over-CAN on the 0x6F1/0x6XX scheme, not UDS DIDs.

title: BMW bus: PT-CAN (powertrain CAN)
text: BMW: PT-CAN (powertrain CAN) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 3-wire, years E-series. DME/DDE, EGS, DSC, EKPS; JBE as gateway. Three wires: CAN-H/CAN-L twisted pair PLUS a separate wake-up line (not CAN signaling — never connect to a transceiver). 120-ohm terminators. DLC presence is model-dependent (absent pre-03/2007).

title: BMW bus: K-CAN (body CAN)
text: BMW: K-CAN (body CAN) — 100 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years E-series. Body/comfort: CAS, FRM, KOMBI, IHKA, MRS, FZD, CCC, PDC. NOT on the DLC — tap behind the JBE. Reported as fault-tolerant-style; TJA1051 compatibility on a tap is UNVERIFIED.

title: BMW bus: K-CAN2
text: BMW: K-CAN2 — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years F-series. REM, FZD, PMA, FLA, FEM-internal ZGW, HU-H (NBT). Not on DLC.

title: BMW bus: F-CAN (chassis CAN)
text: BMW: F-CAN (chassis CAN) — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years E-series. DSC <-> SZL <-> active steering (AL). Direct tap at DSC/SZL.

title: BMW bus: Ethernet / ENET / DoIP
text: BMW: Ethernet / ENET / DoIP — ? kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 12, 13, 8-wire, years F-series; G-series. 100BASE-TX on OBD 3=TX+, 11=TX-, 12=RX+, 13=RX-. F/G-series coding and diagnostics. OUT OF M2 SCOPE — needs Ethernet MAC + DoIP stack.

title: BMW legacy: K-line
text: BMW legacy: K-line — ? kbps, DLC pins 7, years pre-03/2007 E-series. Pre-D-CAN diagnostics; the K+DCAN cable switch selects between K-line and D-CAN.

title: BMW legacy: MOST (fiber-optic ring)
text: BMW legacy: MOST (fiber-optic ring) — ? kbps, DLC pins —, years E/F-series. Infotainment ring (CCC/CIC, amp, TCU). Fiber — no copper tap. OUT OF M2 SCOPE.

title: BMW legacy: byteflight (fiber star)
text: BMW legacy: byteflight (fiber star) — ? kbps, DLC pins —, years E60/E63/E64/E65. Safety bus, 10 Mbit/s over fiber. OUT OF M2 SCOPE.

title: BMW legacy: FlexRay
text: BMW legacy: FlexRay — ? kbps, DLC pins —, years F-series. Chassis dynamics (DSC, ICM, VDM, EPS). 10 Mbit/s. OUT OF M2 SCOPE — no M2 hardware.

title: M2 mapping: D-CAN (6/14)
text: M2 hardware mapping for BMW: CAN0 or CAN1 (TJA1051, due_can) -> D-CAN (6/14). Primary diagnostic + logging path. E-series 0x6F1 KWP2000-over-CAN is implementable in the M2's UDS/diagnostics mode (11-bit IDs, 8-byte frames, fully CAN 2.0).

title: M2 mapping: PT-CAN / K-CAN2 / F-CAN (direct taps)
text: M2 hardware mapping for BMW: Second CAN controller (TJA1051) -> PT-CAN / K-CAN2 / F-CAN (direct taps). Harness taps only; K-CAN tap needs transceiver-compatibility verification first [C].

title: M2 mapping: MOST / byteflight / FlexRay / Ethernet-DoIP / CAN FD (G-series)
text: M2 hardware mapping for BMW: None -> MOST / byteflight / FlexRay / Ethernet-DoIP / CAN FD (G-series). OUT OF M2 SCOPE — no hardware path.

title: MERCEDES bus: CAN-C (powertrain CAN)
text: Mercedes-Benz: CAN-C (powertrain CAN) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2000+. Engine, transmission, ESP, chassis. The DLC exposes the 500k CAN on standard pins 6/14.

title: MERCEDES bus: CAN-B (interior CAN)
text: Mercedes-Benz: CAN-B (interior CAN) — 83.3 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years 2000+. Body/comfort: SAMs, doors, seats, HVAC. Behind the gateway; tap at X30/4-7 distribution hubs in footwells/rocker panels. Odd 83.3k rate is real — confirmed by open-source W203 CAN project.

title: MERCEDES bus: CAN-D (diagnostic CAN)
text: Mercedes-Benz: CAN-D (diagnostic CAN) — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years W211 era. Dedicated diagnostic databus: CGW <-> tester link. Tester path, not raw bus traffic.

title: MERCEDES bus: CAN-E (cluster/infotainment link)
text: Mercedes-Benz: CAN-E (cluster/infotainment link) — 500 kbps, DLC pins not on DLC, 2-wire, years W204/W212 era. Cluster link behind the cluster (W204 cluster connector pins 12/13). Not on DLC.

title: MERCEDES bus: Ethernet / DoIP
text: Mercedes-Benz: Ethernet / DoIP — ? kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 12, 13, 8-wire, years W222/W205 era+. Diagnostics on newer models; DLC pins 3/11 (Rx), 12/13 (Tx), pin 8 activation (ISO 13400 option 1). OUT OF M2 SCOPE.

title: MERCEDES legacy: KWP2000 over CAN (0x4xx/0x5xx diagnostic IDs)
text: Mercedes-Benz legacy: KWP2000 over CAN (0x4xx/0x5xx diagnostic IDs) — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, years W203/W211 era (~2000-2009). Tester request 0x04E0 -> response 0x05FF observed in an XENTRY-passthru capture (Macchina M2 under-dash). Not the 0x7xx block.

title: MERCEDES legacy: K-line
text: Mercedes-Benz legacy: K-line — ? kbps, DLC pins 7, years pre-W203. Older (ME9.7-era) DLCs carried multiple K-lines on pins 1/7/9/11/12/13/15.

title: MERCEDES legacy: MOST (fiber-optic)
text: Mercedes-Benz legacy: MOST (fiber-optic) — ? kbps, DLC pins —, years 2000+. Audio/infotainment (replaces D2B). Fiber — OUT OF M2 SCOPE.

title: M2 mapping: CAN-C / diagnostic CAN (6/14)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mercedes-Benz: CAN0 or CAN1 (TJA1051, due_can) -> CAN-C / diagnostic CAN (6/14). Legislated OBD-II + gateway-filtered diagnostics. THE DLC IS FILTERED: reads pass, writes are restricted to diagnostic CAN IDs, unknown diagnostic IDs are silently dropped — non-response means 'filtered', not 'module absent'. Wake-up frame required before buses carry traffic.

title: M2 mapping: CAN-B (83.3k, X30 hub tap)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mercedes-Benz: Second CAN controller (TJA1051) -> CAN-B (83.3k, X30 hub tap). TJA1051 handles 83.3k. Interior/body traffic behind the gateway.

title: M2 mapping: K-line (older models)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mercedes-Benz: K-line transceiver (TJA1027) -> K-line (older models). Pre-W203 modules.

title: M2 mapping: MOST / FlexRay / Ethernet-DoIP / 2021+ secure gateway
text: M2 hardware mapping for Mercedes-Benz: None -> MOST / FlexRay / Ethernet-DoIP / 2021+ secure gateway. OUT OF M2 SCOPE. 2021+ (W223/W206) secure gateway authenticates OBD-II access — unauthenticated reads blocked.

title: VOLVO bus: HS-CAN
text: Volvo: HS-CAN — 500 kbps, DLC pins 6, 14, 2-wire, years 2005+ (250k in 2004). Powertrain/chassis: ECM, TCM, BCM/ABS, ETM, SAS. CEM acts as inter-bus gateway. Terminators in ABS/BCM + ETM (Bosch EMS MY02+: BCM + ECM).

title: VOLVO bus: LS/MS-CAN
text: Volvo: LS/MS-CAN — 250 kbps, DLC pins 3, 11, 2-wire, years 2005+ (125k in 2004). Body/comfort: SRS, DDM, PDM, PSM, CCM, DIM, RTI, PHM, AUD, REM, SWM, UEM. AT THE DLC on P1/P2/P3 — MS-CAN-capable adapter is mandatory for full third-party coverage. Terminators in UEM + REM.

title: VOLVO legacy: ISO 9141-2 (K-line)
text: Volvo legacy: ISO 9141-2 (K-line) — 10.4 kbps, DLC pins 7, years 1996-2004. 2005+ = CAN. Pins 2/10 are NOT populated on Volvo — Volvo never shipped J1850 despite generic pinout tables.

title: M2 mapping: HS-CAN (6/14)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volvo: CAN0 or CAN1 (TJA1051, due_can) -> HS-CAN (6/14). Primary powertrain/chassis bus. Community proof: Alfaa123/Volvo-CAN-Gauge ran on a Macchina M2 against a 2011 C30 (P1).

title: M2 mapping: LS/MS-CAN (3/11)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volvo: Second CAN controller (TJA1051) -> LS/MS-CAN (3/11). BOTH DLC CAN pairs are usable simultaneously — the M2's dual CAN controllers map 1:1 onto Volvo's dual-bus DLC. Note the model-year bitrate split ('04: 125k/250k; '05+: 250k/500k).

title: M2 mapping: K-line (7)
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volvo: K-line transceiver (TJA1027) -> K-line (7). 1996-2004 models.

title: M2 mapping: SPA/CMA (2016+) Ethernet-DoIP / CAN FD
text: M2 hardware mapping for Volvo: None -> SPA/CMA (2016+) Ethernet-DoIP / CAN FD. OUT OF M2 SCOPE — no Ethernet/DoIP hardware, TJA1051 is CAN 2.0 only. SPA/CMA need a VOE adapter + VIDA.

title: GM diag: 11-bit USDT physical addressing
text: General Motors diagnostic service: 11-bit USDT physical addressing ($7E0-$7E7 req / $7E8-$7EF resp). ECU #1-#8: tester sends $7E0-$7E7, ECU answers $7E8-$7EF. ECM confirmed as ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8) via documented ELM327 VIN-read capture; TCM commonly ECU #2 (community convention).

title: GM diag: Functional (broadcast) diagnostics
text: General Motors diagnostic service: Functional (broadcast) diagnostics ($7DF). Reaches all emission-related ECUs.

title: GM diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: General Motors diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (Modes $01-$0A). On HS GMLAN (6/14). Always available.

title: GM gateway: BCM (Body Control Module)
text: General Motors gateway: BCM (Body Control Module) (2004+). Bridges HS GMLAN to LS/SWCAN and legacy Class 2. Scan-tool traffic to non-HS modules routes through it; a BCM fault can look like a whole-bus failure. Legitimate access: n/a

title: GM seed/key policy
text: General Motors seed/key policy: No factory-published algorithm. Community RE exists for specific OLDER PCMs (E38/E67 — algorithms NOT reproduced here). Tuner-locked PCMs don't follow the GM formula. Global-B and newer: keys are server-issued, not client-computable. For any modern GM controller: NO PUBLIC ALGORITHM — dealer tool (SPS2/GDS2) required.

title: FORD diag: Physical addressing (+8 response offset)
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury diagnostic service: Physical addressing (+8 response offset) (0x7E0 -> 0x7E8). Ford is in the '+8' family: request 0x7E0, response 0x7E8. Known module IDs (2011-2023 Explorer, community spreadsheet): 0x7E0 PCM, 0x7E4 BECM, 0x7E6 SOBDMC, 0x7D0 APIM, 0x726 GWM.

title: FORD diag: Functional (broadcast) diagnostics
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury diagnostic service: Functional (broadcast) diagnostics (0x7DF). Standard ISO 15765-4 practice; generic OBD-II scan behavior.

title: FORD diag: As-built configuration
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury diagnostic service: As-built configuration (manufacturer-specific). FORScan reads/writes module as-built config (extended license for writes). Can only enable/disable features Ford built into the module firmware.

title: FORD gateway: GWM (Gateway Module)
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury gateway: GWM (Gateway Module) (newer platforms). Forwards messages between CAN buses and provides the OBD-II diagnostic bus. Diagnostic requests via the DLC are routed/filtered by the gateway; raw interior-bus traffic may not be visible at the DLC. Legitimate access: n/a

title: FORD gateway: BdyCM (Body Control Module)
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury gateway: BdyCM (Body Control Module) (CGEA era+). Bridges HS-CAN and MS-CAN. Legitimate access: n/a

title: FORD seed/key policy
text: Ford / Lincoln / Mercury seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC FORD ALGORITHM — none found, none invented. PATS (immobilizer) programming via FORScan uses TIMED access (maintain connection 10-12 min until 'Security Access Granted'; interruptions reset the timer) or CODED access (vehicle shows Outcode, authorized generator returns Incode; internals not public). UDS 0x27 without the key returns NRC 0x35.

title: STELLANTIS diag: Standard emissions OBD-II
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) diagnostic service: Standard emissions OBD-II (Modes 0x01-0x0A). Works through the SGW on 6/14 — READS are not blocked.

title: STELLANTIS diag: UDS reads through SGW
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) diagnostic service: UDS reads through SGW (0x19 (DTC), 0x22 (data)). Reading DTCs, live data, version info works with any tool through the SGW.

title: STELLANTIS diag: UDS writes through SGW
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) diagnostic service: UDS writes through SGW (0x14, 0x2E, 0x2F, 0x31). BLOCKED without authentication: DTC clear (0x14), write-by-identifier (0x2E), IO control (0x2F), routine control (0x31), actuations, relearns, programming.

title: STELLANTIS diag: Community UDS example (JL Wrangler)
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) diagnostic service: Community UDS example (JL Wrangler) (CAN ID 620 + 0x2F). Horn control via UDS InputOutputControlByIdentifier — well-documented community project (pre-SGW or bypassed vehicle).

title: STELLANTIS gateway: SGW (Secure Gateway Module)
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) gateway: SGW (Secure Gateway Module) (2018+ (one vendor doc says 2017 — unresolved conflict; consensus is 2018+)). CAN firewall between the OBD-II port and internal networks. READS (DTCs, live data, version info) still work; WRITES (DTC clear, bi-directional controls, actuations, relearns, programming) are BLOCKED without authentication. Legitimate access: Legitimate paths only: (1) AutoAuth — $50/yr shop account (6 users), technician accounts free, approved tools only (Autel, Bosch ADS 4.0+, Innova, TOPDON, LAUNCH); (2) dealer wiTECH 2.0; (3) physical bypass on the owner's own vehicle (12+8 STAR cable or SGW bypass module; remove before dealer visits). NO DIY AutoAuth path exists for a homebrew tool.

title: STELLANTIS gateway: FCM/CGW (pre-SGW)
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) gateway: FCM/CGW (pre-SGW) (pre-2018). Front Control Module / Central Gateway bridged the scan tool (Diagnostic CAN-C at the DLC) to CAN-B/CAN-C; held the Vehicle Build Configuration. Legitimate access: n/a

title: STELLANTIS seed/key policy
text: Stellantis (Chrysler / Dodge / Jeep / RAM / Fiat / Alfa Romeo) seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC FCA SEED/KEY OR SGW BYPASS — none found in public sources, none invented, none reproduced. UDS 0x27 algorithms for FCA ECUs are not public. M2 Stellantis strategy: read-only logging/diagnostics through the SGW, or physical bypass on the owner's own vehicle.

title: TOYOTA diag: Physical addressing (+8 offset)
text: Toyota / Lexus diagnostic service: Physical addressing (+8 offset) (0x7E0 -> 0x7E8). Like Ford: request 0x7E0, response 0x7E8. Hybrid ECUs have their own IDs on the same HS bus: 0x7E2/0x7EA (HV ECU), 0x7E3/0x7EB (HV battery) — a generic scanner on 0x7E0 never sees hybrid DTCs.

title: TOYOTA diag: Hybrid DTC service
text: Toyota / Lexus diagnostic service: Hybrid DTC service (0x13). Toyota hybrids reportedly use service 0x13 (vs standard UDS 0x19) for DTC reads — treat as model-specific, not a general Toyota rule.

title: TOYOTA diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Toyota / Lexus diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (Modes 0x01-0x0A). On HS CAN 6/14. Always available.

title: TOYOTA gateway: Gateway ECU
text: Toyota / Lexus gateway: Gateway ECU (2004+). Performs protocol conversion between CAN, BEAN, and AVC-LAN. MS-CAN and body buses sit behind it — not on the DLC. No Stellantis-style authentication firewall found (absence of evidence; no source describes a Toyota SGW equivalent). Legitimate access: n/a

title: TOYOTA seed/key policy
text: Toyota / Lexus seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC TOYOTA SEED/KEY ALGORITHM — none found, none invented. TSB T-SB-0043-14 documents the server-side flow: Techstream generates a Seed Number, TIS returns a one-time Pass-Code (management approval required). 2018+ adds NASTF LSID subscription (~$65/2-day, ~$1295/yr) for key programming. Security-gated operations are dealer/TIS territory.

title: HONDA diag: 29-bit diagnostic addressing
text: Honda / Acura diagnostic service: 29-bit diagnostic addressing (0x18DB33F1 -> 0x18DAF110). Tester transmits 0x18DB33F1; ECM responds 0x18DAF110 (2009 Civic). e:HEV ECUs answer at 0x18DAF101/102/106/10E/1EF. TRY 29-BIT FIRST.

title: HONDA diag: 11-bit UDS path
text: Honda / Acura diagnostic service: 11-bit UDS path (0x7E0 / 0x7E8). One hobbyist guide reports 2016-2021 Civic UDS at 0x7E0/0x7E8 requiring extended session (0x10 0x03). Single-source — verify on-vehicle.

title: HONDA diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Honda / Acura diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (Modes 0x01-0x0A). On F-CAN 6/14. Always available.

title: HONDA gateway: Gauge control module (tach)
text: Honda / Acura gateway: Gauge control module (tach) (2006-~2015). IS the F-CAN to B-CAN gateway. Runs network self-diagnostic readable on the odo/trip display (Error 1 = F-CAN, Error 2 = B-CAN, Error 3 = UART). Legitimate access: n/a

title: HONDA gateway: Dedicated gateway control module
text: Honda / Acura gateway: Dedicated gateway control module (2016+). Behind the lower-left dash. A dead gateway = OBD-II link error with a healthy ECU. Legitimate access: n/a

title: HONDA seed/key policy
text: Honda / Acura seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC HONDA UDS 0x27 ALGORITHM — none found, none invented. Immobilizer PCM codes derive from the LAST 5 VIN DIGITS via aftermarket calculators (pre-2020; tool-workflow passwords, NOT the UDS crypto exchange). Immobilizer/key functions are dealer/i-HDS territory.

title: VW diag: VCDS module addressing
text: Volkswagen Group diagnostic service: VCDS module addressing (hex words). 01 Engine, 02 Auto Trans, 03 ABS, 08 HVAC, 09 Cent. Elect., 15 Airbags, 16 Steering wheel, 17 Instruments, 19 CAN Gateway, 42/52/62/72 Doors, 46 Central Conv., 5F Information Electr.

title: VW diag: Gateway Installation List
text: Volkswagen Group diagnostic service: Gateway Installation List (via 0x19). J533 reports installed modules and status in ~3 seconds; the list is edited through Gateway Coding. Physically present but unlisted modules (or vice versa) generate DTCs.

title: VW diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Volkswagen Group diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (Modes 0x01-0x0A). On diagnosis CAN 6/14. Always available.

title: VW gateway: J533 (Data Bus On Board Diagnostic Interface)
text: Volkswagen Group gateway: J533 (Data Bus On Board Diagnostic Interface) (2004+). Central gateway between all buses; diagnostic address 0x19. The DLC exposes ONLY the diagnosis CAN pair (6/14) — comfort/infotainment are gateway-internal. Legitimate access: n/a

title: VW gateway: SFD (Schutz Fahrzeugdiagnose)
text: Volkswagen Group gateway: SFD (Schutz Fahrzeugdiagnose) (2020+ (MQB Evo/MEB); SFD2 on 2024+). Blocks WRITING services (adaptations, coding, parametrizations) on protected ECUs. Per VW own workshop manual: READS and BOOTLOADER-BASED FLASHING are explicitly NOT SFD-protected. Legitimate access: Legitimate paths only: (1) ODIS + GEKO (dealer); (2) Autel in-device tokens (24h/VIN); (3) Topdon/Thinkcar manual SFD; (4) OBDeleven (~90-min window, reported VW-authorized). Confirm SFD2 support per VIN on 2024+.

title: VW seed/key policy
text: Volkswagen Group seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC VW GROUP SEED/KEY ALGORITHM — none found, none invented. Pre-SFD used 5-digit login codes; SFD replaced that mechanism from 2020. Immobilizer/component protection via GEKO-gated ODIS.

title: HYUNDAI diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Hyundai / Kia diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (0x7DF / 0x7E8-0x7EF). Confirmed live on a 2018 Kia Soul with responders at 0x7E8-0x7EF.

title: HYUNDAI diag: ADAS diagnostic addresses
text: Hyundai / Kia diagnostic service: ADAS diagnostic addresses (0x7D0 / 0x730 / 0x7B1). 0x7D0 radar/SCC, 0x730 camera, 0x7B1 additional ECU — community-verified diagnostic addresses from opendbc Hyundai port (ECU disable during openpilot operation).

title: HYUNDAI diag: KWP2000-over-CAN (transition era)
text: Hyundai / Kia diagnostic service: KWP2000-over-CAN (transition era) (KWP2000 on ISO 15765 transport). 2005-~2010 CAN Hyundais likely speak KWP2000 on the CAN transport, NOT UDS. A UDS-only tool will fail against these — send KWP2000 session start or verify first.

title: HYUNDAI gateway: Gateway modules (U0146-U0150)
text: Hyundai / Kia gateway: Gateway modules (U0146-U0150) (varies). DTC documentation references gateway modules A/B/C/D/E. Topology and any diagnostic firewalling on 2021+ platforms UNCONFIRMED [?]. No Stellantis-SGW equivalent found — do not assume one exists. Legitimate access: n/a

title: HYUNDAI seed/key policy
text: Hyundai / Kia seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC HYUNDAI/KIA UDS 0x27 ALGORITHM — none found, none invented. Immobilizer/key programming is PIN-GATED (6-digit newer, 4-digit older), dealer/third-party sourced — not seed/key-computed.

title: NISSAN diag: Physical addressing
text: Nissan / Infiniti diagnostic service: Physical addressing (0x7E0 -> 0x7E8). ECM request 0x7E0, response 0x7E8; TCM/CVT at 0x7E9; functional 0x7DF. Standard ISO 15765-4 layout.

title: NISSAN diag: KWP-style local-ID reads
text: Nissan / Infiniti diagnostic service: KWP-style local-ID reads (0x10 0xC0 then 0x21). Nissan enhanced diagnostics answer DiagnosticSessionControl 0x10 0xC0 + readDataByLocalIdentifier 0x21. A strict UDS scanner sending 0x22 gets NRC 0x12 — Marcus UDS mode should offer a KWP-0x21 fallback for Nissan targets.

title: NISSAN diag: DDL command set (legacy)
text: Nissan / Infiniti diagnostic service: DDL command set (legacy) (DDL bytes). 0xD1 read DTCs, 0xC1 clear DTCs, 0x51 clear transient DTCs, 0xD0 read ECU part number, 0x5A start sensor stream, 0xC9 read ROM/RAM, 0x0A active tests.

title: NISSAN diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Nissan / Infiniti diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (Modes 0x01-0x0A). On main CAN 6/14. Always available on CAN-era vehicles.

title: NISSAN gateway: BCM CAN-gateway
text: Nissan / Infiniti gateway: BCM CAN-gateway (2018+ (Pathfinder confirmed)). On gatewayed models the OBD-II port carries DIAGNOSTIC REQUEST/RESPONSE TRAFFIC ONLY. Passive sniffing sees ZERO frames — that is normal, not a fault. Raw inter-module traffic requires a physical internal-bus tap. Legitimate access: n/a

title: NISSAN seed/key policy
text: Nissan / Infiniti seed/key policy: NO PUBLIC NISSAN SEED/KEY ALGORITHM — none found, none invented. NATS/NVIS uses a PIN-to-password scheme via dealer systems; key registration ERASES ALL existing key IDs first — a half-finished procedure can leave zero working keys.

title: SUBARU diag: SSM2 ECU init / address read / block read
text: Subaru diagnostic service: SSM2 ECU init / address read / block read (SSM commands 0xBF / 0xA8 / 0xA0 (dest 0x10 = ECM, 0x18 = TCU)). Packet: 0x80 DEST SRC LEN CMD data CHECKSUM. 0xBF init returns ECU ID + capability bitmap (bytes 9+ = per-parameter support flags). 0xA8 reads 3-byte RAM addresses (§4 parameter catalog). Memory-address-oriented, not service-oriented — no modes/PIDs.

title: SUBARU diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Subaru diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (0x7DF / 0x7E0-0x7E7 (+8 responses)). Standard emissions OBD-II on HS CAN 6/14, 2008+. No Subaru-specific deviation found.

title: SUBARU diag: FreeSSM / BtSsm (community tools)
text: Subaru diagnostic service: FreeSSM / BtSsm (community tools) (SSM2 over K-line). FreeSSM: read/clear generic + manufacturer DTCs, live measuring blocks, adjustments, actuator tests; no ECU reprogramming, no key programming. BtSsm: Android SSM logging/gauges. ELM327 adapters are INCOMPATIBLE with SSM (protocol limitation).

title: SUBARU gateway: BIU (Body Integrated Unit)
text: Subaru gateway: BIU (Body Integrated Unit) (2005+). Central body-control module on HS-CAN; participates in LAN diagnostics (U1201/U1202, C0046). Whether it protocol-converts between HS-CAN and CAN-LS is INFERRED, not verified. Legitimate access: n/a

title: SUBARU seed/key policy
text: Subaru seed/key policy: No public Subaru UDS 0x27 seed/key algorithm was found. None is invented or reproduced here. Immobilizer DTCs (P1570-P1578) and key registration go through SSM3/SSM4 with dealer-issued codes — not something an M2 implementation should attempt.

title: MAZDA diag: Physical addressing (+8 response offset)
text: Mazda diagnostic service: Physical addressing (+8 response offset) (0x7E0 -> 0x7E8). Ford-family convention carried to Mazda: PCM request 0x7E0, response 0x7E8. Standard emissions OBD-II (SAE J1979) on 6/14 works with any generic tool.

title: MAZDA diag: Functional (broadcast) diagnostics
text: Mazda diagnostic service: Functional (broadcast) diagnostics (0x7DF). Follows the Ford/ISO-15765 convention.

title: MAZDA diag: As-built-style configuration
text: Mazda diagnostic service: As-built-style configuration (manufacturer-specific). Ford-format as-built records (7E0-01-01 lines) appear in FORScan Mazda workflows on Ford-era models. Whether SkyActiv models retain Ford-style as-built block addressing is UNVERIFIED.

title: MAZDA seed/key policy
text: Mazda seed/key policy: No public Mazda seed/key (UDS 0x27) algorithm was found. None is invented or reproduced here. Immobilizer work (P1260-class, key programming after PCM replacement) is documented as requiring M-MDS/IDS at the dealer. Read-only diagnostics and standard UDS services are the in-scope surface.

title: BMW diag: E-series D-CAN diagnostics (0x6F1 scheme)
text: BMW diagnostic service: E-series D-CAN diagnostics (0x6F1 scheme) (0x6F1 tester->ECU / 0x600+moduleID ECU->tester). Request: 0x6F1: [moduleID] [len] [cmd0..cmd5]. Response: 0x6XX: [0xF1] [0x10] [len] [data...]. Command bytes = KWP2000 service/subfunction numbers (EDIABAS Tool32 jobs). 0xEF = broadcast, 0xF1 = tester address. Partial module IDs: 0x00 JBBF, 0x01 MRS, 0x40 CAS, 0x60 KOMBI, 0x72 FRM, 0x78 IHKA.

title: BMW diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: BMW diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (SAE J1979 modes). On 6/14, 2008+ (US) / 2001+ petrol, 2004+ diesel (EU).

title: BMW diag: F/G-series UDS over DoIP
text: BMW diagnostic service: F/G-series UDS over DoIP (DoIP (ISO 13400)). Primary diagnostic protocol on F/G-series; CAN-side diagnostics go through the ZGW/BDC gateway. ENET cable on OBD 3/11/12/13.

title: BMW gateway: JBE/JBBF (E90)
text: BMW gateway: JBE/JBBF (E90) (E-series). Gateway between PT-CAN and K-CAN (F-CAN pass-through). Diagnostics for K-CAN modules are routed, not direct; K-CAN is not on the DLC. Legitimate access: n/a

title: BMW gateway: ZGM in FEM (F30)
text: BMW gateway: ZGM in FEM (F30) (F-series). Central gateway routing all buses; contains FlexRay star coupler. CAN-side diagnostic frames are encapsulated (e.g. CAN->FlexRay); raw PT-CAN/K-CAN2/FlexRay traffic is NOT on the DLC. Legitimate access: n/a

title: BMW gateway: BDC / BDC3 (G-series)
text: BMW gateway: BDC / BDC3 (G-series) (2015+). Body Domain Controller replaces FEM as central gateway and core immobilizer/security module. CAN FD + DoIP world. Legitimate access: n/a

title: BMW seed/key policy
text: BMW seed/key policy: BMW UDS 0x27 security access for flashing/programming exists but no public algorithm is documented; none is invented or reproduced here. Immobilizer (EWS/CAS/FEM/BDC + DME ISN alignment) is dealer or licensed-specialist territory. Read-side operations (passive logging, OBD-II, E-series 0x6F1 reads, fault-memory reads) need none of that.

title: MERCEDES diag: KWP2000-era diagnostics
text: Mercedes-Benz diagnostic service: KWP2000-era diagnostics (0x04E0 tester->ECU / 0x05FF ECU->tester (observed)). W203/W211 era: diagnostic addressing in the 0x4xx/0x5xx CAN-ID range, not 0x7xx (single community XENTRY-passthru capture).

title: MERCEDES diag: UDS (non-standard arbitration IDs)
text: Mercedes-Benz diagnostic service: UDS (non-standard arbitration IDs) (e.g. 0x300 (model-specific)). Mercedes does NOT use 0x7DF-0x7E7. UDS probing must use lower IDs (0x300 suggested by community), but the real per-module table is undocumented (XENTRY CBF files; community parser DMCA'd). The gateway silently drops unrecognized diagnostic IDs — non-response means 'filtered', not 'module absent'.

title: MERCEDES diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Mercedes-Benz diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (SAE J1979 modes). On 6/14 for CAN-2.0 models. 2021+ secure gateway may gate even reads.

title: MERCEDES diag: Wake-up frames
text: Mercedes-Benz diagnostic service: Wake-up frames (model-specific CAN IDs). Modules sleep with the car off; a per-model wake-up frame is required before the bus carries traffic (e.g. W203: ID 001C, DLC 8, payload 02 10 92 00 00 00 00 00). W204/W205/W212/W213 frames not in the crowd-sourced table.

title: MERCEDES gateway: CGW / N93 (central gateway)
text: Mercedes-Benz gateway: CGW / N93 (central gateway) (W203/W209/W211/W219 era (~2000-2009)). Gateway between CAN-C and CAN-B (and CAN-D); monitors CAN-B modules, produces DTCs for CAN-B communication problems. The OBD-II port is FILTERED: reads pass, only diagnostic CAN IDs may be written; arbitrary frame injection from the DLC is rejected. Legitimate access: n/a

title: MERCEDES gateway: ZGW (W204 era)
text: Mercedes-Benz gateway: ZGW (W204 era) (~2007-2016). Gateway function continues; naming mixed with CGW in community sources. Legitimate access: n/a

title: MERCEDES gateway: Secure Gateway (2021+)
text: Mercedes-Benz gateway: Secure Gateway (2021+) (W223/W206+). Firewall preventing any OBD-II communication without authentication — blocks reads, live data, DTC reads and bidirectional functions until authenticated. Legitimate path: dealer/XENTRY online. Legitimate access: n/a

title: MERCEDES seed/key policy
text: Mercedes-Benz seed/key policy: No public Mercedes UDS 0x27 algorithm was found. None is invented or reproduced here. Security-gated operations (immobilizer/key learning on DAS-3, component protection, SCN coding) are dealer/XENTRY-online territory. Whether ordinary read DIDs need 0x27 on Mercedes is unknown — treat NRC 0x33 as 'skip this DID'.

title: VOLVO diag: Proprietary diagnostic addressing (P1/P2/P3)
text: Volvo diagnostic service: Proprietary diagnostic addressing (P1/P2/P3) (0x726/0x72E (CEM), 0x730/0x738 (PSCM), 0x764/0x76C (FSM), 0x793/0x79B (CVM); 0x7DF functional). +8 response offset (same convention as Toyota). The 0x72x-0x79x addressing does NOT follow the generic 0x7E0/0x7E8 OBD pattern. Engine-ECM diagnostic addressing not verified. Volvo-specific diagnostics beyond emissions need DiCE + VIDA or a Volvo-aware third-party tool.

title: VOLVO diag: Legislated OBD-II
text: Volvo diagnostic service: Legislated OBD-II (SAE J1979 modes). Standard modes on HS-CAN 6/14, 2005+.

title: VOLVO diag: DoIP diagnostics (SPA/CMA)
text: Volvo diagnostic service: DoIP diagnostics (SPA/CMA) (DoIP (ISO 13400) via VOE adapter). VIDA connects via the OBD connector with an Ethernet cable through a VOE adapter (Volvo p/n 9513108 / 9513062). OUT OF M2 SCOPE.

title: VOLVO gateway: CEM (Central Electronic Module)
text: Volvo gateway: CEM (Central Electronic Module) (P1/P2/P3). Inter-bus gateway between HS-CAN and LS-CAN. Supervises LS-CAN nodes (CEM-1A51-1A64 communication DTCs). CEM<->ECM immobilizer pairing uses SYNC + ABS_ID on CAN 0x7FC-0x7FF. Legitimate access: n/a

title: VOLVO seed/key policy
text: Volvo seed/key policy: No public Volvo UDS 0x27 algorithm exists in the sources consulted, and none is invented or reproduced here. Security-gated work (module software, keys, CEM configuration) is dealer/paid-VIDA territory.

title: DTC P0011 (generic)
text: DTC P0011 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): A Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1). Possible causes: low, dirty, or wrong-viscosity engine oil (leading cause - VVT is hydraulically actuated); stuck oil control valve (OCV)/VVT solenoid; failed camshaft phaser; sludged oil passages; stretched timing chain; faulty camshaft position sensor. Diagnostic notes: Change oil and filter with the exact specified viscosity first - resolves many cases; then remove and test the oil control valve (clean or replace); if symptoms persist, evaluate cam phaser and timing chain

Possible causes: excessive soot accumulation in the diesel particulate filter (DPF); failed or inhibited DPF regeneration; faulty DPF differential pressure sensor. Diagnostic notes: Inspect and clean the DPF; monitor DPF sensor readings with a scan tool; perform/verify regeneration cycles; check engine oil for fuel dilution from repeated regen attempts

title: DTC U0073 (generic)
text: DTC U0073 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Control Module Communication Bus Off. Possible causes: intermittent short on CAN data circuits (GM: circuits 2500/2501); backed-out terminal in transmission harness connections (GM TSB 08-07-30-021). Diagnostic notes: If stored as history only, follow the service manual "Testing for Electrical Intermittents" procedure; the affected BCM may stay offline ~20 minutes until timeout. CONFLICT: scribd "Control Module U Code List" words this as "Control Module Communication Bus A Off" - the two-source wording is used here (see Coverage notes)

title: DTC U0100 (generic)

title: DTC P1101 (gm)
text: DTC P1101 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Intake Air Flow System Performance. Possible causes: Vacuum/air leaks in intake tract; clogged PCV system or valve; dirty or faulty MAF sensor; restricted air filter; faulty/leaking charge-air (intercooler) tubes on turbo engines; faulty boost pressure or MAP sensor. Diagnostic notes: GM SI (Document ID 3355356, 2018 Malibu 2.0L Turbo): "The ECM compares the actual air flow based on throttle position (TP) to a calculated airflow based on MAP sensor and MAF." Sets when actual airflow exceeds calculated. Review PIP5402D / 20-NA-047 for leak checks; verify boost and MAP sensors agree KOEO; MAF should read approx 3 g/s (2000-2500 Hz) at idle. Common on 1.4L LE2 / 1.5L LFV turbo engines.

title: DTC P1174 (gm)
text: DTC P1174 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Fuel Trim Cylinder Balance Bank 1. Possible causes: Clogged fuel injectors (Multec 2 injectors, 2000-2008 models); vacuum leaks; aged O2 sensors; MAF issues. Diagnostic notes: GM TSB 04-06-04-047G (US) / 05-06-04-022D (Canada): "Various Driveability Symptoms Due to Clogged Fuel Injectors" — MIL with P1174/P1175 (+ P0171/P0172/P0174/P0300) on 2000-2008 GM cars/light trucks. GM recommends testing with Active Fuel Injector Tester AFIT CH-47976. CONFLICT: an EOBD overview document lists P1174 as "Injection pump cam ring position sensor" — that reading belongs to the diesel (Duramax/Isuzu) context, not gasoline GM. Report both; use the TSB meaning on gasoline vehicles.

title: DTC P1175 (gm)
text: DTC P1175 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Fuel Trim Cylinder Balance Bank 2. Possible causes: Same as P1174 (clogged injectors, vacuum leaks, O2/MAF issues), bank 2. Diagnostic notes: Covered by the same GM TSB 04-06-04-047G as P1174. Diagnose both banks together; a both-banks fault points to something common (intake leak, MAF, fuel pressure).

title: DTC P1258 (gm)
text: DTC P1258 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Engine Coolant Overtemperature - Protection Mode Active. Possible causes: Cooling system fault (thermostat, water pump, low coolant, cooling fans, restricted radiator); faulty ECT sensor (rule out P0116/P0117/P0118/P0128 first). Diagnostic notes: GM SI: Type A DTC. ECM monitors ECT; sets when coolant exceeds ~131-136 C for several seconds (threshold varies by model/calibration, e.g. 131 C for 7 s on Enclave LZ4/LY7, 136 C for 1 s or 10 s cumulative on CTS). Action: ECM alternately disables groups of cylinders (fuel injectors OFF) to cool the engine — "Overheated Engine Protection Operating Mode"; coolant lamp + DIC message. Diagnose the cooling system, not the code.

title: DTC P1516 (gm)
text: DTC P1516 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Throttle Actuator Control (TAC) Module Throttle Actuator Position Performance. Possible causes: Carbon buildup on throttle plate/bore; faulty TAC module or throttle body; TAC motor wiring open/shorted; poor connector contact; high resistance in TP sensor circuits; ECM fault. Diagnostic notes: GM-ONLY code (same number means different things on other makes). GM SI: sets when actual vs desired throttle position differs by more than 7.5% for 30 s (values vary by model). Type A DTC; ECM commands Reduced Engine Power mode and sets P2106/P2110. Clearing the code restores power only if it is the sole fault. Check throttle body for carbon/ice holding the blade open before replacing parts.

title: DTC P1637 (gm)
text: DTC P1637 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Generator L-Terminal Circuit. Possible causes: Loose or corroded connections at alternator or PCM; faulty voltage regulator; open/grounded L-terminal wire (generator will not operate if L wire is open or grounded); PCM fault. Diagnostic notes: GM SI (1999 Corvette): the L (lamp) terminal enables generator operation after engine start and reports internal faults (regulator grounds L on internal fault). Scan tool: L terminal should read Inactive KOEO and Active with engine running. DTCs P1637 and P1638 may set together; the L-terminal circuit can cause P1638 to set. One diagnostic table covers both.

title: DTC P1638 (gm)
text: DTC P1638 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Generator F-Terminal Circuit. Possible causes: Faulty voltage regulator; open/shorted field winding; wiring fault on F-terminal circuit; wrong/clone alternator (field duty cycle out of range); PCM fault. Diagnostic notes: GM SI: PCM monitors generator field duty cycle (PWM) on the F terminal — expects ~0% KOEO and 5-100% with engine running. Out-of-range PWM sets the code; PCM then sends a Class 2 message to illuminate "Charge System Fault" and may turn the alternator off. Scan tool: F terminal should read 10-40% KOEO, >5% running.

title: DTC P1682 (gm)
text: DTC P1682 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Ignition 1 Switch Circuit 2. Possible causes: Bad relay or blown fuse (ECM/IGN circuits); faulty ignition switch; open/short in ignition-1 wiring; faulty underhood fuse block; ECM fault. Diagnostic notes: GM SI circuit description: two ignition-1 voltage circuits feed the ECM (one via powertrain relay for TAC circuits, one via run/crank relay or ignition switch for remaining circuits). Code sets on a voltage difference between the two circuits (>~3 V reported on some models). Test B+ at both ECM ignition feeds (e.g. C1-19 on some models); swap relays and check fuses before condemning the ECM. Model-year variation exists in which relays feed the two circuits — verify against the model SI.

title: DTC P1811 (gm)
text: DTC P1811 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Maximum Adapt and Long Shift. Possible causes: Pressure control solenoid failure; debris/wear in valve body (torque signal regulator valve or actuator feed limit valve sticking); worn/sticking line boost valve and sleeve; PCM/TCM calibration. Diagnostic notes: Classic 4T65E code. GM SI: shift taking longer than 0.65 s with adapt at its limit increments a counter; counter = 2 in one trip sets the code (Type C — MIL does NOT light; harsh shifts are the symptom). When set, PCM commands maximum line pressure and disables adapts — the bang-shifting is the protection strategy, not the root fault. GM TSB 08-07-30-013 (2007 Terraza/Uplander/Montana SV6/Relay): FALSE P1811 — reprogram TCM with updated calibration (PN 24247599), do NOT replace TCM/valve body/solenoids for that concern. Watch TAP (Transaxle Adaptive Pressure) cells on a scan tool to find the slipping element.

title: DTC P1860 (gm)
text: DTC P1860 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): TCC PWM Solenoid Circuit Electrical. Possible causes: Open or short in TCC PWM solenoid circuit; faulty TCC PWM solenoid valve; wiring harness fault; PCM fault. Diagnostic notes: GM SI: PCM provides a ground path (circuit 418) for the TCC PWM solenoid that smooths TCC apply. Sets on continuous open/short detected via voltage feedback vs commanded duty cycle (command ON/voltage stays B+, or command OFF/voltage stays 0 V). Type varies by model/year (A, B, C, or D). Diagnostic cascade: P1860 can cause P1870 to set — always diagnose the electrical code first.

title: DTC P1870 (gm)
text: DTC P1870 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Transmission Component Slipping. Possible causes: Worn TCC clutch; faulty TCC PWM solenoid (see P1860); sticking shift valves or contamination; TFP manual valve position switch malfunction (P1810); internal transmission failure; low/dirty fluid. Diagnostic notes: GM SI: PCM computes TCC slip from engine speed vs transmission output speed; sets when slip is excessive (e.g. 200-1500 RPM for 8 s, 3 occurrences, on 1997 4T60-E; 90-500 RPM for 10 s on later trucks). Type B (MIL after 2 trips). Actions: inhibits TCC, commands max line pressure, inhibits 4th in hot mode, freezes adapts. Diagnostic aids: a TFP switch fault or shift-solenoid mechanical fault can set P1870; diagnose engine DTCs and electrical trans codes first.

title: DTC P2176 (gm)
text: DTC P2176 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Throttle Actuator Control System - Minimum Throttle Position Not Learned. Possible causes: Faulty TAC module/throttle body; TAC harness open/shorted or poor connection; throttle plate sticking from carbon buildup; ECM fault. Diagnostic notes: GM SI: sets when both TP sensors read above 0.95 V during the minimum-learn procedure (learn runs once per ignition cycle). Type A; commands Reduced Engine Power and sets P2106/P2110. Diagnostic aid: high resistance in TP circuits, or the blade held open (ice in bore). After throttle body service, perform the idle/minimum-position learn procedure.

title: DTC P1E00 (gm)
text: DTC P1E00 (gm manufacturer-specific, category P): Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module Requested MIL Illumination (informational). Possible causes: not documented (code is informational — the root fault is whatever is stored in the hybrid control module). Diagnostic notes: Seen on Chevrolet Volt / Malibu Eco alongside hybrid codes (e.g. P0AFA, P1AF0/P1AF2). Volt community reports these secured high-voltage DTCs cannot be cleared with a generic OBD-II reader; they require a dealer-level tool (GDS2) and in some cases HPCM2 reprogramming (SPS2). Always scan the hybrid/EV powertrain control module for the underlying codes rather than diagnosing P1E00 itself.

title: DTC U0073 (gm)
text: DTC U0073 (gm manufacturer-specific, category U): Control Module Communication Bus A Off. Possible causes: Backed-out terminals in the transmission 16-way electrical connector (GM-documented pattern failure); short between HS GMLAN (+) and (-); any HS GMLAN circuit shorted to ground or voltage; module internal fault shorting the bus; open in HS GMLAN circuits. Diagnostic notes: GM bulletin (Cadillac XLR 2007 / Silverado 2008-2009, doc 2186567): intermittent no-crank, IPC gauge fluctuation, door-lock cycling, transmission no-shift with U0073/U0100/U0101/U0102/U0121/U0140 — cause was a terminal for the High Speed GMLAN serial data bus backed out of the transmission connector. "Do NOT replace BCM, ECM, EBCM, TCM, TCCM or wiring harness before checking terminals in transmission connector." HS GMLAN uses two 120-ohm terminators in parallel (BCM + ECM); 60 ohms across the bus is normal, ~120 ohms indicates an open.

title: DTC U0100 (gm)
text: DTC U0100 (gm manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With ECM/PCM. Possible causes: Same GMLAN bus faults as U0073; blown fuse / dead OBD-II port power; bad ground; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: Appears in the GM TSB set above (transmission-connector terminal pattern failure). Generic scanners often surface U0100 when the real fault is bus-wide — check the full U-code set before condemning the ECM.

title: DTC U0101 (gm)
text: DTC U0101 (gm manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With TCM. Possible causes: TCM not powering up (blown fuse, bad relay, wiring); GMLAN bus fault; faulty TCM. Diagnostic notes: In the GM TSB set above. Diesel/truck community note: U2106-family symptoms (no PRNDL underline, harsh 3rd-gear limp) point to the TCM not powering up rather than a dead TCM.

title: DTC U2100 (gm)
text: DTC U2100 (gm manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN-BUS Communication (bus-off condition). Possible causes: Total or partial loss of high-speed GMLAN serial data (shorts, opens, module internal fault). Diagnostic notes: GM SI: "When a module detects a bus-off condition a DTC U0001 or U2100 will be set. These DTCs can be retrieved as history only." Engine will not start with a total HS GMLAN failure while not running. HS GMLAN modules: BCM, OnStar (communication interface module), EBCM, ESC, ECM, TCM.

title: DTC U2105 (gm)
text: DTC U2105 (gm manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With Transmission Control Module (Silverado 2003 context). Possible causes: TCM wiring/connector damage or corrosion; low system voltage. Diagnostic notes: Single technician source (2003 Silverado 2500HD). Check TCM-PCM harness and battery/charging system; clear and retest.

title: DTC U2106 (gm)
text: DTC U2106 (gm manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With Engine Control Module. Possible causes: ECM connectors/wiring corrosion or damage; blown fuses/relays; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: Diesel-forum and technician reports (2004 6.6L): inspect ECM connectors and fuses; battery-disconnect reset may clear. Often accompanies TCM power issues — verify TCM is powering up (PRNDL display, shift behavior) before condemning the ECM.

title: DTC B1001 (gm)
text: DTC B1001 (gm manufacturer-specific, category B): Option Configuration Error. Possible causes: SDM or BCM replaced without VIN programming; VIN mismatch between SDM (inflatable restraint sensing and diagnostic module) and BCM. Diagnostic notes: The SDM stores the restraint ID from the VIN plus the last 4 digits of the SDM part number; at key-on it compares against the BCM over GMLAN. Mismatch sets B1001 and lights the airbag lamp; the code returns every power cycle until fixed. Fix: with a capable scan tool, run "Setup New BCM" / program the VIN into the SDM so both modules agree. Some vehicles require dealer programming.

title: DTC B1325 (gm)
text: DTC B1325 (gm manufacturer-specific, category B): Device Power / module communication fault (seen as radio-module communication fault on 2015 Silverado/Sierra). Possible causes: Radio module wiring harness damage or loose pins; faulty radio module; BCM communication fault; low system voltage. Diagnostic notes: Technician reports on 2015 Silverado/Sierra pair B1325 with U0164 (lost communication with HVAC/radio network). Inspect radio harness connectors for corrosion; check BCM for related faults; battery-disconnect reset; reprogram or replace the module if wiring is sound. Descriptor varies by module — verify per model SI.

title: DTC C0161 (gm)

title: DTC C0240 (gm)
text: DTC C0240 (gm manufacturer-specific, category C): Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Traction Control Not Allowed. Diagnostic notes: Informational — the PCM is refusing torque reduction; diagnose the PCM-side DTCs first.

title: DTC C0242 (gm)
text: DTC C0242 (gm manufacturer-specific, category C): Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Indicated TCS Malfunction. Possible causes: not documented (fault is in the ECM/PCM, not the EBCM). Diagnostic notes: GM SI circuit description: "When certain PCM DTCs are set, the PCM will not be able to perform the torque reduction for traction control. A serial data message is sent to the EBCM indicating that traction control is not allowed." The EBCM then deactivates traction control. This is an INFORMATION code — the fault is in the ECM; diagnose ECM DTCs, not the EBCM.

title: DTC P1185 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1185 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Fuel Pump Temperature Sensor High / FTS High (Cummins diesel). Diagnostic notes: The diesel-list formatting groups P1184 (engine oil temp) and P1185/P1186 (fuel pump temp sensor high/low). Reported, not resolved: some generic DTC databases map P1185 differently (e.g. to engine oil temp range) — the Cummins context is the verified Stellantis use.

title: DTC P1294 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1294 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Target Idle Not Reached. Possible causes: Engine/brake-booster/vacuum hose leaks; throttle plate/linkage misposition; IAC wiring intermittent or observable defect; throttle body defective; failed PCM; carbon deposits; driver circuit open/shorted. Diagnostic notes: Monitored with engine idling in Drive (auto trans), no MAP/TP sensor codes present. Sets when idle is >200 rpm above or <100 rpm below target for ~14-20 s (two consecutive failures / two bad trips, model-dependent). Scan-tool IAC wiggle test is the standard first check (service manual TC-25A/TC-138B test path).

title: DTC P1390 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1390 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Cam and Crank Signals Don't Match. Possible causes: Timing chain/belt misalignment; CMP/CKP sensor faults; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1391 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1391 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Intermittent Loss of Camshaft Position Sensor or Crankshaft Position Sensor. Possible causes: Failing CMP or CKP sensor; connector/wiring intermittent; tone wheel damage. Diagnostic notes: Classic no-start/stall code on 4.0L/4.7L/5.2L/5.9L era engines; often one of the two sensors fails hot. not documented further in sources checked.

title: DTC P1398 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1398 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Mis-Fire Adapter Numerator at Limit. Possible causes: CKP sensor / tone wheel issues; PCM misfire-adaptive at correction limit. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1491 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1491 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Radiator Fan Control Relay Circuit. Possible causes: Fused B(+) or fused ignition-switch output circuit open; radiator fan relay defective; relay control circuit open or shorted to ground; radiator fan relay ground circuit open; fan motor wiring intermittent/observable defect; PCM defective; (2003+ models: Intelligent Power Module shorted/open). Diagnostic notes: Monitored with ignition on, battery >10-10.4 V, while PCM commands fans on. Sets on open/short detected in the relay control circuit.

title: DTC P1492 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1492 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Battery Temperature Sensor Voltage Too High. Possible causes: Battery temp sensor circuit shorted to voltage; sensor failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1493 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1493 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Battery Temperature Sensor Voltage Too Low. Possible causes: Battery temp sensor circuit shorted to ground or open; sensor failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1494 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1494 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Leak Detection Pump (LDP) Switch or Mechanical Fault — EVAP Leak Detection Pump Pressure Switch Condition. Possible causes: Wiring harness intermittent; LDP switch sense circuit shorted to ground or open; LDP vacuum supply; leak detection pump itself; faulty gas cap or vacuum leak elsewhere in EVAP system; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Monitored immediately after cold start (battery/ambient 40-90 F, coolant within 10 F of ambient). Sets when the pressure-switch state does not change when the solenoid is energized. Inspect LDP hoses/wiring under the vehicle for debris damage before replacing the pump; aftermarket gas caps that bleed down faster than the Mopar cap are a known false trigger. Chrysler's LDP-based EVAP monitor is distinctive to the brand — no other OEM uses this exact pump design.

title: DTC P1495 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1495 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Leak Detection Pump Solenoid Circuit. Possible causes: LDP solenoid electrical failure; solenoid harness open/shorted; poor electrical connection; PCM driver. Diagnostic notes: Electrical-circuit counterpart to P1494's switch/mechanical fault. Check solenoid connector and wiring for damage/corrosion first.

title: DTC P1496 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1496 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): 5 Volt Supply Output Too Low. Possible causes: Shorted 5 V reference circuit (any sensor on the 5 V bus); PCM. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1594 (stellantis)

title: DTC P1595 (stellantis)
