title: DTC P1596 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1596 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Speed Control Switch Always High. Possible causes: Cruise control master switch stuck/faulty; wiring shorted to voltage. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1597 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1597 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Speed Control Switch Always Low. Possible causes: Speed control switch stuck/faulty; wiring shorted to ground. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1598 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1598 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): A/C Pressure Sensor Volts Too High. Possible causes: A/C pressure signal circuit shorted to 5 V supply or battery voltage; A/C pressure sensor internal failure; signal circuit open; sensor ground circuit open; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Factory diagnostic path (NGC-era): verify refrigerant charge first, then read A/C pressure sensor voltage with scan tool — fault threshold is above ~4.6 V; resistance-test the signal circuit against the 5 V supply for a short (<5 ohms = shorted). Note: the same code number means something different on Peugeot and other makes — this entry is the Stellantis definition only.

title: DTC P1599 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1599 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): A/C Pressure Sensor Volts Too Low. Possible causes: A/C pressure sensor circuit shorted to ground or open; low refrigerant charge; sensor failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1602 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1602 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): PCM Not Programmed. Possible causes: New/replacement PCM never flashed; incorrect programming. Diagnostic notes: Set by a fresh or incorrectly programmed PCM; resolve with dealer-level flashing (wiTECH). No sensor diagnosis applies.

title: DTC P1682 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1682 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Charging System Voltage Too Low. Possible causes: Alternator; drive belt; battery; wiring; PCM field control. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1684 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1684 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Battery Disconnected Within Last 50 Starts (informational — not a fault). Possible causes: Battery was disconnected or lost power (intentional service, dead battery, cleared PCM memory); weak battery/connections can also set it. Diagnostic notes: STATUS ONLY — indicates PCM memory was cleared within the last ~50 ignition cycles and does NOT indicate a problem. Self-clears after ~50 starts. On the pre-CAN key-dance readout, "P1684 and done" means only this status is stored. Do not chase it as a drivability fault; if it will not clear alongside real symptoms, check battery cables/voltage.

title: DTC P1685 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1685 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Wrong or Invalid Key Message Received From SKIM (Sentry Key Immobilizer Module). Possible causes: Non-programmed or damaged key; SKIM/ignition antenna ring fault; SKIM module failure; bus communication fault. Diagnostic notes: SKIM says the key presented is not recognized — engine typically cranks then stalls (start-stall) or will not start. Distinct from P1686 (no message at all).

title: DTC P1686 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1686 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): No SKIM Bus Message Received. Possible causes: SKIM not powered (poor connection, broken wire); SKIM module failure; PCI/CCD bus wiring fault; PCM fault. Diagnostic notes: Diagnose with a scan tool that can reach the whole vehicle network — determine which modules answer and which do not to localize the bus break. Cleaning the key/ignition cylinder is the field first step; battery-disconnect capacitor-drain reboot is a documented folk remedy, not factory procedure.

title: DTC P1687 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1687 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): No Cluster Bus Message (no MIC / instrument cluster bus message). Possible causes: Instrument cluster failure or power loss; PCI/CCD bus wiring fault; PCM fault. Diagnostic notes: Often paired with P1686; tach/temp gauges may work intermittently with warning lamps on. Address bus-level faults before condemning modules.

title: DTC P1688 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1688 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Internal Fuel Injection Pump Controller Failure (Cummins diesel). Possible causes: Injection pump controller internal failure; wiring. Diagnostic notes: Cummins-diesel specific. not documented beyond description.

title: DTC P1693 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1693 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): DTC Detected In Companion Module (DTC detected in ECM or PCM). Possible causes: Fault stored in the companion controller (ECM vs PCM split on diesels); companion module fault. Diagnostic notes: Informational pointer — read the companion module for the real fault; most common on Cummins-diesel trucks with separate ECM/PCM.

title: DTC P1694 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1694 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): No CCD Messages Received From ECM. Possible causes: CCD/PCI bus wiring fault; ECM power/ground; ECM failure. Diagnostic notes: Pre-CAN (CCD/PCI bus) era code. Determine which modules the scan tool can reach to localize the fault.

title: DTC P1695 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1695 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): No CCD/J1850 Message From Body Control Module (BCM). Possible causes: BCM power/ground; CCD/PCI bus wiring fault; BCM failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1698 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1698 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): No CCD Messages Received From PCM / No Bus Message From TCM. Possible causes: PCM/TCM power/ground; CCD bus wiring fault; module failure. Diagnostic notes: The reported description varies slightly by source (PCM vs TCM as the silent module) — reported, not resolved; treat as "a powertrain module is silent on the CCD bus" and verify which module the scan tool cannot reach.

title: DTC P1719 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1719 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): Skip Shift Solenoid Circuit. Possible causes: Skip-shift (CAGS) solenoid circuit open/shorted; solenoid failure. Diagnostic notes: Manual-transmission skip-shift (1st-to-4th) solenoid. not documented beyond description.

title: DTC P1740 (stellantis)
text: DTC P1740 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category P): TCC Or OD Solenoid Performance (torque reduction signal rationality). Possible causes: Bad overdrive or torque-converter solenoid; torque converter clutch material unable to hold lockup. Diagnostic notes: Chrysler-only code (not SAE-approved description). On RE transmissions the PCM looks for an RPM drop after OD/TCC apply; lockup occurs in 4th so the PCM cannot distinguish OD shift from TCC lockup by RPM alone.

title: DTC P1756 (stellantis)

Diagnostic notes: RE-series automatic transmission code. not documented beyond description.

Diagnostic notes: Sets when the sensor input is out of range for 3 consecutive park/neutral calibrations.

text: DTC U110A (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With SCM (Steering Control Module). Possible causes: SCM power/ground; CAN bus wiring fault; SCM failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U110C (stellantis)
text: DTC U110C (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Fuel Level Message. Possible causes: CAN bus communication fault; Front Control Module (FCM) failure; wiring/connectors corroded or damaged. Diagnostic notes: Frequently appears with U0141/U1403/U110E as a CAN/FCM cluster of faults — inspect FCM connectors and CAN wiring before replacing modules.

title: DTC U110D (stellantis)
text: DTC U110D (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With Security Siren. Possible causes: Security siren module power/ground; CAN bus wiring fault. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U110E (stellantis)
text: DTC U110E (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Ambient Temperature Message. Possible causes: CAN C bus circuit open or shorted; Body Control Module; PCM; ambient temperature sensor itself. Diagnostic notes: Theory of operation: the ambient temp sensor is a direct BCM input; the BCM transmits it to the PCM over the CAN C bus. A failed ambient temp sensor (located near the radiator/under hood) is a common real fix.

title: DTC U110F (stellantis)
text: DTC U110F (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Fuel Volume Message. Possible causes: CAN bus communication fault; sending module failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1110 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1110 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Vehicle Speed Message. Possible causes: CAN C bus circuit open or shorted; Electronic Pedestrian Protection Module (EPPM); ESP/ABS module; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Often the PRIMARY fault with U1120/U0121 as collateral — fix the vehicle-speed source first. Symptoms: dead speedometer, traction/ABS warnings. EPPM (floor panel under left front seat on some models) is a known failure point; inspect its connector for burned pins.

title: DTC U1113 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1113 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost A/C Pressure Message. Possible causes: CAN bus communication fault; sending module failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1120 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1120 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Wheel Distance Message. Possible causes: Anti-lock Brake Module; CAN C bus circuit open or shorted; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Wheel-distance comes from the ABS module over CAN C. No-speedometer + ABS/traction warnings are typical. Check TCCM/TIPM connectors for corrosion; a tire-size change via tuner has been observed to trigger this family of codes.

title: DTC U113B (stellantis)

title: DTC U1170 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1170 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With Intrusion Sensor 2. Possible causes: Intrusion sensor power/ground; CAN/LIN wiring fault. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1179 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1179 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication With Intrusion Sensor 3. Possible causes: Intrusion sensor power/ground; CAN/LIN wiring fault. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1403 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1403 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Fuel Level Signal Received. Possible causes: CAN B bus open or shorted; CAN B bus hardware DTCs also active; cluster module; Front Control Module; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Monitored with ignition on; continuously monitored; one-trip fault. Diagnostic path: confirm the DTC is active, then check for CAN B hardware DTCs before condemning the cluster/FCM/PCM.

title: DTC U1411 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1411 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Fuel Volume Signal Received. Possible causes: CAN B bus open or shorted; cluster module; Front Control Module; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Same diagnostic family as U1403 (fuel-level/volume messages ride CAN B via cluster/FCM). not documented beyond probable causes.

title: DTC U1412 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1412 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Vehicle Speed Signal Received. Possible causes: Wheel speed sensor / ABS signal fault; CAN C bus fault; ABS module; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Seen together with U1417/U1418 after tire-size changes via aftermarket tuners — the PCM rejects wheel-distance/speed data inconsistent with its configuration. Verify tire size programming matches the fitted tires.

title: DTC U1414 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1414 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible/Missing ECU Network Configuration Data. Possible causes: Module replaced without configuration; network configuration data missing/corrupt. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1415 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1415 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible/Missing Vehicle Configuration Data. Possible causes: Module replaced without PROXI/configuration alignment; corrupt config data. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1416 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1416 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Security Siren Signal Received. Possible causes: Security siren module fault; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U1417 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1417 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Left Wheel Distance Signal Received. Possible causes: Vehicle speed sensor fault active in anti-lock brake module; CAN C bus circuit shorted or open; ABS module; PCM; wheel speed sensor(s). Diagnostic notes: Monitored with ignition on; PCM receives implausible wheel-distance over CAN C from the ABS module; one-trip fault. Diagnostic path: verify the DTC is active, confirm the ABS module is active on CAN C, check for ABS-module DTCs, check FCM for active DTCs. Often appears with U1418 (both sides) — on RAM trucks, front wheel speed sensors were the confirmed fix in owner cases.

title: DTC U1418 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1418 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Right Wheel Distance Signal Received. Possible causes: Same family as U1417 — wheel speed sensor(s); ABS module; CAN C bus open/shorted; PCM. Diagnostic notes: Steering-wheel lock-to-lock rotation x3 is a reported owner workaround for clearing it when the sensor is still good (unverified factory procedure — treat as anecdotal). Triggers CEL and/or ABS/traction warnings.

title: DTC U1419 (stellantis)
text: DTC U1419 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Data Received From OCS Sensor 3 - Left Front. Possible causes: Occupant classification sensor fault; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U141A (stellantis)
text: DTC U141A (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Data Received From OCS Sensor 2 - Right Front. Possible causes: Occupant classification sensor fault; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U141B (stellantis)
text: DTC U141B (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Data Received From OCS Sensor 4 - Left Rear. Possible causes: Occupant classification sensor fault; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC U141C (stellantis)
text: DTC U141C (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category U): Implausible Data Received From OCS Sensor 1 - Right Rear. Possible causes: Occupant classification sensor fault; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC B1B00 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B00 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 1 Circuit Low. Possible causes: Clockspring failure (known issue — FCA TSB 08-119-15 extended clockspring warranty to 10 yr/150,000 mi on 2007 JK Wrangler for this code family); squib wiring shorted low; driver airbag; ORC. Diagnostic notes: Part of the B1B00-B1B07 driver-squib series. Always disconnect the 12 V battery and wait two minutes before working on squib circuits. Use an SRS load tool (not a plain multimeter) on live squib circuits per service procedure.

title: DTC B1B01 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B01 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 1 Circuit High. Possible causes: Clockspring failure; squib wiring shorted high; driver airbag; ORC. Diagnostic notes: See B1B00 notes (same series/procedure).

title: DTC B1B02 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B02 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 1 Circuit Open. Possible causes: Open circuit in the clockspring (most common); improper clockspring neutral position; disengaged/poor-contact squib connector; open in driver airbag squib circuit; ORC malfunction. Diagnostic notes: The classic JK/JK-era code. If the clockspring was already replaced and the code persists, suspect the airbag module itself or the clockspring-to-airbag harness. Factory test: disconnect driver squib connectors, connect SRS load tool, re-read ORC DTCs — if the code clears with the load tool, replace the driver airbag.

title: DTC B1B03 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B03 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 1 Circuit Shorted Together. Possible causes: Squib circuits shorted together; clockspring; wiring; ORC. Diagnostic notes: See B1B00 notes (same series/procedure).

title: DTC B1B04 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B04 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 2 Circuit Low. Possible causes: Clockspring failure; squib wiring shorted low; driver airbag; ORC. Diagnostic notes: See B1B00 notes (same series/procedure).

title: DTC B1B05 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B05 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 2 Circuit High. Possible causes: Clockspring failure; squib wiring shorted high; driver airbag; ORC. Diagnostic notes: See B1B00 notes (same series/procedure).

title: DTC B1B06 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B06 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 2 Circuit Open. Possible causes: Open circuit in the clockspring; improper clockspring neutral position; disengaged/poor-contact squib connector; driver airbag; ORC malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Same family as B1B02 (squib 2 instead of squib 1). See B1B02 notes.

title: DTC B1B07 (stellantis)
text: DTC B1B07 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Airbag Squib 2 Circuit Shorted Together. Possible causes: Squib circuits shorted together; clockspring; wiring; ORC. Diagnostic notes: See B1B00 notes (same series/procedure).

title: DTC C1000 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1000 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Pedal Switch 1 Circuit - Performance. Possible causes: Brake signal 1 circuit shorted to voltage; brake lamp switch operation; ABS module; TIPM/BCM. Diagnostic notes: The ABS module detects an invalid signal between master-cylinder pressure applied and the brake-lamp switch output for ~2 minutes. CONFLICT: a Mitsubishi service source uses C1000 for "stop lamp switch circuit abnormality" — the description above is the FCA (RAM/Journey) use; verify against the vehicle line before applying.

title: DTC C1008 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1008 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Fluid Level Circuit High. Possible causes: Brake fluid level switch circuit shorted high; switch failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C100A (stellantis)
text: DTC C100A (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: Damaged wiring harness/connectors; noise interference; wheel speed sensor malfunction; ABS module malfunction. Diagnostic notes: ABS module monitors voltage fluctuation in each wheel-speed-sensor circuit; sets on detected open/short. After any ABS work, perform a key-off/key-on cycle and re-establish scan-tool communication before rechecking codes — the ABS only re-tests sensors after a key cycle. Wiring should test under 5 ohms with no shorts to power or ground.

title: DTC C1011 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1011 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Signal Erratic Performance. Possible causes: Tone wheel damage/debris; sensor air gap; wiring intermittent; ABS module. Diagnostic notes: Signal-quality (erratic) counterpart to C100A's circuit fault. See C100A notes.

title: DTC C1014 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1014 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Comparative Performance. Possible causes: One wheel-speed reading disagreeing with the other three; tire size mismatch; sensor fault. Diagnostic notes: Comparative/rationality code — the module compares all four wheel speeds. See C100A notes.

title: DTC C1015 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1015 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: Damaged wiring harness/connectors; noise interference; wheel speed sensor malfunction; ABS module malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Right-front counterpart of C100A. See C100A notes.

title: DTC C101C (stellantis)
text: DTC C101C (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Signal Erratic Performance. Possible causes: Tone wheel damage/debris; sensor air gap; wiring intermittent; ABS module. Diagnostic notes: See C1011 notes (left-front counterpart).

title: DTC C101F (stellantis)
text: DTC C101F (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Comparative Performance. Possible causes: Wheel-speed disagreement; tire size mismatch; sensor fault. Diagnostic notes: See C1014 notes (left-front counterpart).

title: DTC C1020 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1020 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: Damaged wiring harness/connectors; noise interference; wheel speed sensor malfunction; ABS module malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Left-rear counterpart of C100A. See C100A notes.

title: DTC C1027 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1027 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Signal Erratic Performance. Possible causes: Tone wheel damage/debris; sensor air gap; wiring intermittent; ABS module. Diagnostic notes: See C1011 notes (front counterpart).

title: DTC C102A (stellantis)

title: DTC C1073 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1073 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): ABS Pump Motor Control Circuit. Possible causes: Pump motor circuit open/shorted; ABS module; TIPM power feed. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C1078 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1078 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Tire Revolutions Range Performance. Possible causes: Tire size does not match programmed revolutions; aftermarket tire-size change without PCM/ABS reconfiguration. Diagnostic notes: Plausibility code on tire revolutions per mile. Documented owner trigger: changing tire size with an aftermarket tuner without updating the vehicle configuration (Power Wagon Registry case also set U1412/U1417/U1418/P1C4E alongside).

title: DTC C107C (stellantis)
text: DTC C107C (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Pedal Switch 1/2 Stuck. Possible causes: Brake pedal switch stuck; switch misadjustment; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C107D (stellantis)
text: DTC C107D (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Pedal Switch 1/2 Correlation. Possible causes: Brake pedal dual-switch disagreement; switch failure; wiring. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C1210 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1210 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): G Sensor Input Circuit Performance. Possible causes: Lateral/longitudinal G-sensor fault; wiring; ABS/ESP module. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C1219 (stellantis)
text: DTC C1219 (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Steering Angle Sensor Erratic Performance. Possible causes: Steering angle sensor fault; clockspring; wiring; sensor not initialized. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C121A (stellantis)
text: DTC C121A (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Steering Angle Sensor Not Initialized. Possible causes: Sensor replaced without calibration; alignment work without SAS reset; module replacement. Diagnostic notes: Requires steering-angle-sensor calibration/initialization procedure after repair (scan tool).

title: DTC C121C (stellantis)
text: DTC C121C (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Torque Request Signal Denied. Possible causes: ESP/PCM torque-request plausibility fault; CAN communication fault. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C121D (stellantis)
text: DTC C121D (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Pressure Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: Brake pressure sensor circuit open/shorted; sensor failure; ABS module. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC C121E (stellantis)
text: DTC C121E (stellantis manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Pressure Sensor Comparative Performance. Possible causes: Brake pressure sensor rationality fault; sensor failure. Diagnostic notes: not documented beyond description

title: DTC P1100 (toyota)
text: DTC P1100 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): BARO Sensor Circuit.

title: DTC P1120 (toyota)
text: DTC P1120 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: open or short in accelerator pedal position sensor circuit; faulty accelerator pedal position sensor; faulty engine ECU. Diagnostic notes: If stored, the ECM shuts down power to the throttle motor and magnetic clutch; the throttle valve closes via return spring (limp-home on the cable). Check VPA/VPA2 voltages (0-5V sweep with pedal).

title: DTC P1121 (toyota)
text: DTC P1121 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor Range/Performance Problem. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — model-dependent meaning. The 2004 Prius repair manual (RM1075U) defines P1121 as "COOLANT FLOW CONTROL VALVE POSITION SENSOR CIRCUIT STUCK" (CHS water valve position sensor / tank outlet temp sensor) [A]. Most other Toyota models use the accelerator-pedal range/performance meaning [B]. Confirm against the model-specific manual.

title: DTC P1125 (toyota)
text: DTC P1125 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Throttle Control Motor Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: open or short in throttle control motor circuit; faulty throttle control motor; faulty ECM.

title: DTC P1126 (toyota)
text: DTC P1126 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Magnetic Clutch Circuit Malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Throttle-body magnetic clutch circuit (ETCS). Check clutch circuit continuity.

title: DTC P1127 (toyota)
text: DTC P1127 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): ETCS Actuator Power Source Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: open in ETCS power source circuit; faulty ECM.

title: DTC P1128 (toyota)
text: DTC P1128 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Throttle Control Motor Lock Malfunction. Possible causes: throttle control motor; throttle body (carbon/deposit lock).

title: DTC P1129 (toyota)
text: DTC P1129 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Electric Throttle Control System Malfunction. Possible causes: electric throttle control system; ECM.

title: DTC P1130 (toyota)
text: DTC P1130 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air/Fuel Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: faulty A/F sensor (Bank 1 Sensor 1); wiring; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Toyota uses wideband A/F sensors (not conventional O2) upstream; test with a scan tool reading A/F sensor current/voltage, not a simple rich/lean toggle.

title: DTC P1133 (toyota)
text: DTC P1133 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air/Fuel Sensor Circuit Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: aging A/F sensor (slow response); exhaust leaks ahead of sensor. Diagnostic notes: Response/slow-response code — the sensor still functions but is lazy; often intermittent before setting permanently.

title: DTC P1135 (toyota)
text: DTC P1135 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air/Fuel Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open/short in heater circuit; failed sensor heater element. Diagnostic notes: Check heater resistance at the sensor connector before replacing the sensor.

title: DTC P1150 (toyota)
text: DTC P1150 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air/Fuel Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: A/F sensor nearing end of life (may test good intermittently); wiring. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — retrolib.info transcribes this as "(Bank 1 Sensor 2)", but Toyota service-manual convention (P1150/P1153/P1155 = Bank 2 Sensor 1) and a Toyota master technician (JustAnswer) confirm Bank 2 Sensor 1. A sensor can read fine at times then fail — the MIL cycling on/off is the classic end-of-life pattern.

title: DTC P1153 (toyota)
text: DTC P1153 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air/Fuel Sensor Circuit Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: aging A/F sensor; exhaust leak ahead of sensor.

title: DTC P1155 (toyota)
text: DTC P1155 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air/Fuel Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open/short in heater circuit; failed sensor heater element. Diagnostic notes: Check heater resistance at the sensor connector first.

title: DTC P1200 (toyota)
text: DTC P1200 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Fuel Pump Relay Circuit Malfunction.

title: DTC P1300 (toyota)
text: DTC P1300 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Igniter Circuit Malfunction (No. 1). Possible causes: open or short in IGF1/IGT1 circuit from No. 1 ignition coil with igniter to ECM; faulty No. 1 ignition coil with igniter; faulty ECM.

title: DTC P1305 (toyota)
text: DTC P1305 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Igniter Circuit Malfunction (No. 2). Possible causes: open or short in IGF2/IGT2 circuit; faulty No. 2 ignition coil with igniter; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: Numbering is model-dependent — on the 2001 Prius the sequence is P1300 (No.1), P1305 (No.2), P1310 (No.3), P1315 (No.4); other models number P1300/P1310 as No.1/No.2.

title: DTC P1310 (toyota)
text: DTC P1310 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Igniter Circuit Malfunction (No. 3). Possible causes: open or short in IGF/IGT circuit; faulty ignition coil with igniter; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: See P1305 numbering note — verify per model.

title: DTC P1315 (toyota)
text: DTC P1315 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Igniter Circuit Malfunction (No. 4). Possible causes: open or short in IGF1/IGT4 circuit; faulty No. 4 ignition coil with igniter; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: See P1305 numbering note — verify per model.

title: DTC P1335 (toyota)
text: DTC P1335 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): No Crankshaft Position Sensor Signal - Engine Running.

title: DTC P1345 (toyota)
text: DTC P1345 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Variable Valve Timing Sensor Circuit (Left Bank). Diagnostic notes: Left/right bank split applies to V-engine models; on inline engines use the Bank 1 codes (P1346/P1349).

title: DTC P1346 (toyota)
text: DTC P1346 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): VVT Sensor / Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Problem (Bank 1). Possible causes: faulty VVT (camshaft position) sensor; VVT sensor harness open/shorted or poor connection; low/dirty engine oil (VVT-i is oil-pressure actuated); stuck/faulty oil control valve (OCV); stretched timing chain/belt or jumped teeth; faulty ECM (rare). Diagnostic notes: The ECM compares crankshaft (NE) and camshaft (VV) signals; check engine oil level/condition FIRST (cheap, common). 2001 Prius manual lists "mechanical system (jumping teeth of timing belt, belt stretched)" as a trouble area.

title: DTC P1349 (toyota)
text: DTC P1349 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): VVT System Malfunction (Bank 1). Possible causes: valve timing off; faulty OCV; faulty VVT controller assembly; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: System-level code (vs P1346 sensor-level): points at the VVT-i actuator/oil-control side rather than the sensor circuit.

title: DTC P1350 (toyota)
text: DTC P1350 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Variable Valve Timing Sensor Circuit Fault (Right Bank). Diagnostic notes: See P1345 bank note.

title: DTC P1351 (toyota)
text: DTC P1351 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Variable Valve Timing Sensor Out of Range (Right Bank). Diagnostic notes: See P1345 bank note.

title: DTC P1354 (toyota)
text: DTC P1354 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Variable Valve Timing Circuit Fault (Right Bank). Diagnostic notes: See P1345 bank note.

title: DTC P1400 (toyota)
text: DTC P1400 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Sub-Throttle Position Sensor Malfunction.

title: DTC P1401 (toyota)
text: DTC P1401 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Sub-Throttle Position Sensor Range/Performance Problem.

title: DTC P1405 (toyota)
text: DTC P1405 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Turbo Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Diesel/turbo models.

title: DTC P1406 (toyota)
text: DTC P1406 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Turbo Pressure Sensor Range/Performance Problem. Diagnostic notes: Diesel/turbo models.

title: DTC P1410 (toyota)
text: DTC P1410 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): EGR Valve Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction.

title: DTC P1411 (toyota)
text: DTC P1411 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): EGR Valve Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance.

title: DTC P1430 (toyota)
text: DTC P1430 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Vacuum Sensor for Adsorber and Catalyst System Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: open or short in vacuum sensor circuit; faulty vacuum sensor for HC adsorber and catalyst system; faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: 2001 Prius HC-adsorber/catalyst system.

title: DTC P1431 (toyota)
text: DTC P1431 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Vacuum Sensor for Adsorber and Catalyst System Circuit Range/Performance Problem. Possible causes: faulty vacuum sensor for HC adsorber and catalyst system; vacuum line fault. Diagnostic notes: 2001 Prius HC-adsorber/catalyst system.

title: DTC P1436 (toyota)
text: DTC P1436 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Variable Valve Malfunction (HC Adsorber and Catalyst System). Possible causes: vacuum line; actuator for HC adsorber and catalyst system; front exhaust pipe. Diagnostic notes: 2001 Prius HC-adsorber/catalyst system.

title: DTC P1437 (toyota)
text: DTC P1437 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Vacuum Line Malfunction (HC Adsorber and Catalyst System). Possible causes: vacuum line; VSV for HC adsorber and catalyst system; check valve. Diagnostic notes: 2001 Prius HC-adsorber/catalyst system.

title: DTC P1455 (toyota)
text: DTC P1455 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Vapor Reducing Fuel Tank System Leak Detected (Small Leak). Possible causes: hose and pipe; heated oxygen sensor; fuel system; VVT system; ignition system; mass air flow meter; ECM. Diagnostic notes: 2001 Prius vapor-reducing fuel tank system (EVAP-adjacent).

title: DTC P1500 (toyota)
text: DTC P1500 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Starter Signal Circuit Malfunction.

title: DTC P1510 (toyota)
text: DTC P1510 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Boost Pressure Control Circuit Malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Turbo models.

title: DTC P1511 (toyota)
text: DTC P1511 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Boost Pressure Low. Diagnostic notes: Turbo models.

title: DTC P1512 (toyota)
text: DTC P1512 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Boost Pressure High. Diagnostic notes: Turbo models.

title: DTC P1520 (toyota)
text: DTC P1520 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Stop Lamp Switch Signal Malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Stop-lamp switch input is used by cruise control and shift interlock; check switch adjustment.

title: DTC P1525 (toyota)
text: DTC P1525 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Resolver Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: HV ECU; engine ECU. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid transaxle resolver (motor position sensor) circuit — hybrid models only.

title: DTC P1565 (toyota)
text: DTC P1565 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Cruise Control Main Switch Circuit Malfunction.

title: DTC P1600 (toyota)
text: DTC P1600 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): ECM BATT Malfunction. Possible causes: open in back-up power source circuit (BATT terminal wiring, EFI fuse); faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: Battery voltage is supplied to the ECM BATT terminal even with ignition OFF (DTC memory, A/F adaptives). HINT from the manual: if P1600 is present, the ECM does not store any other DTC. Check BATT terminal voltage (9-14V) and the EFI fuse first.

title: DTC P1603 (toyota)
text: DTC P1603 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Engine Stall History. Possible causes: ignition system (spark plug, ignition coil); fuel system (injector, fuel pump, fuel quality); intake/exhaust (MAF, air leaks, throttle body, A/F sensor, VVT system); ECM; wiring/connectors; engine coolant temp sensor. Diagnostic notes: Stored when the engine stops without the ignition/engine switch being operated (after P1604 startability monitoring finishes). ALWAYS check whether the vehicle ran out of fuel first — stalling from an empty tank sets this code. MIL does not come on; DTC stored in memory.

title: DTC P1604 (toyota)
text: DTC P1604 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Startability Malfunction. Possible causes: immobiliser system; engine assembly (excess friction, compression loss); starter; crankshaft position sensor; coolant temp sensor; fuel pump/control system; fuel pipes; injector; throttle body; fuel pressure regulator; battery; spark plug; ignition coil circuit; intake system; camshaft timing OCV; MAF meter; A/F sensor; valve timing; purge VSV; EGR; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Stored when the engine does not start despite STA signal input, takes a long time to start, or stalls just after starting (drops to 200 rpm or less within ~2 seconds). Check fuel level FIRST — running out of fuel sets this code. Then review freeze-frame data via Techstream/GTS.

title: DTC P1605 (toyota)
text: DTC P1605 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Rough Idling. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — older Toyota-specific lists (retrolib.info) define P1605 as "Knock Control CPU" [C]. Newer Toyota repair-manual excerpts pair P1605 with P1603 as "Rough Idling" [B]. Meaning is era/model-dependent; confirm against the model-specific manual.

title: DTC P1630 (toyota)
text: DTC P1630 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Traction Control System Malfunction.

title: DTC P1633 (toyota)
text: DTC P1633 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): ECU Malfunction (ETCS Circuit). Possible causes: ECM (internal ETCS circuit fault). Diagnostic notes: 2001 Prius lists this as an ECM-internal fault — the listed remedy is ECM replacement after ruling out external circuits.

title: DTC P1636 (toyota)
text: DTC P1636 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): HV ECU Malfunction. Possible causes: HV ECU; engine ECU. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid models only.

title: DTC P1637 (toyota)
text: DTC P1637 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): EGSTP Signal Malfunction. Possible causes: HV ECU; engine ECU. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid models only (EGSTP = engine-stop signal line between HV ECU and engine ECU).

title: DTC P1656 (toyota)
text: DTC P1656 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): OCV Circuit Malfunction (for VVT-i). Possible causes: open or short in OCV circuit; faulty oil control valve (OCV); faulty ECM. Diagnostic notes: The OCV meters oil pressure to the VVT-i controller — a frequent companion to P1346/P1349.

title: DTC P3190 (toyota)
text: DTC P3190 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Poor Engine Power. Possible causes: air induction system; throttle body; fuel pressure; engine; mass air flow meter. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid models (2001 Prius): engine cannot produce expected power.

title: DTC P3191 (toyota)
text: DTC P3191 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Engine Does Not Start. Possible causes: mass air flow meter; out of fuel; engine coolant temp sensor; crankshaft position sensor; camshaft position sensor; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid models (2001 Prius). Check fuel level first.

title: DTC B1181 (toyota)
text: DTC B1181 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in D Squib (2nd Step) Circuit. Possible causes: open in D+ or D- wire harness of squib; D squib (2nd step) malfunction; spiral cable sub-assembly malfunction; airbag sensor assembly center malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Driver airbag 2nd-stage squib circuit. Disconnect battery, wait 90+ seconds before probing SRS circuits. Check D2+/D2- resistance (below 1 ohm OK). A broken clockspring (spiral cable) is the most common cause on high-mileage vehicles.

title: DTC B1207 (toyota)
text: DTC B1207 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Smart ECU Communication Stop. Possible causes: smart ECU malfunction; wire harness (MPX lines); gateway ECU. Diagnostic notes: Stored when communication between the smart ECU and gateway ECU stops for more than 10 seconds. 2004 Prius multiplex system.

title: DTC B1660 (toyota)
text: DTC B1660 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): P Seat Airbag Active Mode Indicator Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: open/short to ground or short to B+ in passenger airbag ON/OFF indicator circuit; faulty telltale light assembly; faulty airbag ECU assembly; instrument panel wire harness. Diagnostic notes: Passenger airbag ON/OFF indicator circuit fault (not the airbag itself). A common field fix on Highlanders is the indicator LED/board in the overhead console.

title: DTC B1901 (toyota)
text: DTC B1901 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in P/T Squib (RH) Circuit. Possible causes: deployed seatbelt pretensioner (RH); open in pretensioner squib circuit; wiring. Diagnostic notes: "P/T squib" = seatbelt pretensioner squib. If the vehicle was in a crash, check the pretensioner for deployment (orange visible through inspection holes = popped, replace the assembly). 2006-2011 Yaris SRS codes are identical across those years.

title: DTC C0278 (toyota)
text: DTC C0278 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open or Short in ABS Solenoid Relay Circuit. Possible causes: ABS solenoid relay; wiring; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Seen on LX470/land-cruiser-family ABS. Often appears in a cascade with other ABS codes when battery voltage is low — address C1241 first.

title: DTC C1201 (toyota)
text: DTC C1201 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Engine Control System Malfunction. Possible causes: any stored engine (P-code) malfunction — this code is a consequence, not a root cause. Diagnostic notes: INFORMATIONAL. Set by the skid control ECU whenever the engine control system has a malfunction; TRAC/A-TRAC/VSC are disabled as fail-safe. CONFLICT: an AI-generated JustAnswer snippet describes C1201 as a crankshaft-position/MAP-sensor circuit code — that contradicts the Toyota brake-control DTC chart (BC-85), which defines it as Engine Control System Malfunction [A/B]. Diagnose and repair the underlying P-code; C1201 then clears.

title: DTC C1203 (toyota)
text: DTC C1203 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): ECM Communication Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: ECM; CAN communication circuit; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Brake-control-system view of an ECM communication loss.

title: DTC C1210 (toyota)
text: DTC C1210 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Zero Point Calibration of Yaw Rate Sensor Undone. Possible causes: zero point calibration incomplete (e.g. after sensor/ECU replacement or battery disconnect); faulty yaw rate sensor. Diagnostic notes: Perform yaw-rate-sensor zero-point calibration with Techstream (on level ground, steering centered), then clear the code.

title: DTC C1223 (toyota)
text: DTC C1223 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): ABS Control System Malfunction. Possible causes: skid control ECU; ABS actuator circuit faults. Diagnostic notes: General ABS-system fault flag — read the accompanying specific C-codes (wheel speed, solenoid) for the real fault.

title: DTC C1231 (toyota)
text: DTC C1231 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Steering Angle Sensor Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: steering angle sensor; sensor circuit; sensor power supply; CAN communication system.

title: DTC C1232 (toyota)
text: DTC C1232 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Stuck in Deceleration Sensor. Possible causes: yaw rate / deceleration sensor; sensor circuit.

title: DTC C1234 (toyota)
text: DTC C1234 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Yaw Rate Sensor Malfunction. Possible causes: yaw rate sensor; yaw rate sensor circuit.

title: DTC C1241 (toyota)
text: DTC C1241 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Low Battery Positive Voltage or Abnormally High Battery Positive Voltage. Possible causes: low battery charge; faulty battery; faulty charging system (alternator); power source circuit fault to the skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Recorded when voltage at the skid-control-ECU terminal falls outside the detection threshold. A weak battery causes CASCADING false ABS/VSC codes (C0278, C1223, C1231, C1253, C1256, C1340 often appear together) — always load-test the battery and charging system before chasing the other codes. Seen on Prius ABS/VSC/TRAC reports and LX470.

title: DTC C1242 (toyota)
text: DTC C1242 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open Circuit in IG1/IG2 Power Source Circuit. Possible causes: IG1/IG2 power source wiring; fuse; skid control ECU power circuit. Diagnostic notes: Seen on Prius ABS/VSC/TRAC Techstream reports.

title: DTC C1249 (toyota)
text: DTC C1249 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open in Stop Lamp Switch Power Line. Possible causes: break or damage in the power line supplying the stop lamp switch.

title: DTC C1253 (toyota)
text: DTC C1253 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Hydro-Booster Pump Motor Relay Malfunction. Possible causes: pump motor relay; wiring; accumulator pressure. Diagnostic notes: Land Cruiser / LX470 brake hydro-booster system. Often cascades with C1241 (low voltage).

title: DTC C1256 (toyota)
text: DTC C1256 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Accumulator Low Pressure. Possible causes: accumulator; hydro-booster pump; low system voltage. Diagnostic notes: Seen on Prius and LX470 brake reports; check C1241 first.

title: DTC C1271 (toyota)
text: DTC C1271 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Low Output Signal of Front Speed Sensor RH (Test Mode DTC). Possible causes: front speed sensor; sensor circuit; sensor installation; foreign matter on sensor rotor. Diagnostic notes: Test-mode DTC — set during the ABS sensor check function, not during normal driving.

title: DTC C1272 (toyota)
text: DTC C1272 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Low Output Signal of Front Speed Sensor LH (Test Mode DTC). Possible causes: front speed sensor; sensor circuit; sensor installation; foreign matter on sensor rotor. Diagnostic notes: Test-mode DTC — see C1271.

title: DTC C1273 (toyota)
text: DTC C1273 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Low Output Signal of Rear Speed Sensor RH (Test Mode DTC). Possible causes: rear speed sensor; sensor circuit; sensor installation; foreign matter on sensor rotor. Diagnostic notes: Test-mode DTC — see C1271.

title: DTC C1290 (toyota)
text: DTC C1290 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Steering Angle Sensor Zero Point Malfunction. Possible causes: yaw rate/deceleration sensor zero-point calibration incomplete; poor steering-wheel center adjustment; poor front wheel alignment. Diagnostic notes: Perform zero-point calibration (level ground, centered steering, correct alignment) with Techstream.

title: DTC C1300 (toyota)
text: DTC C1300 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Skid Control ECU Malfunction (ABS ECU Malfunction). Possible causes: software malfunction in the skid control ECU; oxidized contacts; damaged power supply wiring to the module. Diagnostic notes: Seen as current on a Prius Techstream ABS report. Check power/ground to the actuator before condemning the ECU.

title: DTC C1331 (toyota)
text: DTC C1331 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): ABS Controller Wiring Fault (Front Left Wheel). Possible causes: damaged wiring to the front-left wheel ABS sensor; insulation damage. Diagnostic notes: Check the sensor harness for chafing along its routing.

title: DTC C1336 (toyota)
text: DTC C1336 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Zero Point Calibration of Acceleration Sensor Undone. Possible causes: zero point calibration incomplete; ABS and traction actuator (skid control ECU). Diagnostic notes: Perform acceleration-sensor zero-point calibration with Techstream.

title: DTC C1340 (toyota)
text: DTC C1340 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open Circuit in Center Differential Lock Signal. Possible causes: center differential lock signal circuit; transfer indicator. Diagnostic notes: 4WD models (LX470/Land Cruiser). Set with the center diff lock ON.

title: DTC C1380 (toyota)
text: DTC C1380 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Stop Light Control Relay Malfunction. Possible causes: stop light assembly; stop light switch circuit; STOP LP CTRL relay; ABS and traction actuator (skid control ECU).

title: DTC C1391 (toyota)
text: DTC C1391 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Abnormal Leak of Accumulator Pressure. Possible causes: accumulator; brake actuator internal leak. Diagnostic notes: Seen on Prius ABS/VSC/TRAC Techstream reports.

title: DTC U1103 (toyota)
text: DTC U1103 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Stop and Start Control Module. Possible causes: ECM; engine stop-and-start ECU; CAN communication system fault. Diagnostic notes: Stored when there is no communication between the ECM and the engine stop-and-start ECU for 1.16+ seconds with the ignition on (1-trip logic). MIL does not come on. (Techstream may display the extended form U110387.)

title: DTC U1104 (toyota)
text: DTC U1104 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Driving Support ECU. Possible causes: driving support ECU; millimeter-wave radar / camera sensors; CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash safety system: set on a communication malfunction between the collision-detection sensors/ECUs or the pre-crash control ECUs.

title: DTC U1110 (toyota)
text: DTC U1110 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Intuitive Parking Assist Module. Possible causes: clearance warning ECU assembly; CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Lexus parking-assist (clearance sonar) module. NOTE: U1110 is make-specific — on Dodge/RAM it has a different definition. Do not cross-apply.

title: DTC U1118 (toyota)
text: DTC U1118 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Rear Radar Sensor. Possible causes: rear radar sensor; CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash safety system family — see U1104.

title: DTC U1121 (toyota)
text: DTC U1121 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Driver Monitor ECU. Possible causes: driver monitor ECU/camera; CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash safety system family — see U1104.

title: DTC P1259 (honda)
text: DTC P1259 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): VTEC System Malfunction (Rear Bank / Bank 1). Possible causes: low engine oil level; dirty/degraded oil; faulty VTEC solenoid (spool valve assembly); faulty VTEC oil pressure switch; wiring fault to solenoid/switch. Diagnostic notes: If the code sets at or below ~4000 RPM it tends to be wiring/switch; above ~4000 RPM it tends to be oil-related (Honda master tech guidance). Check oil level and condition FIRST — VTEC is hydraulically actuated. On 1998-2002 Accord the fix was commonly the VTEC spool valve assembly.

title: DTC P1297 (honda)
text: DTC P1297 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Electrical Load Detector (ELD) Circuit Low Input. Possible causes: faulty ELD unit; ELD harness open/shorted; poor electrical connection in ELD circuit.

title: DTC P1298 (honda)
text: DTC P1298 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Electrical Load Detector (ELD) Circuit High Input. Possible causes: faulty ELD (faulty solder joint per Honda service bulletin — most common); blown fuse; poor connections/loose terminals at ELD or PCM; open in wire between under-dash fuse/relay box and ELD; faulty PCM (rare). Diagnostic notes: Honda service bulletin covers this: replace the ELD (P/N 38255-S5A-003); replacement ELDs are now sold separately so the whole under-hood fuse/relay box no longer needs replacement. ELD 3P connector is behind/beneath the under-hood fuse box. Check fuse No. 4 and battery voltage at ELD terminal 1 (BLK/ORN wire) with ignition on.

title: DTC P1300 (honda)

title: DTC P1361 (honda)
text: DTC P1361 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Intermittent Interruption in Top Dead Center (TDC) 1 Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: TDC sensor inside distributor (1990s models — replace distributor assembly per Honda); TDC sensor sub-harness damage at firewall side of timing cover (2000s models); poor connections/loose terminals between distributor/sensor and ECM/PCM; faulty ECM/PCM (rare). Diagnostic notes: On distributor-era Hondas the TDC sensor is integral to the distributor — Honda recommends the whole distributor. On 2001+ Civic the sensor sits behind the top timing cover (driver side); inspect the 4-pin sub-harness connector and scope the AC sine wave (Green/Red wires for TDC) while wiggling the harness. Can put the engine in limp mode (3500 RPM limit).

title: DTC P1362 (honda)
text: DTC P1362 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): No Signal in Top Dead Center (TDC) 1 Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: failed TDC sensor; CKP/TDC sensor sub-harness open; distributor ignition housing failure; poor connections/loose terminals between distributor and ECM/PCM; faulty ECM/PCM (rare). Diagnostic notes: P1361 = intermittent interruption, P1362 = complete signal loss. Check for metal shavings, oil, or rust inside the distributor (rust indicates worn bearings — replace distributor). Voltage checks: ~12V on BLK/YEL wire, ~5V reference on GRN wire with ignition on.

title: DTC P1456 (honda)
text: DTC P1456 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Evaporative Emission (EVAP) Control System Leak Detected (Fuel Tank System). Possible causes: loose or faulty fuel filler cap (most common — use OEM Honda cap, tighten 3 clicks); leaking EVAP bypass solenoid; leaking two-way valve; leaking ORVR valve on top of fuel tank; leak in fuel tank or tank-side hoses. Diagnostic notes: Honda's EVAP self-test runs the tank-side test (P1456) BEFORE the canister-side test (P1457) — a P1456 must be resolved first. Back-probe the fuel tank pressure sensor (GRN wire): ~2.5V at rest; voltage rises as the tank builds pressure with the engine running and should not fall after shutdown. Clamp the hose between the bypass solenoid/two-way valve assembly and the canister to isolate tank-side vs canister-side leaks.

title: DTC P1457 (honda)
text: DTC P1457 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Evaporative Emission (EVAP) Control System Leak Detected (EVAP Control Canister System). Possible causes: faulty EVAP canister vent shut (CVS) valve stuck open — most common (valve lives under the car near the rear axle, corrodes); cracked/rotted EVAP hoses; saturated charcoal canister (from habitual fuel top-offs); faulty fuel cap. Diagnostic notes: Will not affect drivability but fails emissions inspection. A bi-directional scan tool can command the vent (CVS) valve closed while listening for the click; a smoke machine finds the small leaks. Note: the tank-side test (P1456) must pass before the canister-side test runs, so fix P1456 first when both appear.

title: DTC P1491 (honda)
text: DTC P1491 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) Valve Lift Insufficient Detected. Possible causes: faulty EGR valve; clogged EGR ports/passages in intake manifold (carbon buildup — very common on V6 Accord); faulty EGR vacuum regulator/solenoid. Diagnostic notes: Honda TSB covers the V6 Accord: remove the intake manifold, drill out the EGR port, and install a stainless-steel sleeve kit to prevent carbon re-clogging (goodwill/warranty extension applied on some vehicles). Closed-valve lift-sensor voltage is normally 1.1-1.2V on the WHT/BLK wire; manually applying battery voltage to the valve should swing it to ~4.0V. Use OEM EGR parts.

title: DTC P1498 (honda)
text: DTC P1498 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) Valve Lift Sensor High Voltage. Possible causes: faulty EGR valve/position sensor (note: aftermarket EGR valves have caused repeat P1498); EGR harness connector not supplying 5V reference. Diagnostic notes: Check the harness connector to the EGR for 5V reference (measured ~5.1V good). If reference voltage is present and the code returns, suspect the EGR valve itself.

title: DTC P1607 (honda)
text: DTC P1607 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): ECM/PCM Internal Circuit Failure A. Possible causes: failed ECM/PCM (bad solder joints / cracked power rectifier reported); weak battery or charging-system fault (low voltage can set it); corroded/loose ECM/PCM powers, grounds, or connector pins. Diagnostic notes: Honda procedure: reset the ECM/PCM (disconnect ~5 minutes), ignition ON 40 seconds, recheck. If P1607 returns, update the ECM/PCM software or substitute a known-good unit — if the symptom clears, replace the original. Rule out battery/charging first (cold-weather P1607 that clears when warm points at solder-joint/connection issues). PCM replacement requires immobilizer reprogramming.

title: DTC P1885 (honda)
text: DTC P1885 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Problem in CVT Drive Pulley Speed Sensor Circuit. Possible causes: faulty CVT drive pulley speed sensor; wiring fault between sensor and TCM. Diagnostic notes: Honda advanced diagnostics: malfunction detected when drive pulley speed reads lower than the TCM-estimated value (factor 0.53 vs engine speed) for 15 seconds in D/L/R. One drive cycle, MIL on, D indicator blinks. CONFLICT (A-vs-A, recorded not resolved): Honda SB 03-020 [A] maps P1885 to 'Secondary Gear Speed Sensor 2 Circuit Malfunction' (Civic Hybrid). The Insight-CVT advanced-diagnostics mapping above ('Problem in CVT Drive Pulley Speed Sensor Circuit') is also [A]; likely model/generation-dependent. Verify per model.

title: DTC P1886 (honda)
text: DTC P1886 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Problem in CVT Driven Pulley Speed Sensor Circuit (no signal). Possible causes: faulty CVT driven pulley speed sensor; wiring fault. Diagnostic notes: Honda advanced diagnostics: no signals from the driven pulley speed sensor for 15 seconds. Drive-pattern retest: hold 600+ RPM in D for 15 seconds, or steady 43-62 mph for 15 seconds.

title: DTC P1890 (honda)
text: DTC P1890 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Problem in Shift Control System (CVT Speed Control System). Possible causes: incorrect PCM learning value causing CVT pressure problem (2015-16 Accord/CR-V — Honda product update); CVT belt slip; drive/driven pulley pressure control solenoid fault. Diagnostic notes: Honda product update (service bulletin 16-053, Aug 2016) for 2015-16 Accord and CR-V: incorrect learning value in the PCM can cause CVT belt slip at highway speeds (RPM surge) and set P1890. Repair: update PGM-FI software; if the DTC is already set, replace the transmission AND update software. One drive cycle, MIL on, D indicator blinks. CONFLICT (A-vs-A, recorded not resolved): Honda SB 03-020 [A] maps P1890 to 'Problem in CVT Speed Sensor 2 Circuit' (Civic Hybrid). The Insight-CVT advanced-diagnostics mapping above ('Problem in Shift Control System (CVT Speed Control System)') is also [A]; likely model/generation-dependent. Verify per model.

title: DTC P1894 (honda)
text: DTC P1894 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): Problem in Start Clutch System. Possible causes: solenoid valve failure; control line open/shorted; ground line open. Diagnostic notes: Honda SB 03-020 detection item [A]. CONFLICT (model/generation-dependent, recorded not resolved): micro-tronik list [C] maps P1894 to 'CVT Drive Pulley Pressure Control Valve Malfunction' (TCM VBU input voltage < 6V for 2 seconds at engine start). SB 03-020 [A] is preferred.

title: DTC P2646 (honda)
text: DTC P2646 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): "A" Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance / Stuck Off (Bank 1). Possible causes: low or dirty engine oil (check FIRST — system is oil-pressure actuated); faulty VTEC/rocker-arm oil pressure switch; faulty rocker-arm oil control solenoid (VTEC solenoid); wiring/connector fault to switch or solenoid; outdated PCM software. Diagnostic notes: Honda factory service bulletin (SB-10052884-2696, July 2013) for 2003-12 Accord L4, 2002-05 Civic Si, 2002-09 CR-V, 2011 CR-Z, 2003-11 Element, 2007-11 Fit: replace the VTEC oil pressure switch (P/N 37250-PNE-G01). Honda's own code meaning: "oil pressure switch circuit, low voltage". After repair, clear with scan tool and drive normally to confirm.

title: DTC P2647 (honda)
text: DTC P2647 (honda manufacturer-specific, category P): "A" Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On (Bank 1). Possible causes: faulty VTEC oil pressure switch (circuit high voltage); low/contaminated oil. Diagnostic notes: Companion to P2646: P2646 = oil pressure switch circuit low voltage, P2647 = high voltage. Same TSB switch replacement (P/N 37250-PNE-G01) applies to 2003-05 Accord L4, 2003-05 Element, 2002-05 CR-V per Honda dealer tech guidance.

title: DTC U0155 (honda)
text: DTC U0155 (honda manufacturer-specific, category U): F-CAN Malfunction (Gauge Control Module - ECM/PCM). Possible causes: open in F-CAN wiring between gauge control module and ECM/PCM (check continuity ECM connector A36/A37 to gauge 36P connector terminals 1/19); faulty gauge control module; poor connections/loose terminals. Diagnostic notes: Honda's descriptor for U0155 is F-CAN-specific (not the generic "lost communication with IPC" text). Honda procedure: clear with HDS, recheck; jump the SCS line; continuity-check the CAN lines; substitute a known-good gauge control module. Remember the gauge module IS the F-CAN/B-CAN gateway on 2006-~2015 models — a dead gateway produces exactly this code plus an OBD-II link error.

title: DTC P1128 (vw)
text: DTC P1128 (vw manufacturer-specific, category P): Long Term Fuel Trim — System Too Lean (Bank 1). Possible causes: vacuum/intake leaks (unmetered air); MAF under-reporting (Ross-Tech notes the MAF may die slowly without setting a MAF code — 17536/P1128 is the classic symptom); exhaust leak ahead of O2 sensor; low fuel pressure. Diagnostic notes: VAG 5-digit: 17536. Ross-Tech MAF tech tip: a dying MAF under-reports airflow and the ECU compensates lean — check MAF g/s against spec under load, not just at idle. WD-40/propane around intake joints to find vacuum leaks.

title: DTC P1340 (vw)
text: DTC P1340 (vw manufacturer-specific, category P): Camshaft Position Sensor (G40) / Engine Speed Sensor (G28) — Incorrect Correlation. Possible causes: timing belt/chain incorrectly installed (chain probably lengthened); Camshaft Position Sensor (G40) faulty; Engine Speed Sensor (G28) faulty. Diagnostic notes: VAG 5-digit: 17748. Ross-Tech: check timing installation (use MVB to check chain), check/replace G40 and G28. Special notes: on 1.8T check engine oil pressure (pickup may be restricted) and confirm the correct G40 is installed (single-gap vs 4-gap); on VR6 see Technical Bulletin 15-07-03; on 30-valve V6 with companion code 17755 check cam chain tensioners are on the correct heads. Almost always a mechanical timing deficiency, not just a sensor.

title: DTC P1476 (vw)
text: DTC P1476 (vw manufacturer-specific, category P): EVAP Emission Control System Leak Detection Pump — Malfunction / Insufficient Vacuum. Possible causes: EVAP system faulty/leaking; leak detection pump faulty; insufficient vacuum supply to the pump. Diagnostic notes: VAG 5-digit: 17884. Check the EVAP system for leaks, check the LDP itself, check vacuum supply at the LDP. Technician guidance: check the gas cap first (worn seal), then inspect all vacuum lines — the braided fabric lines near the air filter housing are known to fail; larger lines can soften, collapse or split. The LDP sits below the air filter housing at the frame rail (2.0). VCDS basic settings can exercise the LDP (listen for clicking).

title: DTC U1121 (vw)
text: DTC U1121 (vw manufacturer-specific, category U): Databus — Missing Message. Possible causes: indicated control module not transmitting; wiring/connector fault; module offline after coding change. Diagnostic notes: VW TSB 01-21-10 lists U112100 as logged across multiple control units (front camera, HV battery charger, etc.), usually passive/sporadic. Extremely common on MQB-platform vehicles — often a consequence of another module's fault rather than a databus wiring problem. Diagnose the indicated missing-message source (symptom byte identifies it) before condemning wiring.

title: DTC U1122 (vw)
text: DTC U1122 (vw manufacturer-specific, category U): Databus — Implausible Message. Possible causes: transmitting module sending out-of-range values; software mismatch after retrofit. Diagnostic notes: Seen in VCDS scans as "U1122 00 - Implausible Message". Often accompanies retrofits or module swaps.

title: DTC U1123 (vw)
text: DTC U1123 (vw manufacturer-specific, category U): Databus — Received Error Value. Possible causes: transmitting module reporting an error state; e.g. ACC reporting irreversible error cascades U1123 into dependent modules. Diagnostic notes: VW TSB 01-21-10 lists U112300 (received error value for data bus). VCDS scans show it with a bracketed source identifier (e.g. the ACC or instrument cluster message that carried the error value). Usually passive; clear and road-test.

title: DTC P1148 (nissan)
text: DTC P1148 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): Closed Loop Control (Bank 1) — A/F sensor closed-loop fault. Possible causes: failed A/F sensor (bank 1 sensor 1); damaged sensor connectors; poor grounding; wiring shorts; exhaust leaks. Diagnostic notes: Nissan TSB NTB04-032a covers 2004 Titan/Armada MIL ON with P1148/P1168 — fix is an ECM reprogram (verify ECM part number against the bulletin first). On other models, inspect the A/F sensor harness and connectors before condemning the sensor.

title: DTC P1165 (nissan)

title: DTC P1168 (nissan)
text: DTC P1168 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): Closed Loop Control (Bank 2) — A/F sensor closed-loop fault. Possible causes: failed A/F sensor (bank 2 sensor 1); wiring/connector damage; poor grounding. Diagnostic notes: Bank-2 counterpart of P1148; same TSB NTB04-032a ECM-reprogram coverage on 2004 Titan/Armada.

title: DTC P1211 (nissan)

title: DTC P1212 (nissan)
text: DTC P1212 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): ABS/TCS Communication Line — ECM cannot receive information from ABS actuator and electric unit (control unit) continuously. Possible causes: CAN communication line open or shorted (harness/connectors); ABS actuator and electric unit (control unit); weak battery. Diagnostic notes: Diagnose U1000/U1001 communication codes FIRST before chasing P1212; the TCM/ABS module is not necessarily at fault.

title: DTC P1217 (nissan)
text: DTC P1217 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): Engine Over Temperature (Overheat).

title: DTC P1273 (nissan)
text: DTC P1273 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): A/F Sensor Bank 1 Lean Shift Monitoring — A/F signal shifted lean for a specified period. Possible causes: faulty A/F sensor 1 (bank 1); sensor harness open/shorted; poor electrical connection; low fuel pressure; faulty fuel injector; faulty mass air flow sensor; intake air leaks. Diagnostic notes: Nissan TSBs 04-090A/04-126/04-027a/05-095/04-025 cover P1273/P1283 on 2004-2005 VQ35/VQ40 vehicles — review the bulletins before normal troubleshooting. After repair, clear the mixture-ratio self-learning data or the code can return.

title: DTC P1274 (nissan)
text: DTC P1274 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): A/F Sensor Bank 1 Rich Shift Monitoring. Diagnostic notes: Bank-1 rich counterpart of P1273; referenced in the same Nissan TSB family (04-090A series).

title: DTC P1283 (nissan)
text: DTC P1283 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): A/F Sensor Bank 2 Lean Shift Monitoring — A/F signal shifted lean for a specified period. Possible causes: faulty A/F sensor 1 (bank 2); sensor harness open/shorted; poor electrical connection; low fuel pressure; faulty fuel injector; intake air leaks; faulty air flow meter. Diagnostic notes: Same TSB family and self-learning-clear requirement as P1273 (bank 2).

title: DTC P1284 (nissan)

P1550 meaning is model/year-dependent — verify against the year-specific FSM.

title: DTC P1610 (nissan)
text: DTC P1610 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): NATS Lock Mode — NATS shifted to a mode preventing engine start after 5+ consecutive start attempts with an unregistered key or malfunctioning IMMU/ECM. Possible causes: unregistered ignition key used repeatedly; IMMU or ECM malfunction; low battery voltage mimicking NATS failure. Diagnostic notes: Nissan TSB (2005-2008 NATS vehicles, via Mitchell 1): a no-start with P1610 is often NOT NATS-related — check battery voltage/state of charge with GR-8 first; do NOT replace NATS components until battery service is ruled out. P1610 with other NATS codes (P1611-P1615, B2191-B2193, B2590) points to the service manual.

title: DTC P1611 (nissan)
text: DTC P1611 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): NATS ID Discord IMMU-ECM — ID verification between IMMU/BCM (NATS control unit) and ECM is NG; system initialization required. Possible causes: ECM replaced without NATS initialization; key ID registration lost. Diagnostic notes: Common after ECM replacement — reprogramming/initialization of keys is required (dealer or locksmith with NATS capability). Initialization erases ALL registered key IDs; have all customer keys present.

title: DTC P1612 (nissan)
text: DTC P1612 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): NATS Chain of ECM-IMMU — communication impossible between ECM and IMMU (NATS control unit). Possible causes: wiring between ECM and IMMU; IMMU malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Service manual note: CHAIN OF ECM-IMMU can be stored spuriously during the key registration procedure even when nothing is malfunctioning — do not chase it if it appears mid-registration.

title: DTC P1613 (nissan)
text: DTC P1613 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): NATS ECM INT CIRC-IMMU — malfunction of the ECM internal circuit of the IMMU communication line.

title: DTC P1614 (nissan)
text: DTC P1614 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): NATS Chain of IMMU-Key — IMMU cannot receive the key ID signal. Possible causes: NATS antenna amplifier (on ignition cylinder) faulty; unregistered or damaged key/FOB; blown fuse; weak FOB battery. Diagnostic notes: If it is the only code, try a different registered key first and check fuses; the antenna amp communicates with the BCM — inspect it before condemning the ECM.

title: DTC P1615 (nissan)
text: DTC P1615 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): NATS Difference of Key — IMMU receives the key ID signal but ID verification between key ID and IMMU is NG. Possible causes: unregistered or wrong key used. Diagnostic notes: Key must be registered to the vehicle via CONSULT-II/III NATS software; all keys must be present at registration.

title: DTC P1705 (nissan)

title: DTC P1760 (nissan)
