title: DTC P1815 (nissan)
text: DTC P1815 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): Manual Mode Switch — impossible switch-signal pattern detected (manual/non-manual/up/down). Possible causes: harness or connectors (switch circuits open or shorted); mode select switch (in A/T control device); position select switch (in A/T control device); sticky/bad microswitch in the shifter assembly. Diagnostic notes: NOT an OBD-II self-diagnostic item — CONSULT-III only. The up/down switches are in series with the manual throw; the code means one switch shows active while the auto throw also shows active, which is impossible with working switches. Check for spills/debris in the shifter assembly.

title: DTC U1000 (nissan)
text: DTC U1000 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN Communication Line — missing CAN communications on the network (signal malfunction). Possible causes: CAN communication harness open or shorted; faulty ECM; poor harness ground connection (engine compartment and behind-dash grounds); low battery voltage. Diagnostic notes: Nissan TSB NTB10-066C: always diagnose communication codes FIRST; when a module reports U1000 it is typically operating normally — the fault is external to that module. Set when communication is lost for longer than 2 seconds. A well-known field fix is cleaning/resecuring the harness grounds (paint under dash-brace grounds causes high resistance).

title: DTC U1001 (nissan)
text: DTC U1001 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN Communication Line — ECM-specific missing CAN communications on the network. Possible causes: CAN harness open/shorted; faulty ECM; poor grounds; failed combination meter or other control unit pulling the bus down. Diagnostic notes: Same TSB NTB10-066C guidance as U1000. A failed control unit (e.g. combination meter) can cause U1001 — CAN diagnostics with an advanced scanner identifies the silent module.

title: DTC U1002 (nissan)
text: DTC U1002 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN Communication Line — missing CAN communications, tighter specification than U1000. Diagnostic notes: Per TSB NTB10-066C, same diagnostic path as U1000 with a tighter detection spec.

title: DTC U1010 (nissan)
text: DTC U1010 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category U): Control Unit — module internal error. Diagnostic notes: TSB NTB10-066C: if a module is highlighted as faulty while other modules/segments show communication errors, diagnose the others first, erase DTCs, and re-run CAN diagnosis — replace the module only if it is still flagged alone.

title: DTC B2014 (nissan)
text: DTC B2014 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Chain of S/L-BCM — steering lock unit to BCM communication fault; inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: From the Nissan power-distribution service manual BCM DTC chart; engine cranking is inhibited while this code is active.

title: DTC B2190 (nissan)
text: DTC B2190 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Difference of Key (NATS antenna) — different/unregistered key detected via NATS antenna. Possible causes: unregistered key used. Diagnostic notes: BCM-level counterpart to P1615; resolve any U-codes (communication faults) before diagnosing B-codes.

title: DTC B2191 (nissan)
text: DTC B2191 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Difference of Key — ID verification between BCM and Intelligent Key is NG; prohibits steering-lock release / engine start with unregistered Intelligent Key. Possible causes: unregistered Intelligent Key; Intelligent Key malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Nissan service-manual procedure: perform initialization with CONSULT-III and re-register ALL Intelligent Keys. CONFLICT: one YouTube DTC video labels B2191 as "HO2S Heater Circuit Short (Right Bank)" — this contradicts the Nissan service manual and is almost certainly a mislabeled generic decode; the service-manual definition (Difference of Key) is used here.

title: DTC B2192 (nissan)
text: DTC B2192 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): ID Discord BCM-ECM — BCM performs ID verification with ECM; inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: BCM-level counterpart to P1611; erase DTC after initialization.

title: DTC B2193 (nissan)
text: DTC B2193 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Chain of BCM-ECM — BCM to ECM communication chain fault; inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: BCM-level counterpart to P1612; erase DTC after repair.

title: DTC B2195 (nissan)
text: DTC B2195 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Anti-Scanning — inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: NATS anti-scanning function tripped; ignition ON/OFF cycle per service manual.

title: DTC B2196 (nissan)
text: DTC B2196 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Dongle NG — inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: Dongle-unit (RHD models) malfunction; erase DTC after repair.

title: DTC B2198 (nissan)
text: DTC B2198 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): NATS Antenna Amp — inhibits engine cranking. Possible causes: NATS antenna amplifier malfunction. Diagnostic notes: BCM-level counterpart to P1614; erase DTC 500 ms after signal communication becomes consistent.

title: DTC B2590 (nissan)
text: DTC B2590 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): not verified — referenced as a NATS DTC in a Mitchell 1 Nissan TSB alongside P1610-P1615/B2191-B2193, but no definition was found in verifiable sources. Diagnostic notes: Listed here for completeness so the TSB's code set is not silently truncated; treat the definition as unverified.

title: DTC B2608 (nissan)
text: DTC B2608 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Starter Relay — inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: Starter motor relay control signal / CAN status signal inconsistency.

title: DTC B260F (nissan)
text: DTC B260F (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Engine State Signal Lost — inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: Received engine status signal (CAN) lost after power position changes to ACC.

title: DTC B2619 (nissan)
text: DTC B2619 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): BCM — inhibits engine cranking. Diagnostic notes: BCM-internal fault flag in the cranking-inhibit chart.

title: DTC B26F1 (nissan)
text: DTC B26F1 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Ignition Relay OFF — inhibits engine cranking.

title: DTC C1101 (nissan)
text: DTC C1101 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): RR RH Sensor 1 — circuit of rear RH wheel sensor is open. Possible causes: wheel sensor; sensor reluctor/tone ring; wiring harness between ABS module and sensor; faulty ABS actuator and electric unit (control unit). Diagnostic notes: From the Nissan brake-control service manual self-diagnostic item chart. If the sensor was already replaced with no change, inspect the reluctor ring and the harness before condemning the ABS unit; a capable scanner reading ABS live wheel-speed data is the fastest next step.

title: DTC C1102 (nissan)
text: DTC C1102 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): RR LH Sensor 1 — circuit of rear LH wheel sensor is open. Possible causes: wheel sensor; reluctor; harness; ABS control unit. Diagnostic notes: Same diagnostic path as C1101 (rear LH position).

title: DTC C1103 (nissan)
text: DTC C1103 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): FR RH Sensor 1 — circuit of front RH wheel sensor is open. Possible causes: wheel sensor; reluctor; harness; ABS control unit. Diagnostic notes: Same diagnostic path as C1101 (front RH position).

title: DTC C1104 (nissan)
text: DTC C1104 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): FR LH Sensor 1 — circuit of front LH wheel sensor is open. Possible causes: wheel sensor; reluctor; harness; ABS control unit. Diagnostic notes: Same diagnostic path as C1101 (front LH position). Note: some scan tools convert Nissan 2-digit ABS codes to 4-digit codes inaccurately — confirm with a Nissan-capable tool.

title: DTC C1105 (nissan)
text: DTC C1105 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): RR RH Sensor 2 — circuit of rear RH wheel sensor is shorted, or sensor power voltage is unusual. Possible causes: shorted sensor circuit; abnormal sensor supply voltage; excessive gap between wheel sensor and sensor rotor (control unit cannot identify pulses).

title: DTC C1106 (nissan)
text: DTC C1106 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): RR LH Sensor 2 — circuit of rear LH wheel sensor is shorted, or sensor power voltage is unusual. Possible causes: shorted sensor circuit; abnormal sensor supply voltage; excessive sensor-to-rotor gap.

title: DTC C1107 (nissan)
text: DTC C1107 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): FR RH Sensor 2 — circuit of front RH wheel sensor is shorted, or sensor power voltage is unusual. Possible causes: shorted sensor circuit; abnormal sensor supply voltage; excessive sensor-to-rotor gap.

title: DTC C1108 (nissan)
text: DTC C1108 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): FR LH Sensor 2 — circuit of front LH wheel sensor is shorted, or sensor power voltage is unusual. Possible causes: shorted sensor circuit; abnormal sensor supply voltage; excessive sensor-to-rotor gap.

title: DTC C1109 (nissan)
text: DTC C1109 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): Battery Voltage Abnormal — ABS actuator and electric unit (control unit) power voltage too low. Possible causes: low battery voltage; charging system fault. Diagnostic notes: Check battery/charging before condemning the ABS unit — low voltage alone sets this code.

title: DTC C1110 (nissan)
text: DTC C1110 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): Controller Failure — internal malfunction of ABS actuator and electric unit (control unit). Possible causes: internal ABS control-unit failure. Diagnostic notes: Service-manual reference: ABS/TCS/VDC control unit inspection; this code means the unit itself, not its inputs.

title: DTC C1111 (nissan)
text: DTC C1111 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): Pump Motor — ABS pump motor fault during actuator motor operation. Possible causes: ABS pump motor; power/ground to the pump. Diagnostic notes: The pump can be bench-tested by remotely applying power and ground to verify it activates.

title: DTC P2111 (toyota)
text: DTC P2111 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Open. Possible causes: throttle actuator; throttle body assembly; throttle valve; ECM; wire harness or connector. Diagnostic notes: Set when the ECM signals the throttle actuator to close but it stays open (1-trip). Monitor logic: throttle valve remains at a fixed angle despite high drive current (2 A+, 80%+ close duty) with no TP voltage change for 0.5 s. MIL immediate. Confirmation: clear DTCs, start engine, fully depress and release the pedal quickly.

title: DTC P2112 (toyota)
text: DTC P2112 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Closed. Possible causes: throttle actuator; throttle body assembly; throttle valve; ECM; wire harness or connector. Diagnostic notes: Mirror of P2111 — ECM signals open, actuator stays closed (2 A+, 80%+ open duty, no TP voltage change, 0.5 s, 1-trip, MIL immediate).

title: DTC P2118 (toyota)
text: DTC P2118 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range / Performance. Possible causes: open in ETCS power source (+BM) circuit; battery; battery terminals; ETCS fuse; ECM. Diagnostic notes: The ETCS has a dedicated +BM power supply; when it drops below 4 V for 0.8 s+ the ECM calls it an open and cuts current to the throttle actuator. After repair, cycle the ignition off for the ECM to re-allow actuator current.

title: DTC P2120 (toyota)
text: DTC P2120 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "D" Circuit. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: VPA fluctuates rapidly beyond the upper/lower malfunction thresholds for 0.5 s+ (1-trip). Check Accel Sensor Out No.1/No.2 via Techstream (Data List).

title: DTC P2121 (toyota)
text: DTC P2121 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "D" Circuit Range/Performance. Possible causes: accelerator pedal position sensor assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Range/performance companion to the P2120 circuit codes. Toyota inspection procedure checks VCPA/VCP2 reference voltage (4.5–5.5 V), then replaces the pedal sensor assembly, then the ECM if the DTC recurs.

title: DTC P2122 (toyota)
text: DTC P2122 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "D" Circuit Low Input. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; open in VCPA circuit; open or ground short in VPA circuit; ECM. Diagnostic notes: VPA 0.4 V or less for 0.5 s+ (1-trip). MIL on, DTC stored.

title: DTC P2123 (toyota)
text: DTC P2123 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "D" Circuit High Input. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; open in EPA circuit; ECM. Diagnostic notes: VPA 4.8 V or more for 2.0 s+ (1-trip). MIL on, DTC stored.

title: DTC P2125 (toyota)
text: DTC P2125 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "E" Circuit. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: VPA2 fluctuates rapidly beyond thresholds for 0.5 s+ (1-trip) — the "E"/No.2 channel mirror of P2120.

title: DTC P2126 (toyota)
text: DTC P2126 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "E" Circuit Range/Performance. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Range/performance companion to P2125; see P2121 diagnostic note for the Toyota inspection sequence.

title: DTC P2127 (toyota)
text: DTC P2127 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "E" Circuit Low Input. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; open in VCP2 circuit; open or ground short in VPA2 circuit; ECM. Diagnostic notes: VPA2 1.2 V or less for 0.5 s+ (1-trip). MIL on, DTC stored.

title: DTC P2128 (toyota)
text: DTC P2128 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "E" Circuit High Input. Possible causes: accelerator pedal sensor assembly; open in EPA2 circuit; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Both conditions for 2.0 s+ (1-trip): (a) VPA2 4.8 V or more, (b) VPA between 0.4 V and 3.45 V.

title: DTC P2135 (toyota)
text: DTC P2135 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "A" / "B" Voltage Correlation. Possible causes: short between VTA1 and VTA2 circuits; throttle position sensor (built into throttle body with motor assembly); ECM. Diagnostic notes: Correlation code for the two TP sensors in the throttle body. Set when (a) VTA1–VTA2 differ by 0.02 V or less for 0.5 s+, or (b) VTA1 is 0.2 V or less and VTA2 is 1.75 V or less for 0.4 s+ (1-trip). Check Throttle Position No.1/No.2 via Techstream — normal: No.1 0.5–1.1 V released / 3.2–4.8 V depressed; No.2 2.1–3.1 V released / 4.6–4.98 V depressed.

title: DTC P2138 (toyota)
text: DTC P2138 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor / Switch "D" / "E" Voltage Correlation. Possible causes: short between VPA and VPA2 circuits; accelerator pedal sensor assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: APP-sensor correlation companion to P2135. Set when (a) |VPA − VPA2| is 0.02 V or less, or (b) VPA is 0.4 V or less and VPA2 is 1.2 V or less, for 2.0 s+ (1-trip). Check Accel Sensor Out No.1/No.2 via Techstream.

title: DTC P2195 (toyota)
text: DTC P2195 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Oxygen (A/F) Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open or short in A/F sensor (Bank 1 Sensor 1) circuit; A/F sensor; intake system; fuel pressure; fuel injector assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Two monitors: (1) voltage — A/F voltage above 3.8 V (very lean) while HO2 sensor rises from below 0.21 V to 0.59 V+ for 5 s; (2) current — during fuel-cut, A/F current 3.6 mA or more for 3 s cumulative (high-side stuck). Use the A/F CONTROL active test to graph A/F vs HO2 response; P2A00 may set alongside.

title: DTC P2196 (toyota)
text: DTC P2196 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Oxygen (A/F) Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open or short in A/F sensor (Bank 1 Sensor 1) circuit; A/F sensor; intake system; fuel pressure; fuel injector assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Mirror of P2195: A/F voltage below 2.8 V (very rich) while HO2 falls from 0.59 V+ to below 0.21 V for 5 s, or fuel-cut A/F current below ~1.0 mA for 3 s cumulative (low-side stuck). 2-trip logic.

title: DTC P2197 (toyota)
text: DTC P2197 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Oxygen (A/F) Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open or short in A/F sensor (Bank 2 Sensor 1) circuit; A/F sensor; intake system; fuel pressure; fuel injector assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 mirror of P2195. On Toyota V-engines Bank 2 is the bank containing cylinder No. 2.

title: DTC P2198 (toyota)
text: DTC P2198 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Oxygen (A/F) Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open or short in A/F sensor (Bank 2 Sensor 1) circuit; A/F sensor; intake system; fuel pressure; fuel injector assembly; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 mirror of P2196.

title: DTC P2A00 (toyota)
text: DTC P2A00 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): A/F Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open or short in A/F sensor circuit; A/F sensor; A/F sensor heater; EFI main relay; air induction system; fuel pressure; injector; ECM. Diagnostic notes: After warm-up the ECM runs active A/F control (~10 s), forcing injection volume up/down around stoichiometry and measuring the A/F sensor response rate; if the deterioration level is below threshold the DTC sets. Confirmation: check Mode 06 O2-sensor monitor data via Techstream. Although the title says "oxygen sensor", on Toyota this is the wideband A/F sensor.

title: DTC P2A03 (toyota)
text: DTC P2A03 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): A/F Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: not documented (same family as P2A00). Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 companion to P2A00 — see P2A00 notes. Listed alongside P2A00 in the Toyota SFI charts.

title: DTC P2440 (toyota)
text: DTC P2440 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1). Possible causes: air switching valve stuck open (carbon buildup, debris from disintegrated air-pump filter foam or impeller blades, moisture); air injection pump. Diagnostic notes: Toyota/Lexus secondary-air systems are a known failure family. A Toyota TSB (2005–2009 2UZ-FE 4.7L) attributes these codes to debris passing through the air pump contaminating the valves — inspect pump, hoses and bypass valve; replacement typically covers pump + hoses + valve assembly. Field check: pull the hose, start the engine — exhaust at the valve port means the valve is stuck open.

title: DTC P2441 (toyota)
text: DTC P2441 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1). Possible causes: air switching valve stuck closed (carbon, debris); air injection pump. Diagnostic notes: See P2440 — same TSB/debris context. Bypass-harness field fixes target this family but defeat an emissions monitor; not recommended as a repair.

title: DTC P2442 (toyota)
text: DTC P2442 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2). Possible causes: air switching valve stuck open (carbon, debris, moisture); air injection pump. Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 mirror of P2440.

title: DTC P2443 (toyota)
text: DTC P2443 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2). Possible causes: air switching valve stuck closed (carbon, debris); air injection pump. Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 mirror of P2441.

title: DTC P2444 (toyota)
text: DTC P2444 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck ON (Bank 1). Possible causes: air injection pump relay stuck; pump control circuit fault. Diagnostic notes: Pump-side companion to the valve codes — the pump runs when it should be off. Not individually enumerated in the forum guides; definition follows the SAE J2012 P244x pattern (P2445/P2447 stuck-OFF are documented there).

title: DTC P2445 (toyota)
text: DTC P2445 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck OFF (Bank 1). Possible causes: failed air injection pump; pump relay/circuit open; debris-seized pump. Diagnostic notes: See P2440 — pump failures in this family commonly trace to the disintegrating internal foam filter.

title: DTC P2446 (toyota)
text: DTC P2446 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck ON (Bank 2). Possible causes: air injection pump relay stuck; pump control circuit fault. Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 mirror of P2444 — see P2444 note.

title: DTC P2447 (toyota)
text: DTC P2447 (SAE J2012 generic, category P): Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck OFF (Bank 2). Possible causes: failed air injection pump; pump relay/circuit open. Diagnostic notes: Bank 2 mirror of P2445.

title: DTC P3000 (toyota)
text: DTC P3000 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery Fault.

title: DTC P3001 (toyota)
text: DTC P3001 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery ECU Fault. Diagnostic notes: NOTE — the source list gives both P3001 and P3100 as "High Voltage Battery ECU Fault" and P3105/P3109 as battery-ECU communication faults; the distinctions are the source's, not independently verified.

title: DTC P3002 (toyota)
text: DTC P3002 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery ECU Communication Fault. Possible causes: wire harness; battery ECU. Diagnostic notes: A Toyota master technician (JustAnswer) describes the P3105-family symptom as communication failure between the battery ECU (inside the HV battery case) and the HV ECU (under the passenger footrest) — check connectors and harness before condemning either ECU.

title: DTC P3004 (toyota)
text: DTC P3004 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Power Cable Fault.

title: DTC P3005 (toyota)
text: DTC P3005 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Fuse Blown.

title: DTC P3006 (toyota)
text: DTC P3006 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery State Of Charge Uneven.

title: DTC P3009 (toyota)
text: DTC P3009 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Leak Detected. Diagnostic notes: High-voltage insulation/leak fault — hybrid models only. Treat as a safety-relevant code; do not probe HV circuits without training and PPE.

title: DTC P3011 (toyota)
text: DTC P3011 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery Module 1 Fault. Diagnostic notes: P3011 through P3029 map to HV battery modules/blocks 1 through 19 (per the source list); only P3011 is entered here as the range representative — do not invent per-module entries.

title: DTC P3030 (toyota)
text: DTC P3030 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery Monitor Circuit Fault.

title: DTC P3060 (toyota)
text: DTC P3060 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery Temperature Sensor or Circuit Fault.

title: DTC P3076 (toyota)
text: DTC P3076 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery Cooling Fan Abnormal Air Flow.

title: DTC P3077 (toyota)
text: DTC P3077 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery Cooling Fan Motor or Circuit Fault.

title: DTC P3100 (toyota)
text: DTC P3100 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery ECU Fault. Diagnostic notes: See P3001 note — the source lists both P3001 and P3100 with this description; distinction unverified.

title: DTC P3101 (toyota)
text: DTC P3101 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Engine System Fault. Diagnostic notes: Seen on Gen 1 Prius alongside P3191 (engine does not start); owner threads pair it with no-start diagnosis (fuel, spark, MAF).

title: DTC P3105 (toyota)
text: DTC P3105 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery ECU or Communication Circuit Fault. Possible causes: wire harness; battery ECU. Diagnostic notes: See P3002 — battery ECU ↔ HV ECU communication failure; reseat connectors, check harness continuity.

title: DTC P3106 (toyota)
text: DTC P3106 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Engine ECM or Communication Circuit Fault.

title: DTC P3107 (toyota)
text: DTC P3107 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Air Bag ECU or Communication Circuit Fault. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid-vehicle-control view of an SRS ECU communication fault — check SRS codes as well.

title: DTC P3108 (toyota)
text: DTC P3108 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): A/C Amplifier ECU or Communication Circuit Fault.

title: DTC P3109 (toyota)
text: DTC P3109 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Battery ECU or Communication Circuit Fault. Diagnostic notes: See P3105 note — source lists both P3105 and P3109 with this description; distinction unverified.

title: DTC P3110 (toyota)
text: DTC P3110 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): HV IGCT Relay or Circuit Fault.

title: DTC P3115 (toyota)
text: DTC P3115 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Hybrid System Main Relay Fault. Diagnostic notes: System main relay (SMR) circuit — hybrid models only.

title: DTC P3120 (toyota)
text: DTC P3120 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Transaxle Fault. Diagnostic notes: An ATSG technical bulletin reproduces a scan tool showing "P3120 HV transaxle assy malfunction" set in the HV ECU with the master warning lamp on and READY on; information sub-codes narrow it to resolver/MG data — read the INF codes before condemning the transaxle.

title: DTC P3125 (toyota)
text: DTC P3125 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Converter & Inverter Assembly Malfunction. Possible causes: +B short in DC/DC converter NODD wiring; DC/DC converter malfunction; open or ground short in DC/DC converter NODD wiring; converter & inverter assembly; wire harness. Diagnostic notes: From the 2002 Prius repair manual (RM883U DI-271): the HV ECU monitors DC/DC converter operation because a failed converter drains the auxiliary battery until the car cannot keep driving. Information codes 263/264/265 narrow it (263: +B short in NODD wiring; 264: converter malfunction; 265: open/GND short in NODD wiring). NOTE: a Toyota TSB advises that if P3125 is present due to P3130, do not diagnose P3125 — fix the inverter cooling fault first.

title: DTC P3130 (toyota)
text: DTC P3130 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Inverter Cooling System Malfunction. Possible causes: inverter coolant pump (electric water pump) failure; coolant flow blockage/kinked hoses; low coolant. Diagnostic notes: Snap-on SureTrack documented case (2001 Prius): inverter temperature exceeded range with clean full coolant — no circulation at the reservoir despite voltage at the pump; replacing the electric water pump fixed it. A Toyota TSB covers P3130+P3125 together: check inverter-reservoir water flow first; if P3125 is present due to P3130, ignore P3125.

title: DTC P3135 (toyota)
text: DTC P3135 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): High Voltage Circuit Breaker Sensor Fault.

title: DTC P3140 (toyota)
text: DTC P3140 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Interlock Malfunction. Possible causes: service plug not installed correctly (handle not flipped up, bent/broken microswitch tab); inverter terminal cover or sensor cover removed; open in interlock signal circuit. Diagnostic notes: From the 2002 Prius repair manual (RM883U): the HV ECU shuts down the system main relay if it detects safety-device operation (service plug removal, inverter terminal cover, sensor cover) while the vehicle is stopped (INF 350); an open in the interlock signal circuit while running sets INF 351 without shutting down HV. PriusChat field reports confirm the service-plug microswitch as the common cause — the code returns immediately at key-on until the switch closes.

title: DTC P3145 (toyota)
text: DTC P3145 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Vehicle Speed Sensor or Circuit Fault. Diagnostic notes: Hybrid-vehicle-control view of a vehicle speed sensor fault.

title: DTC P3193 (toyota)
text: DTC P3193 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category P): Fuel Run Out. Possible causes: out of fuel; ECM. Diagnostic notes: Set when the fuel-low-level signal is input to the ECM AND the P3190/P3191 detection condition is satisfied (1-trip). Hybrid note: running out of fuel forces the car onto battery-only operation, deep-discharging the HV battery — refuel and recharge promptly.

title: DTC B1100 (toyota)
text: DTC B1100 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Airbag Sensor Assembly Center Malfunction. Possible causes: airbag sensor assembly center (internal malfunction). Diagnostic notes: Recorded when the airbag sensor assembly center detects its own internal malfunction (sub-code /31 on 2004 Corolla). Manual hint: if any other SRS code is present at the same time, repair the other code FIRST. Inspection starts with IG2 supply voltage (10–14 V) — check battery/charging system if out of range. Disconnect battery and wait 90+ seconds before probing SRS circuits.

title: DTC B1135 (toyota)
text: DTC B1135 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Half Connection Detection Malfunction. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — make-dependent meaning. On Toyota (2004 Corolla RM1037U SRS chart, B1135/24) this is "HALF CONNECTION DETECTION MALFUNCTION" (connector half-connection detection) [A]. On Nissan (2014 Cube SRS manual) B1135 is "SIDE AIR BAG MODULE LH [VB-SHORT]" [B]. Do not cross-apply.

title: DTC B1140 (toyota)
text: DTC B1140 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Side Airbag Sensor Assembly RH Malfunction. Possible causes: side airbag sensor assembly RH; airbag sensor assembly center; instrument panel wire No.3. Diagnostic notes: Satellite side-impact sensor (RH) internal malfunction (sub-code /32 on 2004 Corolla).

title: DTC B1141 (toyota)
text: DTC B1141 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Side Airbag Sensor Assembly LH Malfunction. Possible causes: side airbag sensor assembly LH; airbag sensor assembly center; instrument panel wire No.3. Diagnostic notes: Satellite side-impact sensor (LH) internal malfunction (sub-code /33 on 2004 Corolla).

title: DTC B1150 (toyota)
text: DTC B1150 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Classification ECU Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: occupant classification ECU; FSR+/FSR- sensor circuit (open/short to ground or to B+); wire harness. Diagnostic notes: From the 2005 4Runner repair manual (RM1165U) CI B1150/23 diagnostics: check FSR+ to FSR- isolation (1 MΩ or higher), then FSR lines to body ground (below 1 V with ignition ON). Occupant-classification (passenger weight-sensor) circuit.

title: DTC B1153 (toyota)
text: DTC B1153 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Seat Position Airbag Sensor Assembly Malfunction. Possible causes: seat position airbag sensor; airbag sensor assembly center; instrument panel wire No.3; wire harness (seat position airbag sensor – front seat inner belt assembly). Diagnostic notes: Seat-track position sensor used for dual-stage deployment decisions (sub-code /25 on 2004 Corolla).

title: DTC B1180 (toyota)
text: DTC B1180 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in D Squib (2nd Step) Circuit. Possible causes: horn button assembly (D squib 2nd step); spiral cable sub-assembly; airbag sensor assembly center; instrument panel wire. Diagnostic notes: Driver airbag 2nd-stage squib line short (sub-code /17). A Toyota technician (JustAnswer) notes the clockspring (spiral cable) is the most common cause; airbag sensor and wiring are the other candidates. B1181 (dedup) is the open-circuit sibling; B1182 is the short-to-ground sibling.

title: DTC B1182 (toyota)
text: DTC B1182 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in D Squib (2nd Step) Circuit. Possible causes: horn button assembly (D squib 2nd step); spiral cable sub-assembly; airbag sensor assembly center; instrument panel wire. Diagnostic notes: Third member of the chart sequence B1180/17 (short), B1181/18 (open), B1182/19 (short to ground) — driver 2nd-stage squib. Individual detection-item text not captured beyond the sequence; the short/open/GND/B+ 4-code pattern is the Toyota SRS convention.

title: DTC B1771 (toyota)
text: DTC B1771 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Detection Malfunction. Diagnostic notes: Seen on a Techstream readout alongside B1801/B1811 after steering/column work (listed as "Occupation Detection" in the owner transcription — likely "Occupant Detection"). Occupant-classification system area.

title: DTC B1800 (toyota)
text: DTC B1800 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Driver Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Set when the airbag sensor assembly receives a line-short signal 5 times in the driver squib circuit during the primary check (sub-code /51). Disconnect battery, wait 90+ seconds before probing. A failed clockspring is the classic cause.

title: DTC B1801 (toyota)
text: DTC B1801 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Driver Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Open signal received for 2 seconds (sub-code /51). A Toyota master technician (JustAnswer, Hilux B1801) identifies the spiral cable under the steering wheel as the recognized failure point; the wheel must come off to replace it.

title: DTC B1802 (toyota)
text: DTC B1802 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Driver Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-ground signal received for 0.5 seconds (sub-code /51).

title: DTC B1803 (toyota)
text: DTC B1803 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Driver Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-B+ signal received for 0.5 seconds (sub-code /51).

title: DTC B1805 (toyota)
text: DTC B1805 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Front Passenger Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 2 instrument panel wire; front passenger side squib (instrument panel passenger airbag assembly); airbag ECU assembly. Diagnostic notes: Line short detected during the primary check (sub-code /52). Passenger-dash airbag squib.

title: DTC B1806 (toyota)
text: DTC B1806 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Front Passenger Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 2 instrument panel wire; front passenger side squib (instrument panel passenger airbag assembly); airbag ECU assembly. Diagnostic notes: Open detected in the passenger squib circuit (sub-code /52). A Yaris owner thread shows this presenting as "open circuit in passenger front squib" — check for anything disconnected under/around the passenger dash and seat.

title: DTC B1807 (toyota)
text: DTC B1807 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Front Passenger Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 2 instrument panel wire; front passenger side squib (instrument panel passenger airbag assembly); airbag ECU assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-ground detected (sub-code /52).

title: DTC B1808 (toyota)
text: DTC B1808 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Front Passenger Side Squib Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 2 instrument panel wire; front passenger side squib (instrument panel passenger airbag assembly); airbag ECU assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-B+ detected (sub-code /52).

title: DTC B1810 (toyota)
text: DTC B1810 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Driver Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Driver dual-stage airbag 2nd-step squib (sub-code /53). NOTE — generic B-body databases (ecutesting.com, retrolib.info) list B1810–B1813 as lamp/wiper circuits; those are non-Toyota body-control definitions. On Toyota these are SRS squib circuits per the Toyota service-manual DTC charts — do not cross-apply.

title: DTC B1811 (toyota)
text: DTC B1811 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Driver Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Open in the driver 2nd-step squib circuit (sub-code /53). A Yaris owner thread defines it as "Open in D squib (Dual stage - 2nd step) circuit" and notes the code cannot be cleared until the underlying open is repaired. See B1810 cross-apply warning.

title: DTC B1812 (toyota)
text: DTC B1812 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Driver Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-ground in the driver 2nd-step squib circuit (sub-code /53). See B1810 cross-apply warning.

title: DTC B1813 (toyota)
text: DTC B1813 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Driver Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; spiral cable (with sensor) sub-assembly; horn button assembly / steering pad (driver side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-B+ in the driver 2nd-step squib circuit (sub-code /53). See B1810 cross-apply warning.

title: DTC B1815 (toyota)
text: DTC B1815 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Front Passenger Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 3 instrument panel wire; instrument panel passenger airbag assembly (front passenger side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Passenger dual-stage airbag 2nd-step squib (sub-code /54).

title: DTC B1816 (toyota)
text: DTC B1816 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Front Passenger Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 3 instrument panel wire; instrument panel passenger airbag assembly (front passenger side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Open in the passenger 2nd-step squib circuit (sub-code /54).

title: DTC B1817 (toyota)
text: DTC B1817 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Front Passenger Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 3 instrument panel wire; instrument panel passenger airbag assembly (front passenger side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-ground in the passenger 2nd-step squib circuit (sub-code /54).

title: DTC B1818 (toyota)
text: DTC B1818 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Front Passenger Side Squib 2nd Step Circuit. Possible causes: instrument panel wire; No. 3 instrument panel wire; instrument panel passenger airbag assembly (front passenger side squib 2nd step); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-B+ in the passenger 2nd-step squib circuit (sub-code /54).

title: DTC B181A (toyota)
text: DTC B181A (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Passenger Side Airbag Variable Vent Hole Squib Circuit. Diagnostic notes: Hex-digit DTC (B181A–B181D) for the passenger airbag variable-vent-hole squib, from the Toyota Venza/4Runner/Tacoma airbag DTC charts (check-mode *2). Trouble areas not captured in the excerpts.

title: DTC B181B (toyota)
text: DTC B181B (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Passenger Side Airbag Variable Vent Hole Squib Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B181A.

title: DTC B181C (toyota)
text: DTC B181C (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Passenger Side Airbag Variable Vent Hole Squib Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B181A.

title: DTC B181D (toyota)
text: DTC B181D (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Passenger Side Airbag Variable Vent Hole Squib Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B181A.

title: DTC B1820 (toyota)
text: DTC B1820 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Side Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: No. 2 floor wire; front seat airbag assembly RH (side squib RH); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: RH seat side-airbag squib (sub-code /55). Older manuals phrase it as "Side Squib (D Seat Side)" — D = driver side on LHD vehicles.

title: DTC B1821 (toyota)
text: DTC B1821 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Side Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: floor wire / No. 2 floor wire; front seat airbag assembly RH (side squib RH); airbag sensor assembly; seat-harness chafing under the seat. Diagnostic notes: Toyota TSB EL002-08 (revised 2008) specifically covers DTC B1821/B1826 "OPEN SIDE SQUIB CIRCUIT" — SRS light on; the repair procedure addresses the seat side-airbag harness (harness chafing/pinching under the front seats). Check the seat harness routing before condemning the squib.

title: DTC B1822 (toyota)
text: DTC B1822 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Side Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: No. 2 floor wire; front seat airbag assembly RH (side squib RH); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-ground in the RH side squib circuit (sub-code /55).

title: DTC B1823 (toyota)
text: DTC B1823 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Side Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: No. 2 floor wire; front seat airbag assembly RH (side squib RH); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-B+ in the RH side squib circuit (sub-code /55).

title: DTC B1825 (toyota)
text: DTC B1825 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Side Squib LH Circuit. Possible causes: floor wire; front seat airbag assembly LH (side squib LH); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: LH seat side-airbag squib (sub-code /56).

title: DTC B1826 (toyota)
text: DTC B1826 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Side Squib LH Circuit. Possible causes: floor wire; front seat airbag assembly LH (side squib LH); airbag sensor assembly; seat-harness chafing under the seat. Diagnostic notes: Covered by Toyota TSB EL002-08 alongside B1821 — see B1821 notes.

title: DTC B1827 (toyota)
text: DTC B1827 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Side Squib LH Circuit. Possible causes: floor wire; front seat airbag assembly LH (side squib LH); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-ground in the LH side squib circuit (sub-code /56).

title: DTC B1828 (toyota)
text: DTC B1828 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Side Squib LH Circuit. Possible causes: floor wire; front seat airbag assembly LH (side squib LH); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: Short-to-B+ in the LH side squib circuit (sub-code /56).

title: DTC B1830 (toyota)
text: DTC B1830 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Curtain Shield Squib RH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: RH roof curtain-shield airbag squib (sub-code /57). Trouble areas not captured in the excerpts.

title: DTC B1831 (toyota)
text: DTC B1831 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Curtain Shield Squib RH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1830.

title: DTC B1832 (toyota)
text: DTC B1832 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Curtain Shield Squib RH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1830.

title: DTC B1833 (toyota)
text: DTC B1833 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Curtain Shield Squib RH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1830.

title: DTC B1835 (toyota)
text: DTC B1835 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Curtain Shield Squib LH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: LH roof curtain-shield airbag squib (sub-code /58).

title: DTC B1836 (toyota)
text: DTC B1836 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Curtain Shield Squib LH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1835.

title: DTC B1837 (toyota)
text: DTC B1837 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Curtain Shield Squib LH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1835.

title: DTC B1838 (toyota)
text: DTC B1838 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Curtain Shield Squib LH Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1835.

title: DTC B1840 (toyota)
text: DTC B1840 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Curtain Shield Squib RH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: RH curtain-shield 2nd-step squib (sub-code /59). Trouble areas not captured in the excerpts.

title: DTC B1841 (toyota)
text: DTC B1841 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Curtain Shield Squib RH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1840.

title: DTC B1842 (toyota)
text: DTC B1842 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Curtain Shield Squib RH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1840.

title: DTC B1843 (toyota)
text: DTC B1843 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Curtain Shield Squib RH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: See B1840.

title: DTC B1845 (toyota)
text: DTC B1845 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Curtain Shield Squib LH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: LH curtain-shield 2nd-step squib (sub-code /61). B1845 confirmed in the chart; B1846/B1847/B1848 follow the standard short/open/GND/B+ 4-code pattern but their individual detection-item rows were not captured in the excerpt.

title: DTC B1846 (toyota)
text: DTC B1846 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Open in Curtain Shield Squib LH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: Pattern-inferred sibling of B1845 — see B1845 note.

title: DTC B1847 (toyota)
text: DTC B1847 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Curtain Shield Squib LH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: Pattern-inferred sibling of B1845 — see B1845 note.

title: DTC B1848 (toyota)
text: DTC B1848 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Curtain Shield Squib LH 2nd Step Circuit. Diagnostic notes: Pattern-inferred sibling of B1845 — see B1845 note.

title: DTC B1900 (toyota)
text: DTC B1900 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short in Front Pretensioner Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: shorted seatbelt pretensioner wiring (melted/chafed insulation near the connector); front seat outer belt assembly RH (pretensioner squib); airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: RH seatbelt pretensioner squib (sub-code /73 — shared across B1900–B1903; the SRS warning light blink code alone cannot distinguish them, use a scan tool). A Yaris field thread found melted pretensioner-wire insulation a few inches from the connector with the exposed conductors touching — inspect the yellow / yellow-black pair end to end.

title: DTC B1902 (toyota)
text: DTC B1902 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to GND in Front Pretensioner Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: shorted seatbelt pretensioner wiring; front seat outer belt assembly RH; airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: See B1900 — sub-code /73 family.

title: DTC B1903 (toyota)
text: DTC B1903 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category B): Short to B+ in Front Pretensioner Squib RH Circuit. Possible causes: shorted seatbelt pretensioner wiring; front seat outer belt assembly RH; airbag sensor assembly. Diagnostic notes: See B1900 — sub-code /73 family. (B1901, the open-circuit sibling, is in the v1.2.1 file.)

title: DTC C1202 (toyota)
text: DTC C1202 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Fluid Level Low / Open Circuit in Brake Fluid Level Warning Switch Circuit. Possible causes: brake fluid level; brake fluid level warning switch; harness and connector; skid control ECU; ABS No.1 relay; ABS No.2 relay. Diagnostic notes: Check the reservoir level first — the code covers both genuinely low fluid and an open in the warning-switch circuit (sub-code /68 on Prius).

title: DTC C1233 (toyota)
text: DTC C1233 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): VSC Controller Power Line Fault. Diagnostic notes: A single community source describes C1233 as a short or break in the power line of the VSC controller; no Toyota chart excerpt was found for it in this pass.

title: DTC C1235 (toyota)
text: DTC C1235 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Foreign Matter on Front Speed Sensor RH Tip / Abnormal Pulse Waveform (FR). Possible causes: right front speed sensor; speed sensor circuit; sensor installation; sensor rotor; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Set when the speed-sensor pulse waveform is abnormal for 5 s+ at 20 km/h (12 mph) or more (sub-code /35 on Prius). The chart also lists foreign matter on the sensor tip as a cause.

title: DTC C1236 (toyota)
text: DTC C1236 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Foreign Matter on Front Speed Sensor LH Tip / Abnormal Pulse Waveform (FL). Possible causes: left front speed sensor; speed sensor circuit; sensor installation; sensor rotor; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Left-front mirror of C1235 (sub-code /36). NOTE: C1237 was not confirmed in the excerpts — do not assume it exists.

title: DTC C1238 (toyota)
text: DTC C1238 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Foreign Matter on Rear Speed Sensor RH Tip / Abnormal Pulse Waveform (RR). Possible causes: right rear speed sensor; speed sensor circuit; sensor installation; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Right-rear mirror of C1235 (sub-code /38, detailed code 304).

title: DTC C1239 (toyota)
text: DTC C1239 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Foreign Matter on Rear Speed Sensor LH Tip / Abnormal Pulse Waveform (RL). Possible causes: left rear speed sensor; speed sensor circuit; sensor installation; sensor rotor; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Left-rear mirror of C1235 (sub-code /39, detailed code 305).

title: DTC C1243 (toyota)
text: DTC C1243 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Deceleration Sensor (Constant Output). Possible causes: yaw rate sensor (deceleration sensor); yaw rate sensor circuit (deceleration sensor circuit). Diagnostic notes: From the Kluger/Highlander ABS-VSC chart (05-288): constant-output malfunction of the deceleration sensor (sub-code /43). Fail-safe: the ECU cuts current to the ABS solenoid relay and prohibits ABS control — the brake system reverts to normal (non-ABS) braking.

title: DTC C1244 (toyota)
text: DTC C1244 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Deceleration Sensor. Possible causes: yaw rate sensor (deceleration sensor); yaw rate sensor circuit (deceleration sensor circuit). Diagnostic notes: General deceleration-sensor malfunction (sub-code /44) — see C1243 fail-safe note.

title: DTC C1245 (toyota)
text: DTC C1245 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Deceleration Sensor. Possible causes: yaw rate sensor (deceleration sensor); yaw rate sensor circuit (deceleration sensor circuit). Diagnostic notes: Set when, at 30 km/h+, the difference between the acceleration/deceleration values computed from the deceleration sensor and from vehicle speed exceeds 0.35 G for 60 s+ (sub-code /45). Fail-safe per C1243.

title: DTC C1246 (toyota)
text: DTC C1246 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Master Cylinder Pressure Sensor. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake pedal stroke sensor. Diagnostic notes: Prius ECB brake system (sub-code /46). Do not confuse with C1364 (W/C pressure sensor).

title: DTC C1247 (toyota)
text: DTC C1247 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Stroke Sensor. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector. Diagnostic notes: Brake pedal stroke sensor (sub-code /47, Prius ECB).

title: DTC C1251 (toyota)
text: DTC C1251 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open in Pump Motor Circuit. Possible causes: wire harness; ABS and traction actuator. Diagnostic notes: The brake-control VSC chart lists C1251/51 as "Open in Pump Motor Circuit" (BC-109); the Kluger ABS chart phrases the same code as "ABS pump motor is locked / open circuit in pump motor circuit". Check the pump-motor circuit before condemning the actuator.

title: DTC C1252 (toyota)
text: DTC C1252 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Hydro-Booster Pump Motor Malfunction. Possible causes: brake actuator assembly; ABS MTR relay. Diagnostic notes: Prius ECB hydro-booster pump motor (sub-code /52).

title: DTC C1259 (toyota)
text: DTC C1259 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): HV System Regenerative Malfunction. Possible causes: hybrid control system. Diagnostic notes: Regenerative-brake coordination fault on the hybrid side (sub-code /58, Prius). A JustAnswer thread pairs it with P3120 on a 2001 Prius under hard acceleration — check hybrid codes alongside.

title: DTC C1267 (toyota)
text: DTC C1267 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open or Short Circuit of Brake Pedal Load Sensing Switch Circuit. Possible causes: brake pedal load sensing switch; brake pedal load sensing switch circuit; ABS No.2 fuse. Diagnostic notes: Sub-code /67 on the brake-control chart (BC-111).

title: DTC C1311 (toyota)
text: DTC C1311 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open Circuit in Main Relay 1. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; ABS No.1 relay. Diagnostic notes: Prius ECB main-relay diagnostics (sub-code /11). C1311–C1314 cover open/short of main relays 1 and 2.

title: DTC C1312 (toyota)
text: DTC C1312 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Short Circuit in Main Relay 1. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; ABS No.2 relay. Diagnostic notes: See C1311 (sub-code /12).

title: DTC C1313 (toyota)
text: DTC C1313 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Open Circuit in Main Relay 2. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; ABS No.1 relay. Diagnostic notes: See C1311 (sub-code /13).

title: DTC C1314 (toyota)
text: DTC C1314 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Short Circuit in Main Relay 2. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; ABS No.2 relay. Diagnostic notes: See C1311 (sub-code /14).

title: DTC C1315 (toyota)
text: DTC C1315 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Changeover Solenoid Malfunction (SMC1). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly (SMC1). Diagnostic notes: Prius ECB stroke-simulator cut/changeover solenoid SMC1 (sub-code /31).

title: DTC C1316 (toyota)
text: DTC C1316 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Changeover Solenoid Malfunction (SMC2). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly (SMC2). Diagnostic notes: See C1315 (sub-code /32).

title: DTC C1319 (toyota)
text: DTC C1319 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Changeover Solenoid Malfunction (SCSS). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; stroke simulator; fluid leakage. Diagnostic notes: Stroke-simulator cut solenoid (sub-code /35). The chart lists fluid leakage as a trouble area — inspect for external leaks.

title: DTC C1337 (toyota)
text: DTC C1337 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Different Diameter Tire Malfunction. Possible causes: tire size (mismatched tire diameters). Diagnostic notes: Set when wheel-speed logic detects implausible diameter differences (sub-code /37, BC-117). Check for a mismatched spare or mixed tire sizes before chasing sensors.

title: DTC C1341 (toyota)
text: DTC C1341 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Hydraulic System (FR). Possible causes: brake actuator assembly; disc rotor; fluid leakage. Diagnostic notes: Front-right hydraulic circuit malfunction (sub-code /62, Prius). A PriusChat thread notes an INF sub-code is available for C1343 (RR sibling) — expect similar detail codes here.

title: DTC C1342 (toyota)
text: DTC C1342 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Hydraulic System (FL). Possible causes: brake actuator assembly; fluid leakage. Diagnostic notes: Front-left mirror of C1341 (sub-code /63).

title: DTC C1343 (toyota)
text: DTC C1343 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in Hydraulic System (RR). Possible causes: fluid leakage; warped disc rotor; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: A PriusChat thread (Gen 2 Prius, C1241 + C1343) describes C1343 as "difficulty holding the pressure constant in the right rear brake line" — check for leaks and rotor warpage before condemning the actuator, and read the three-digit INF sub-code for the detailed workup. (C1344, the presumed RL sibling, was not verified in this pass.)

title: DTC C1352 (toyota)
text: DTC C1352 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Increasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (FR). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: Front-right pressure-increase solenoid (sub-code /21, Prius). C1352–C1355 = increasing-pressure solenoids FR/FL/RR/RL; C1356–C1359 = decreasing-pressure solenoids FR/FL/RR/RL.

title: DTC C1353 (toyota)
text: DTC C1353 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Increasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (FL). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: See C1352 (sub-code /23).

title: DTC C1354 (toyota)
text: DTC C1354 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Increasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (RR). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: See C1352 (sub-code /25).

title: DTC C1355 (toyota)
text: DTC C1355 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Increasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (RL). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: See C1352 (sub-code /27).

title: DTC C1356 (toyota)
text: DTC C1356 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Decreasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (FR). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: Front-right pressure-decrease solenoid (sub-code /22).

title: DTC C1357 (toyota)
text: DTC C1357 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Decreasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (FL). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: See C1356 (sub-code /24).

title: DTC C1358 (toyota)
text: DTC C1358 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Decreasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (RR). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: See C1356 (sub-code /26).

title: DTC C1359 (toyota)
text: DTC C1359 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Decreasing Pressure Solenoid Malfunction (RL). Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector; brake actuator assembly. Diagnostic notes: See C1356 (sub-code /28).

title: DTC C1361 (toyota)
text: DTC C1361 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Short Circuit in ABS Motor Fail Safe Relay Circuit. Possible causes: ABS1 H-fuse; VSC MTR relay; VSC MTR relay circuit; VSC FAIL relay; VSC FAIL relay circuit; ABS and traction actuator. Diagnostic notes: Sub-code /91 on the brake-control VSC chart (BC-78).

title: DTC C1364 (toyota)
text: DTC C1364 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in W/C Pressure Sensor. Possible causes: skid control ECU; harness and connector. Diagnostic notes: Wheel-cylinder pressure sensor (sub-code /61, Prius). Do not confuse with C1246 (master cylinder pressure sensor).

title: DTC C1365 (toyota)
text: DTC C1365 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Malfunction in ACC Pressure Sensor. Possible causes: brake actuator assembly (accumulator pressure sensor); skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Accumulator pressure sensor (sub-code /54, Prius).

title: DTC C1368 (toyota)
text: DTC C1368 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Linear Valve Offset Malfunction. Possible causes: initialization of linear solenoid valve and calibration undone; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Set when linear-solenoid-valve initialization/calibration has not been performed (sub-code /67, Prius) — run the calibration with Techstream.

title: DTC C1377 (toyota)
text: DTC C1377 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Capacitor Malfunction. Possible causes: brake control power supply assembly (capacitor); harness and connector; ABS No.1 fuse; ABS No.2 fuse; ABS No.3 fuse. Diagnostic notes: The brake control power supply (capacitor block, "black box near the battery in the rear" on Gen 2 Prius) provides auxiliary brake power when 12 V drops. Detailed codes: 101 capacitor deteriorated (replace), 102 excessive self-discharge, 103 input voltage 16.4 V+ for 10 s+, 105/106/108 internal charge/backup-output/voltage-monitor circuit faults, 109/110 open/short in 12 V input or OUT1/OUT2 lines. Check 12 V battery, grounds and ABS fuses first — the capacitor block itself is very reliable, and the code often appears after brake work disturbs its connectors.

title: DTC C1378 (toyota)
text: DTC C1378 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Capacitor Communication Circuit Malfunction. Possible causes: harness and connector; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Communication fault between the skid control ECU and the brake control power supply (sub-code /44, Prius).

title: DTC C1431 (toyota)
text: DTC C1431 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category C): Brake Actuator Pump Motor DTC (2012–2013 Camry). Possible causes: poor ground on the left fender side panel bracket (after collision/body repair); brake actuator pump motor. Diagnostic notes: Toyota TSB T-SB-0172-13 (Nov 2013): some 2012–2013 Camry vehicles exhibit ABS brake-actuator pump-motor noise from the engine compartment with brake, ABS and/or TRAC warning lamps on and DTC C1431 stored — caused by a poor ground on the left fender side panel bracket (loose, incorrect bolts, or improperly painted after body-shop repairs). Inspect and repair the fender grounds. The TSB excerpt does not state the formal detection-item title.

title: DTC U0101 (toyota)
text: DTC U0101 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with TCM. Possible causes: CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: On Toyota hybrids the lane-departure/pre-crash documentation phrases this as lost communication with the hybrid vehicle control ECU; the clearance-warning (IPA) documentation phrases it as lost communication with the TCM. When 2+ U-codes set simultaneously, inspect the connectors and wire harnesses of each ECU rather than chasing them individually.

title: DTC U0111 (toyota)
text: DTC U0111 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Battery Energy Control Module "A". Possible causes: hybrid battery ECU; CAN communication system; corroded battery terminals/connections. Diagnostic notes: A Toyota master technician (JustAnswer, 2007 Prius) describes U0111 as interrupted communication with the hybrid battery's computer (ECU); it commonly appears alongside P0A80 (replace hybrid battery pack). Check battery connections for corrosion first.

title: DTC U0121 (toyota)
text: DTC U0121 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with ABS Control Module. Possible causes: CANL/CANH circuit; skid control ECU. Diagnostic notes: From the 2004 Scion xB repair manual (RM1031U) CAN communication system, skid-control-ECU communication-stop mode (sub-code /94): the condition where the skid control ECU cannot transmit data continues for 5+ seconds, or the no-transmit condition repeatedly occurs 10 times.

title: DTC U0122 (toyota)
text: DTC U0122 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Vehicle Dynamics Control Module. Possible causes: CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: From the Toyota 4WD-control DTC documentation: communication lost between the skid control ECU (brake actuator assembly) and the 4-wheel-drive control ECU for 0.72 s+ (1-trip). Note: this DTC also appears transiently while skid-control-ECU data is being overwritten (4LO lamp blinks) — clear DTCs after such work.

title: DTC U0123 (toyota)
text: DTC U0123 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Yaw Rate Sensor Module. Possible causes: yaw rate sensor; CANL/CANH circuit; skid control ECU; steering angle sensor; junction connector. Diagnostic notes: 2004 Scion xB RM1031U: with ECU IG1 voltage at 9.5 V+, no data received from the yaw rate sensor for 1 s+, or reception impossible one or more times within 5 s repeatedly 10 times (sub-code /62).

title: DTC U0124 (toyota)
text: DTC U0124 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Lateral Acceleration Sensor Module. Possible causes: yaw rate sensor (deceleration sensor); CANL/CANH circuit; skid control ECU; junction connector. Diagnostic notes: Same detection pattern as U0123 but for the deceleration (lateral-G) sensor channel (sub-code /95). See also C1243–C1245 for the sensor-side faults.

title: DTC U0126 (toyota)
text: DTC U0126 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Steering Angle Sensor Module. Possible causes: steering angle sensor (spiral cable with sensor sub-assembly); CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Same detection pattern as U0123 for the steering angle sensor (sub-code /63). The IPA/parking-assist documentation phrases it as lost communication with the spiral cable with sensor sub-assembly.

title: DTC U0129 (toyota)
text: DTC U0129 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Brake System Control Module. Possible causes: brake actuator assembly (skid control ECU); CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash safety city sensor view: unable to receive data from the brake actuator assembly (skid control ECU) for 5 s+ while driving at 5 km/h+. Also reported by the power steering ECU and combination meter.

title: DTC U0130 (toyota)
text: DTC U0130 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with VGRS. Possible causes: VGRS ECU (front steering control ECU); CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Variable Gear Ratio Steering models only — lost communication with the VGRS ECU (front steering control ECU).

title: DTC U0131 (toyota)
text: DTC U0131 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Power Steering Control Module. Possible causes: power steering ECU assembly; CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Reported by the combination meter assembly and lane-departure system when power-steering ECU data stops.

title: DTC U0140 (toyota)
text: DTC U0140 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Main Body ECU. Possible causes: main body ECU (multiplex network body ECU); CAN communication system; seat belt control ECU; driving support ECU. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash view: communication stop between the main body ECU and the driving support ECU (or seat belt control ECU) for 1 s+ with the engine switch on (IG). The certification-ECU (smart key) documentation uses the same definition with 1-trip logic.

title: DTC U0142 (toyota)
text: DTC U0142 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Body Control Module "B". Possible causes: main body ECU (multiplex network body ECU); CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — the lane-departure/CAN-chart documentation defines U0142 as "Lost Communication with Body Control Module 'B'" (reported by the combination meter), while the certification-ECU (smart key) documentation defines U0142 identically to U0140: "Lost Communication with Main Body ECU" (CAN error between certification ECU and main body ECU). Both are Toyota repair-manual sources; the reporting ECU determines which definition applies.

title: DTC U0151 (toyota)
text: DTC U0151 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Restraints Control Module. Possible causes: center airbag sensor assembly; CAN communication system; seat belt control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash view: communication stop between the center airbag sensor and the seat belt control ECU for 1 s+ (IG on). The CAN chart phrases it as "Lost Communication with Airbag ECU".

title: DTC U0155 (toyota)
text: DTC U0155 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Combination Meter. Possible causes: combination meter assembly; CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash safety city sensor view: unable to receive data from the combination meter for 80 s+ while driving at 5 km/h+. The clearance-warning ECU documentation phrases it as lost communication with the instrument panel cluster (IPC).

title: DTC U0163 (toyota)
text: DTC U0163 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Navigation Control Module. Possible causes: radio receiver assembly (navigation); CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Phrased in the Toyota IPA documentation as lost communication with the radio receiver assembly. A community fault guide notes GPS malfunction as a symptom.

title: DTC U0208 (toyota)
text: DTC U0208 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with "Seat Control Module A". Diagnostic notes: Appears as a row in the Toyota CAN communication system DTC matrix (RHD with entry-and-start system); per-system detection conditions not captured in the excerpts.

title: DTC U0235 (toyota)
text: DTC U0235 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): Lost Communication with Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor. Possible causes: front millimeter wave radar sensor; CAN communication system; driving support ECU. Diagnostic notes: Pre-crash view: communication stop between the front millimeter wave radar sensor and the driving support ECU for 1 s+ (IG on).

title: DTC U0293 (toyota)
text: DTC U0293 (SAE J2012 generic, category U): HV ECU Communication Malfunction. Possible causes: CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: Listed in the Toyota lane-departure-alert DTC set as "HV ECU Communication" — a communication malfunction involving the hybrid vehicle control ECU. Per-system detection conditions not captured in the excerpts.

title: DTC U1100 (toyota)
text: DTC U1100 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Seat Belt Control ECU. Possible causes: seat belt control ECU branch line or connector; power source circuit of seat belt control ECU; seat belt control ECU ground circuit; seat belt control ECU. Diagnostic notes: Set when no communication from the seat belt control ECU continues. Pre-crash safety system family (see U1104 in v1.2.1).

title: DTC U1114 (toyota)
text: DTC U1114 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Main Switch Module. Possible causes: CAN communication system. Diagnostic notes: The clearance-warning ECU documentation phrases it as lost communication with the integration control and panel assembly. Appears in the Toyota CAN communication DTC matrix.

title: DTC U1115 (toyota)
text: DTC U1115 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Tilt and Telescopic Module. Possible causes: multiplex tilt and telescopic ECU CAN branch wire or connector; power source circuit of multiplex tilt and telescopic ECU; multiplex tilt and telescopic ECU ground circuit; multiplex tilt and telescopic ECU. Diagnostic notes: No communication from the multiplex tilt and telescopic ECU; reported by the main body ECU (multiplex network body ECU). Power tilt/telescopic steering column models.

title: DTC U1117 (toyota)
text: DTC U1117 (toyota manufacturer-specific, category U): Lost Communication with Accessory Gateway. Possible causes: connector and branch wire of sub bus 2 of option connector (bus buffer ECU); internal malfunction of option connector (bus buffer ECU). title: DTC P1032 (nissan)
text: DTC P1032 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): Air Fuel Ratio (A/F) Sensor 1 Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1). Possible causes: faulty A/F sensor 1 (bank 1); A/F sensor 1 heater harness open or shorted; poor electrical connection in A/F sensor 1 circuit. Diagnostic notes: High-circuit counterpart of P1031. Nissan TSB NTB04-032a (2004 Titan/Armada) covers the A/F sensor heater low-circuit codes P1031/P1051 (ECM reprogram after confirming ECM part number); the high-circuit codes P1032/P1052 share the same heater circuit diagnosis.

title: DTC P1065 (nissan)
text: DTC P1065 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category P): ECM Power Supply (Battery Voltage Supply). Possible causes: failing battery (voltage below 12V engine-off); failing alternator (outside 13.2–14.4V running); loose/corroded battery cables; wiring fault to ECM backup power. Diagnostic notes: ECM receives battery voltage at all times for memory backup. Per Nissan tech guidance: check alternator output (13.2–14.4V running), then battery voltage after 15 min rest (below 12V suggests a bad cell); code may self-clear after 75–100 miles of driving if power supply is healthy.

Possible causes: dirty/low engine oil; faulty intake valve timing control solenoid valve (bank 1); solenoid harness open/shorted; faulty crankshaft position sensor (POS); faulty camshaft position sensor. Diagnostic notes: Set when the gap between target and actual cam phase angle exceeds the threshold. Check/change engine oil and filter before replacing the solenoid valve.

title: DTC B1017 (nissan)
text: DTC B1017 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Classification System Control Unit [Unit Fail]. Diagnostic notes: OCS control unit malfunctioning; FSM repair order: replace RH front seat cushion/OCS control unit assembly (do not disassemble the cushion).

title: DTC B1018 (nissan)
text: DTC B1018 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Classification Sensor [Unit Fail]. Possible causes: damaged wiring under passenger seat; poor connector contact; failed OCS sensor mat in seat cushion. Diagnostic notes: OCS sensor mat malfunctioning. Check wiring under the seat, unplug/clean/reconnect; the sensor is inside the seat cushion and is not separately serviceable — cushion assembly replacement is the FSM repair.

title: DTC B1019 (nissan)
text: DTC B1019 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Belt Tension Sensor [Unit Fail]. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — 2007 Xterra FSM lists B1019 as "BELT TENSION SENS [UNIT FAIL]" (belt tension sensor malfunctioning; repair: replace RH front seat belt assembly), while the 2010 Altima SRC section lists B1019 as "OCCUPANT SENS [OTHER FAIL]" (OCS malfunctioning). Meaning appears model/year-dependent; verify against the specific vehicle's FSM.

title: DTC B1020 (nissan)
text: DTC B1020 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Classification System Control Unit [Unit Fail]. Diagnostic notes: Grouped with B1017/B1021 in the FSM chart; same OCS control unit diagnosis.

title: DTC B1021 (nissan)
text: DTC B1021 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Classification System Control Unit [Unit Fail]. Diagnostic notes: Grouped with B1017/B1020 in the FSM chart; same OCS control unit diagnosis.

title: DTC B1022 (nissan)
text: DTC B1022 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Occupant Classification System Control Unit [Communication Fail]. Diagnostic notes: Communication between the OCS control unit and the air bag diagnosis sensor unit is interrupted; check harness connections before replacing units.

title: DTC B1023 (nissan)
text: DTC B1023 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Front Passenger Air Bag OFF Indicator Circuit. Diagnostic notes: Front passenger air bag OFF indicator malfunctioning; FSM repair order: check harness, replace harness, replace the indicator, replace air bag diagnosis sensor unit.

title: DTC B1033 (nissan)
text: DTC B1033 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Crash Zone Sensor [Unit Fail]. Diagnostic notes: Crash zone sensor internal failure; FSM repair order: check harness, replace harness, replace crash zone sensor, replace air bag diagnosis sensor unit.

title: DTC B1034 (nissan)
text: DTC B1034 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Crash Zone Sensor [Unit Fail]. Diagnostic notes: See B1033.

title: DTC B1035 (nissan)
text: DTC B1035 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Crash Zone Sensor [Communication Fail]. Diagnostic notes: Crash zone sensor communication failure with air bag diagnosis sensor unit.

title: DTC B1049 (nissan)
text: DTC B1049 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Driver Air Bag Module [Open]. Possible causes: open in driver air bag module circuit including spiral cable (clock spring); damaged harness; faulty module. Diagnostic notes: CONFLICT — the 2007 Xterra FSM CONSULT-II chart places B1049/B1054 under DRIVER AIRBAG MODULE [OPEN] (circuit open including the spiral cable), while community sources (JustAnswer) variously describe B1049 as a front-passenger airbag/OCS/pretensioner fault. FSM repair order: visually check harness, replace harness if damaged, replace driver air bag module, replace spiral cable, replace air bag diagnosis sensor unit. Trust the FSM for the specific vehicle.
