title: DTC B2108 (nissan)
text: DTC B2108 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Steering Lock Relay ON. Possible causes: faulty IPDM E/R (relay stuck ON). Diagnostic notes: IPDM E/R detects the steering lock relay stuck at ON for ~1 second even though the BCM commands it OFF. Check 10A fuse No. 40 in IPDM E/R; if the code is current, replace IPDM E/R.

title: DTC B2109 (nissan)
text: DTC B2109 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Steering Lock Relay. Diagnostic notes: Steering lock relay ON signal transmitted from BCM to IPDM E/R via CAN; IPDM E/R turns the relay ON and reports steering release to BCM. (Coupe variant in source.)

title: DTC B210B (nissan)
text: DTC B210B (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Starter Control Relay — Stuck ON. Possible causes: faulty IPDM E/R; harness/connector faults in starter control relay circuit. Diagnostic notes: IPDM E/R detects the starter control relay stuck in the ON position for 1 second or more (comparing BCM CAN signals against IPDM E/R inputs). If current, replace IPDM E/R.

title: DTC B210C (nissan)
text: DTC B210C (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Starter Control Relay — Stuck OFF (Circuit). Possible causes: faulty IPDM E/R; faulty BCM; low IPDM E/R supply voltage (~7–8V); harness faults. Diagnostic notes: IPDM E/R detects the starter control relay stuck in the OFF position for 1 second or more. May set spuriously on low IPDM E/R supply voltage.

title: DTC B210D (nissan)
text: DTC B210D (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Starter Relay — Stuck ON (Circuit). Possible causes: harness/connectors (starter motor relay control circuit open/shorted); faulty IPDM E/R; faulty BCM. Diagnostic notes: IPDM E/R detects the starter relay stuck in the ON position for 5 seconds or more.

title: DTC B210E (nissan)
text: DTC B210E (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Starter Relay — Stuck OFF. Possible causes: faulty IPDM E/R; faulty BCM; low battery/IPDM E/R supply voltage. Diagnostic notes: IPDM E/R detects the starter relay stuck in the OFF position for 5 seconds or more. Diagnose B2605 first if displayed together.

title: DTC B210F (nissan)
text: DTC B210F (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Shift Position / Clutch Interlock Switch. Possible causes: harness/connectors (CAN line or transmission range switch circuit open/shorted); faulty transmission range switch; faulty IPDM E/R; faulty BCM. Diagnostic notes: IPDM E/R detects a mismatch between the hardwired P/N position signal from the transmission range switch and the P/N signal received from BCM via CAN.

title: DTC B2110 (nissan)
text: DTC B2110 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category B): Shift Position / Clutch Interlock Switch. Diagnostic notes: Pairs with B210F in the SEC diagnosis section (shift position/clutch interlock switch circuit).

Possible causes: accessory relay circuit open/shorted; faulty BCM; faulty accessory relay; harness/connectors. Diagnostic notes: BCM requests accessory relay operation but gets no response for 2+ seconds. (PCS section: power distribution system.)

title: DTC C1115 (nissan)
text: DTC C1115 (nissan manufacturer-specific, category C): ABS Sensor [Abnormal Signal]. Possible causes: incorrect (non-specified) tires fitted; wheel sensor / sensor rotor issues; ABS module ground faults. Diagnostic notes: Set when a wheel-speed difference vs the other wheels is detected while driving (e.g., wrong-size tires). Inspect sensor connectors for corrosion/damage, clean sensor rings, check harness and module grounds.

Diagnostic notes: TPMS low-pressure warning. Check and adjust all tire pressures to specification, then drive at 40 km/h (25 MPH) or more for ~10 minutes and re-run BCM self-diagnosis.

title: DTC P1718 (subaru)
text: DTC P1718 (subaru manufacturer-specific, category P): AT CAN Communication Circuit. Possible causes: CAN communication line fault (ECM↔TCM/BIU); wiring harness, grounds, power, CAN twisted pair. Diagnostic notes: 2006 Legacy GT owner report: "P1718 code meaning an issue with the CAN communication circuit". Appears in the FSM LAN-diagnostics tables alongside U1201/U1221 — always read the LAN system DTCs together with it. On a 2005+ vehicle, check harness grounds (the DLC shares a ground point with the BIU) before condemning modules.

title: DTC U1201 (subaru)
text: DTC U1201 (subaru manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN-HS Counter Abnormal. Possible causes: unstable high-speed CAN communication (high-speed CAN communication error); faulty control module on the HS bus. Diagnostic notes: FSM detecting condition: "Communication is unstable due to a high-speed CAN communication error." Symptoms: combination-meter fault display; possible control issues. Diagnostic procedure: if U0073 is current, diagnose U0073 first; clear and recheck (temporary poor communication is common); if persistent, disconnect control modules other than the BIU one at a time (fitting 120 Ω across CAN-Hi/Lo when the ECM or VDC CM is disconnected) until U1201 clears — the last-removed module is faulty.

title: DTC P0126 (mazda)
text: DTC P0126 (mazda manufacturer-specific, category P): Insufficient coolant temperature for stable operation. Possible causes: failsafe thermostat stuck open (coolant infiltration of the dry cavity in the Coolant Control Valve integrated thermostat). Diagnostic notes: Mazda-specific pattern failure: the engine fails to reach operating temperature. Mazda issued a chain of TSBs (#01-011/21, #01-013/22, #01-005/23, #01-005/24, #01-001/26) and Special Service Program SSP D8 extended the warranty to 15 years/150,000 miles (2018–2025 CX-5, 2019–2023 Mazda3, 2019–2022 CX-3, 2018–2021 Mazda6, 2020–2023 CX-30). Fix is an updated dummy-plug kit plus PCM software update — check dealer VIN coverage before paying.

title: DTC P1132 (bmw)
text: DTC P1132 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): O2 Sensor Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open/short in heater circuit; failed heater element. Diagnostic notes: Check heater resistance at the sensor connector first.

title: DTC P1133 (bmw)
text: DTC P1133 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): O2 Sensor Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Possible causes: open/short in heater circuit; failed heater element. Diagnostic notes: See P1132.

title: DTC P1318 (bmw)
text: DTC P1318 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): Camshaft Position Sensor 'B' Circuit Signal Duration after Initialization (Bank 1). Possible causes: camshaft position sensor B (exhaust); wiring. Diagnostic notes: BMW-specific code — generic scanners list no definition. Often appears with P0340/P0365.

title: DTC P1339 (bmw)
text: DTC P1339 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): Camshaft Position Sensor 'B' Faulty Phase Position (Bank 1). Possible causes: camshaft sensor B; timing/phase issue. Diagnostic notes: See P1318.

title: DTC 2A82 (bmw)
text: DTC 2A82 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): VANOS intake — stiff; jammed mechanically. Possible causes: insufficient oil pressure supply to the intake VANOS adjustment unit; sticking VANOS solenoid; oil passages restricted. Diagnostic notes: BMW SIB 11 02 08: faults set when the camshaft is "late" or does not reach target position in the specified time under all engine conditions; engine power may be reduced with a check-control message. Check oil quality/level and pressure before replacing solenoids. N52/N54 engines.

title: DTC 2A87 (bmw)
text: DTC 2A87 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): VANOS exhaust — stiff; jammed mechanically. Possible causes: insufficient oil pressure to the exhaust VANOS unit; sticking exhaust VANOS solenoid. Diagnostic notes: Exhaust-side companion to 2A82 — same SIB, same diagnostic path. Tool32 MSD80 list phrases it as "outlet-Vanos variable cam control test, mechanics". N52/N54.

title: DTC 2A7C (bmw)
text: DTC 2A7C (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): Intake VANOS solenoid fault. Possible causes: faulty or dirty intake VANOS solenoid; infrequent oil changes. Diagnostic notes: A BMW technician (JustAnswer) notes the solenoids can be removed and cleaned as a first step; proper testing needs a BMW-specific scan tool. Solenoid electrical connectors can be swapped by mistake on reinstallation — verify routing.

title: DTC 2B3A (bmw)
text: DTC 2B3A (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): DMTL pump fault (diagnosis module for tank leakage). Possible causes: failed DMTL pump (in left rear fender liner); wiring. Diagnostic notes: EVAP leak-detection pump; common failure, ~1 hour replacement per the technician source. The N54 CAN DME list phrases it "DMTL diagnosis module tank leakage, system failure".

title: DTC 29CD (bmw)

Diagnostic notes: Per-cylinder misfire codes; N54 engine. Read companion fuel-mixture codes (29E0/29E1) before condemning ignition parts.

title: DTC 3100 (bmw)
text: DTC 3100 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category P): Boost pressure control — deactivation; boost pressure buildup prohibited. Possible causes: set as a consequential fault when VANOS or charge-air faults are present — not a root cause. Diagnostic notes: INFORMATIONAL per BMW SIB 11 02 08 (listed as a secondary fault to 2A82/2A87, alongside 120408 "charge-air pressure control, cutout"). Do not chase as a turbo fault; fix the primary code first. N54.

title: DTC 9CB5 (bmw)
text: DTC 9CB5 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category B): FRM: Battery exhausted (exhaustive-discharge protection: deactivation). Possible causes: weak/dead battery; FRM load-shedding active. Diagnostic notes: FRM shuts down lighting outputs to protect the battery — check battery/charging first; the lighting faults (A8AA/A8AC/A8B7…) are consequences.

title: DTC A559 (bmw)
text: DTC A559 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category B): KOMBI: Power supply switched off — closed-circuit current cutoff relay. Possible causes: parasitic drain countermeasure; battery rundown. Diagnostic notes: Set when the car cuts terminal 30g loads due to low battery.

title: DTC 931D (bmw)
text: DTC 931D (bmw manufacturer-specific, category B): KOMBI: Undervoltage or overvoltage. Possible causes: battery; alternator/charging system. Diagnostic notes: Voltage faults cascade into many body codes — address charging system before chasing the others.

title: DTC 93C3 (bmw)
text: DTC 93C3 (bmw manufacturer-specific, category B): MRS: Seat-occupancy detector, passenger. Possible causes: passenger occupancy sensor mat; wiring under seat. Diagnostic notes: SRS system — observe airbag safety precautions (battery disconnect, wait time) before probing.

title: DTC P1000 (mercedes)

title: DTC P1228 (mercedes)

title: DTC P1750 (mercedes)

title: DTC P1832 (mercedes)

title: DTC CEM-1A51 (volvo)
text: DTC CEM-1A51 (volvo manufacturer-specific, category U): Communication with the supplemental restraint system module (SRS). Signal missing. Diagnostic notes: Typical of an open circuit in the CAN bus; often appears with other CEM-1A5x codes. Disconnecting a node without first disconnecting the battery can set these.

title: DTC CEM-DF03 (volvo)

Possible causes: pinched/shorted LS-CAN wiring; short between CAN_H and CAN_L; single-wire operation. Diagnostic notes: Detection is continuous; a permanent fault is detected within a few seconds. Check for shorts between CAN H/L and to battery/ground on the LS bus.

title: DTC CEM-DF04 (volvo)

title: DTC E000 (volvo)
text: DTC E000 (volvo manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN high speed checksum error — communication fault with control unit on HS-CAN. Possible causes: disturbed/corrupt CAN message; contact bounce; single-wire operation; wrong-baud-rate node; faulty crystal in a node. Diagnostic notes: Posted by any node; designed for contact-bounce/corrupted-message detection but also appears on CAN_H↔CAN_L shorts or one-wire communication. A permanent fault is detected within seconds.

title: DTC E001 (volvo)
text: DTC E001 (volvo manufacturer-specific, category U): CAN low speed checksum error — communication fault with control unit on LS-CAN. Possible causes: see E000, on the LS bus. Diagnostic notes: LS counterpart of E000. E003 in some modules = configuration fault on the same buses.
